autotuner-multi-kernel.title: Compilation of Generalized Matrix Chains with Symbolic Sizes
autotuner-multi-kernel.one_liner: Multi-versioning codegen selects near-optimal BLAS/LAPACK kernel sequences for symbolic-size matrix chains
autotuner-multi-kernel.regime: symbolic-size BLAS/LAPACK matrix-chain sequencing, CPU, no reported search-budget
autotuner-multi-kernel.centrality_rationale: GMC is a compiler system selecting BLAS/LAPACK kernel-call sequences, matching the group's own definition, but it optimizes matrix CHAINS rather than the fixed suite's single dense/sparse kernels and reports no search-cost number (explicitly flagged in survey.md as a track gap).

autotuner-multi-kernel.title: Exo 2: Growing a Scheduling Language
autotuner-multi-kernel.one_liner: User-extensible scheduling language; 80+ high-performance kernels competitive with SOTA on 3 platforms
autotuner-multi-kernel.regime: 80+ hand-scheduled BLAS/GEMM kernels via a user-extensible scheduling language, CPU/ARM, no confirmed search-cost or correctness protocol
autotuner-multi-kernel.centrality_rationale: Exo 2 is a scheduling-language autotuning system generating high-performance kernels including GEMM/BLAS, but survey.md notes this is the lowest-confidence entry (abstract-only) and its evaluation is expert-schedule-driven rather than the suite's fixed kernel set with a reported search/tuning cost.

autotuner-multi-kernel.title: Pruner: A Draft-then-Verify Exploration Mechanism to Accelerate Tensor Program Tuning
autotuner-multi-kernel.one_liner: Draft-then-verify search speeds tensor-program autotuning, finding fast DNN kernels with fewer cost-model queries.
autotuner-multi-kernel.regime: LLM/DNN operator kernels (matmul, conv, attention) fp32/fp16 on NVIDIA GPUs, jointly-reported search-cost-vs-performance curve
autotuner-multi-kernel.centrality_rationale: Explicitly named in the spec as the clearest example of jointly reporting search cost and achieved kernel performance; its LLM-kernel workloads match the suite's gemm_llm_ffn/batched_attention entries.

autotuner-multi-kernel.title: CuAsmRL: Optimizing GPU SASS Schedules via Deep Reinforcement Learning
autotuner-multi-kernel.one_liner: CuAsmRL: RL-optimized GPU SASS instruction scheduling, up to 26% over specialized kernels
autotuner-multi-kernel.regime: fused LLM kernels (feed-forward, matmul, batched matmul, flash-attention) fp16 on a single A100, search cost reported separately as one-time RL training cost
autotuner-multi-kernel.centrality_rationale: Explicitly named in the spec text; its LLM-kernel targets match the suite's gemm_llm_ffn/batched_attention framing and it reports tuning cost (RL training time) separately from throughput as the spec requires.

autotuner-multi-kernel.title: Gensor: A Graph-Based Construction Tensor Compilation Method for Deep Learning
autotuner-multi-kernel.one_liner: Gensor: graph-based tensor compilation with Markov-analysis search, 18% avg operator speedup over SOTA
autotuner-multi-kernel.regime: DNN operator kernels (Conv2d/GEMM/GEMV/AvgPool) on cloud/edge NVIDIA GPUs, compile time and FLOPS reported in separate figures, not jointly
autotuner-multi-kernel.centrality_rationale: Gensor's GEMM/Conv2d configs overlap the suite but GEMV/AvgPool do not, and per survey.md it reports search/compile time and steady-state performance in separate figures rather than a joint Pareto curve.

autotuner-multi-kernel.title: Retargeting and Respecializing GPU Workloads for Performance Portability
autotuner-multi-kernel.one_liner: MLIR-based CUDA-to-AMD retargeting with granularity autotuning, 27% geomean on Rodinia
autotuner-multi-kernel.regime: Rodinia benchmark-suite mini-apps (BFS, hotspot, LUD, etc.), cross-vendor NVIDIA/AMD GPU granularity autotuning
autotuner-multi-kernel.centrality_rationale: The autotuning/retargeting compiler is squarely the group's kind of system, but its evaluated suite (Rodinia mini-apps) is a completely different benchmark set from the spec's dense/sparse tensor-kernel or PolyBench suites.

autotuner-multi-kernel.title: Harnessing Deep Learning and HPC Kernels via High-Level Loop and Tensor Abstractions on CPU Architectures
autotuner-multi-kernel.one_liner: Tensor Processing Primitives plus declarative loop abstractions yield portable, near-peak DL/HPC kernels on CPUs
autotuner-multi-kernel.regime: GEMM/MLP/ResNet-50-conv/block-sparse-matmul kernels on CPU, explicit wall-time tuning-cost comparison vs TVM-Ansor
autotuner-multi-kernel.centrality_rationale: Explicitly named in the spec as reporting search cost in wall time; its GEMM/conv kernels match the suite's gemm_square/conv2d_resnet50 entries.

autotuner-multi-kernel.title: A Holistic Approach to Automatic Mixed-Precision Code Generation and Tuning for Affine Programs
autotuner-multi-kernel.one_liner: PrecTuner: unified mixed-precision code generator + autotuner for affine programs, up to 3.28x over LuIs
autotuner-multi-kernel.regime: PolyBench/C affine kernels (nussinov, fdtd-2d, heat-3d, seidel-2d, etc.), precision-vs-speed frontier, CPU+GPU
autotuner-multi-kernel.centrality_rationale: The spec's polybench-affine-mixed-precision variant is built directly and explicitly around PrecTuner's own confirmed test set.

autotuner-multi-kernel.title: SparseTIR: Composable Abstractions for Sparse Compilation in Deep Learning
autotuner-multi-kernel.one_liner: Composable sparse tensor compiler: 1.2-2.3x on GNN ops, up to 7.5x sparse conv vs vendor GPU libraries.
autotuner-multi-kernel.regime: SpMM/SDDMM/sparse attention/sparse conv on GNN graphs (Cora/CiteSeer/PubMed/OGB/Reddit) on NVIDIA GPUs, rigorous 10-100-warmup/100-rep protocol
autotuner-multi-kernel.centrality_rationale: SparseTIR's SpMM/SDDMM workloads directly match the suite's spmm/sddmm entries (same GNN-graph convention as benchspecs/spmm); its own search-cost amortization is only argued qualitatively, not quantified.

autotuner-multi-kernel.title: WACO: Learning Workload-Aware Co-optimization of the Format and Schedule of a Sparse Tensor Program
autotuner-multi-kernel.one_liner: Learned co-optimization of sparse format+schedule; 1.14-1.43x over MKL/ASpT on SpMV/SpMM/SDDMM/MTTKRP
autotuner-multi-kernel.regime: SpMV/SpMM/SDDMM/MTTKRP over 726 generated sparsity patterns on CPU, search/tuning cost unreported despite being the paper's core contribution
autotuner-multi-kernel.centrality_rationale: WACO's kernel types (SpMM/SDDMM/MTTKRP) overlap the suite but its 726-pattern corpus differs from the suite's fixed matrices, and survey.md flags that WACO's core ANN-search cost is never quantified despite being explicitly named in the spec as a track gap.

autotuner-multi-kernel.title: FlexTensor: An Automatic Schedule Exploration and Optimization Framework for Tensor Computation on Heterogeneous System
autotuner-multi-kernel.one_liner: Automatic schedule exploration/autotuning generating tensor kernels (GEMM, conv) for GPUs and FPGAs
autotuner-multi-kernel.regime: GEMM/conv/tensor-contraction kernels across GPU/FPGA/CPU vendor-library comparisons
autotuner-multi-kernel.centrality_rationale: FlexTensor's GEMM/conv targets match the suite's gemm_square/conv2d_resnet50 entries; explicitly named in the spec as one of the papers reporting post-tuning numbers with no bounded search budget.

string-regex-matching.title: Combining MLIR Dialects with Domain-Specific Architecture for Efficient Regular Expression Matching
string-regex-matching.one_liner: MLIR dialects generate regex-matching code targeting a domain-specific architecture
string-regex-matching.regime: domain-specific-architecture-executed regex matching, MLIR-compiled binaries; execution-time/energy improvement over the same DSA's baseline compiler
string-regex-matching.centrality_rationale: The MLIR dialects target only regex matching (not a multi-kernel general compiler); this is a compilation-technique paper whose contribution is squarely regex-matching codegen, matching the compilation-amortized variant's description.

string-regex-matching.title: ngAP: Non-blocking Large-scale Automata Processing on GPUs
string-regex-matching.one_liner: Non-blocking GPU automata processing with prefetch/memoization; avg 7.9x over SOTA GPU engine
string-regex-matching.regime: large-scale automata workloads (20 applications), steady-state GPU matching throughput vs SOTA GPU automata engine
string-regex-matching.centrality_rationale: Headline IS a GPU automata-processing kernel technique (non-blocking symbol processing), evaluated as precompiled-automaton steady-state throughput, exactly the precompiled-kernel variant.

string-regex-matching.title: One Automaton to Rule Them All: Beyond Multiple Regular Expressions Execution
string-regex-matching.one_liner: MFSA merges multi-regex automata; ~6x matching throughput vs multiple parallel FSAs
string-regex-matching.regime: multi-regex rulesets executed via FSA, CPU single/multi-threaded, compilation overhead reported separately from matching throughput
string-regex-matching.centrality_rationale: MFSA/iMFAnt's headline IS a regex-matching engine (automaton merging + execution), with matching throughput and compilation cost reported as separate numbers, matching the spec's precompiled-throughput vs. compilation-amortized split.

string-regex-matching.title: GSpecPal: Speculation-Centric Finite State Machine Parallelization on GPUs
string-regex-matching.one_liner: GSpecPal: speculation-centric FSM parallelization on GPU, 7.2x average speedup
string-regex-matching.regime: real-world FSM workloads, GPU steady-state matching throughput vs SOTA GPU FSM parallelization
string-regex-matching.centrality_rationale: Headline IS a GPU FSM/regex-matching parallelization technique (speculation-centric scheduling) benchmarked at kernel-level throughput.

string-regex-matching.title: Why GPUs are Slow at Executing NFAs and How to Make them Faster
string-regex-matching.one_liner: GPU NFA kernels via read privatization and dynamic load balancing; beats prior GPU and Automata Processor
string-regex-matching.regime: NFA matching workloads, GPU steady-state throughput vs prior GPU NFA implementations and a domain-specific Automata Processor
string-regex-matching.centrality_rationale: Headline IS a GPU NFA-matching kernel optimization (read privatization, dynamic load balancing) evaluated at kernel-level throughput against both software and hardware (Automata Processor) baselines.

convolution.title: Accelerated Auto-Tuning of GPU Kernels for Tensor Computations
convolution.one_liner: Faster TVM auto-tuning of GPU GEMM/convolution tensor kernels
convolution.regime: TVM/Ansor autotuning-search-cost reduction for GEMM+conv2d task sets (YOLO/ResNet networks), RTX3090/4090; found kernel quality matches, not beats, vanilla Ansor by design
convolution.centrality_rationale: Ansor-AF-DS is a general autotuner covering both GEMM and conv2d (a compiler that generates this kernel among others), so conv is one of two target ops; its actual contribution -- reaching the same code quality in far fewer trials -- is exactly the spec's dedicated conv-tuning-cost variant, which the spec built around this paper.

convolution.title: Tetris: Accelerating Sparse Convolution by Exploiting Memory Reuse on GPU
convolution.one_liner: Memory-reuse-optimized sparse convolution kernel for GPU inference of pruned CNNs
convolution.regime: pruned sparse conv layers extracted from VGG19/ResNet50/YOLOv3/MobileNet checkpoints at multiple sparsity levels, fp32, single V100
convolution.centrality_rationale: Tetris's own benchmark methodology (take a base dense CNN layer, prune it, time the pruned shape) is quoted verbatim as the spec's conv-sparse-pruned-kernel-fp32 variant's methodology.

convolution.title: Hidet: Task-Mapping Programming Paradigm for Deep Learning Tensor Programs
convolution.one_liner: Task-mapping paradigm compiles DL tensor programs into fast GPU kernels rivaling hand-optimized libraries.
convolution.regime: general DL tensor-program task-mapping compiler for GPU and TPU (GEMM, conv, and other operators); claims inference latency rivaling cuDNN/cuBLAS but exact conv workload/shapes unconfirmed (abstract-l
convolution.centrality_rationale: Hidet generates many different tensor-program kernel types via a task-mapping paradigm, so conv is one of several outputs (component), but survey.md could not confirm its specific conv evaluation protocol/shapes beyond the abstract's general claim.

convolution.title: A Comprehensive Automated Exploration Framework for Systolic Array Designs
convolution.one_liner: Odyssey DSE tool explores tiling/dataflow for systolic-array matmul and conv kernels on FPGA
convolution.regime: HLS systolic-array design-space search for GEMM+conv layers sampled from VGG16/MobileNetV2/ResNet50/ResNet152, HLS-estimated cycle/latency/resource cost model rather than a measured wall-clock kernel
convolution.centrality_rationale: Odyssey is a DSE tool spanning both matmul and conv kernels (component); per survey.md its own run_tests.py entry point is a synthesis-model search, not a profiled kernel execution, which is a categorically different measurement paradigm from this spec's GFLOP/s kernel variants.

convolution.title: Analytical characterization and design space exploration for optimization of CNNs
convolution.one_liner: Analytical model finds optimal CNN loop tiling/permutation on multicore CPUs, matching or beating autotuners
convolution.regime: dense conv2d layer shapes from ResNet-18/YOLO/MobileNet-depthwise (the exact shape lists the spec's suite is built from), fp32, multicore CPU, per-iteration cache-flushed timing
convolution.centrality_rationale: This paper's own resnet.txt/yolo.txt/deepwise.txt layer-shape files are the literal source of the spec's conv-dense-kernel-fp32 recommended_subset; headline is a loop-tiling analytical model evaluated at kernel level against oneDNN/AutoTVM.

convolution.title: VeGen: a vectorizer generator for SIMD and beyond
convolution.one_liner: Auto-generates vectorizers for non-SIMD ISAs; speeds up DSP/image/ML kernels over LLVM on CPU
convolution.regime: non-SIMD vectorizer generator targeting DSP/image/ML kernels; convolution is one of several target kernels, its specific workload/shape details not independently confirmed, CPU
convolution.centrality_rationale: Per survey.md, 'convolution is not [VeGen's] primary or sole subject the way it is for [the other convolution-track] papers' -- it is peripheral evidence for a general vectorizer-generator, fitting the compiler-generates-this-kernel-among-others component case, but with real uncertainty about how closely its conv target matches the spec's shape suite.

convolution.title: DSXplore: Optimizing Convolutional Neural Networks via Sliding-Channel Convolutions
convolution.one_liner: Novel sliding-channel convolution design with optimized GPU backward/channel-cyclic kernels for CNNs
convolution.regime: sliding-channel convolution (a novel grouped-conv variant) evaluated only via a full 350-epoch PyTorch CIFAR-10 training loop (loss/accuracy progress bar), no isolated forward-conv kernel timing harne
convolution.centrality_rationale: Per survey.md, DSXplore's repo has no isolated forward-conv-only timing harness -- the paper's claimed kernel-level speedups are not reproducible from the artifact without extracting and separately benchmarking the SCC op, so despite a genuinely novel kernel design the actual evaluation regime is end-to-end training, not kernel-level.

convolution.title: Accelerating Binarized Neural Networks via Bit-Tensor-Cores in Turing GPUs
convolution.one_liner: Bit-Tensor-Core BNN kernels (bit-GEMM, bit-convolution) on Turing GPUs, 77% faster than prior art
convolution.regime: 1-bit XNOR bit-Tensor-Core convolution/GEMM; headline metric is end-to-end ResNet-18 ImageNet throughput (images/sec), not per-layer kernel GFLOP/s, Turing GPU
convolution.centrality_rationale: Per survey.md, TC-BNN's headline number is whole-network images/sec (5.6K img/s), explicitly noted as an end-to-end rather than kernel-only data point despite bit-convolution being the paper's central kernel design.

convolution.title: Automatic generation of high-performance quantized machine learning kernels
convolution.one_liner: Automatic generation/tuning of ultra-low-precision quantized ML inference kernels
convolution.regime: sub-8-bit/binary quantized ResNet-18 layer-by-layer convolution (1x1/1x2/2x2 weight/activation-bit precisions), ARM CPU (Raspberry Pi 3B+)
convolution.centrality_rationale: This paper's own ResNet-18 layer-by-layer benchmark at ultra-low-bit precision is reused verbatim as the spec's conv-quantized-kernel variant's suite; it also cleanly separates kernel-only timing from end-to-end and from one-shot micro-kernel synthesis cost.

blas-level1-2.title: Exo 2: Growing a Scheduling Language
blas-level1-2.one_liner: User-extensible scheduling language; 80+ high-performance kernels competitive with SOTA on 3 platforms
blas-level1-2.regime: general user-extensible scheduling language generating 80+ high-performance kernels across domains; BLAS-L1/L2-shaped kernels are among the broader set, exact op list and sizes unconfirmed, CPU/ARM
blas-level1-2.centrality_rationale: Exo 2 is a general USL/codegen framework (a compiler that generates this kernel among others), explicitly named as a target for the spec's blas-l1l2-generated-kernel-suite variant, but the spec itself flags the exact BLAS op list as an open question.

blas-level1-2.title: SySTeC: A Symmetric Sparse Tensor Compiler
blas-level1-2.one_liner: SySTeC compiler auto-generates symmetry-aware sparse/dense tensor kernels, up to 30.4x on MTTKRP
blas-level1-2.regime: symmetric sparse/dense tensor compiler generating symmetry-aware kernels including SSYMV among MTTKRP and general n-dimensional symmetric tensor kernels, CPU
blas-level1-2.centrality_rationale: SySTeC's `ssymv` is directly named as the pairing partner for GEMV in the spec's blas-l2-gemv-symv-kernel variant, but SySTeC is a general compiler (SSYMV is one of many symmetry-aware kernels it generates) and its own SYMV problem size could not be confirmed from source.

blas-level1-2.title: VeGen: a vectorizer generator for SIMD and beyond
blas-level1-2.one_liner: Auto-generates vectorizers for non-SIMD ISAs; speeds up DSP/image/ML kernels over LLVM on CPU
blas-level1-2.regime: non-SIMD vectorizer generator; dot product (uint8 x int8 -> int32, native VNNI instruction width) is one of several target kernels and is the paper's own basis for the mixed-precision-reduction varian
blas-level1-2.centrality_rationale: VeGen's own `dot_16x1x16_uint8_int8_int32` kernel is the literal basis for the spec's blas-l1-mixed-precision-reduction variant, but the spec explicitly notes VeGen's own evaluation is a static instruction-count comparison rather than the measured wall-clock throughput the variant requires -- a genuine evaluation-protocol gap, not just an input-regime one.

blas-level1-2.title: fBLAS: streaming linear algebra on FPGA
blas-level1-2.one_liner: fBLAS: open-source streaming HLS BLAS library for FPGAs
blas-level1-2.regime: named BLAS L1/L2/L3 routines (dot, gemv, trsm, etc.) as a streaming HLS library, on-the-fly synthetic vectors/matrices, FPGA
blas-level1-2.centrality_rationale: fBLAS is the only one of the four papers in this track that benchmarks named BLAS routines directly against a reference library (the spec says so explicitly); its own sdot/ddot/sgemv/dgemv harnesses are the direct basis for both blas-l1-vector-kernel and blas-l2-gemv-symv-kernel.

gemm.title: Compilation of Generalized Matrix Chains with Symbolic Sizes
gemm.one_liner: Multi-versioning codegen selects near-optimal BLAS/LAPACK kernel sequences for symbolic-size matrix chains
gemm.regime: symbolic-size BLAS/LAPACK kernel-chain sequencing overhead, not a standalone GEMM benchmark
gemm.centrality_rationale: Headline is a multi-versioning codegen that selects/sequences BLAS/LAPACK kernel calls (GEMM among TRSM/SYRK/etc.) for symbolic-size chains; the reported metric is FLOPs/time within 15% of optimal chain cost, not GEMM throughput vs. a vendor baseline. CPU only.

gemm.title: Hexcute: A Compiler Framework for Automating Layout Synthesis in GPU Programs
gemm.one_liner: Hexcute auto-synthesizes GPU tensor layouts, matching cuBLAS/FlashAttention, 6.46x over Triton on MoE
gemm.regime: DL-shaped (attention/MoE-adjacent) fp16 tensor-core GEMM via an auto-layout-synthesis compiler
gemm.centrality_rationale: Hexcute is a layout-synthesis compiler that generates many kernel types (GEMM, FlashAttention, MoE); it reports matching cuBLAS on GEMM but the shapes are DL-workload-derived rather than the track's square/irregular sweep.

gemm.title: Communication-Avoiding Linear Algebraic Kernel K-Means on GPUs
gemm.one_liner: 1.5D communication-avoiding distributed LA algorithms scale Kernel K-means to 256 GPUs, 79.7% weak-scaling eff.
gemm.regime: distributed multi-GPU dense/sparse GEMM primitives tailored to Kernel K-means, not general-purpose square GEMM
gemm.centrality_rationale: GEMM/SpGEMM appear only as communication-efficient primitives inside a distributed Kernel K-means clustering algorithm evaluated end-to-end (weak-scaling efficiency to 256 GPUs); no standalone GEMM benchmark, and the contribution is fundamentally multi-GPU distributed, not a single-card path.

gemm.title: Demystifying ARM SME to Optimize General Matrix Multiplications
gemm.one_liner: MPGEMM exploits ARM SME for multi-precision GEMM, 1.23x over Apple Accelerate on M4 Pro.
gemm.regime: small/irregular DeepSeek/LLaMA-derived GEMM shapes, multi-precision, ARM SME
gemm.centrality_rationale: MPGEMM's headline IS an open-source GEMM library evaluated kernel-level against Apple Accelerate/OpenBLAS/Eigen; its DeepSeek/LLaMA shapes are explicitly one of the spec's own cited sources for the small-irregular variant. CPU (ARM) only, no GPU.

gemm.title: High-Order-Preserving Acceleration of a Shallow-Water Dynamical Core Using Tensor Units
gemm.one_liner: Ozaki-scheme FP16 Tensor Cores accelerate high-order shallow-water stencil dynamical core, up to 4.34x speedup.
gemm.regime: Ozaki-scheme FP16 tensor-core convolution-reformulated stencil update, not a standalone dense GEMM
gemm.centrality_rationale: GEMM here is a reformulation vehicle for a shallow-water stencil dynamical core (headline is the PDE solver); there is no standalone dense-GEMM kernel benchmark against vendor libraries.

gemm.title: Exo 2: Growing a Scheduling Language
gemm.one_liner: User-extensible scheduling language; 80+ high-performance kernels competitive with SOTA on 3 platforms
gemm.regime: 80+ hand-schedulable HPC/DL kernels including GEMM, cross-platform (CPU/ARM)
gemm.centrality_rationale: Exo 2 is a user-extensible scheduling-language compiler whose evaluation spans 80+ kernels including GEMM; matches the 'autotuner/DSL that generates this kernel among others' component pattern. CPU/ARM only, exact shape overlap with the track's sweep unconfirmed.

gemm.title: A Multi-level Compiler Backend for Accelerated Micro-kernels Targeting RISC-V ISA Extensions
gemm.one_liner: MLIR compiler backend generating DNN micro-kernels for RISC-V streaming-register accelerator
gemm.regime: RISC-V streaming-register-accelerator DNN micro-kernels, FPU-utilization metric, not GEMM GFLOP/s
gemm.centrality_rationale: An MLIR compiler backend that generates generic 'DNN micro-kernels' (GEMM-like) for a custom RISC-V accelerator; evaluated via FPU utilization %, not vendor-comparable GEMM throughput. Platform is a custom accelerator, not CPU/GPU/FPGA in the track's sense.

gemm.title: Loop Fusion in Matrix Multiplications with Sparse Dependence
gemm.one_liner: Tile-fusion compiler fusing consecutive matmuls with sparse dependence (GNN, sparse solve), 2.33x/1.32x
gemm.regime: sparse-dependence-fused dense/SpMM matmul for GNN training and sparse solves
gemm.centrality_rationale: Tile-fusion is a compiler technique fusing a dense matmul loop with a sparse (SpMM) loop for GNN/solver pipelines; GEMM is one half of a fused kernel evaluated via GNN-training and sparse-solve speedups, not standalone dense GEMM throughput. CPU only.

gemm.title: Rethinking Back Transformation in 2-stage Eigenvalue Decomposition on Heterogeneous Architectures
gemm.one_liner: Restructured back-transformation in 2-stage EVD beats MAGMA/cuSOLVER by up to 3.58x/2.21x
gemm.regime: one incidental GEMM call inside an EVD back-transformation reordering, not a benchmarked GEMM kernel
gemm.centrality_rationale: GEMM appears only as 'one additional GEMM computation' incurred by restructuring EVD back-transformation; the paper's kernel and baselines are all EVD-specific (MAGMA/cuSOLVER), not a GEMM benchmark.

gemm.title: T2-RELION: Task Parallelism, Tensor Core Accelerated RELION for Cryo-EM 3D Reconstruction
gemm.one_liner: Tensor-Core-accelerated hot-spot difference kernel for cryo-EM RELION reconstruction, up to 23.7x
gemm.regime: tensor-core cross-correlation difference kernel for cryo-EM, not a general dense GEMM
gemm.centrality_rationale: The accelerated kernel is a cryo-EM cross-correlation/difference computation reformulated via Tensor Cores, not a general-purpose GEMM; evaluated against RELION's own baseline, not vendor GEMM libraries.

gemm.title: TurboFNO: High-Performance Fourier Neural Operator with Fused FFT-GEMM-iFFT on GPU
gemm.one_liner: First fully-fused FFT-GEMM-iFFT GPU kernel for Fourier Neural Operators, up to 150% faster than PyTorch/cuFFT
gemm.regime: fp32/fp16 GEMM sized to Fourier Neural Operator hidden dimensions, fused with FFT/iFFT
gemm.centrality_rationale: TurboFNO builds a real from-scratch GEMM kernel matching/exceeding cuBLAS, but the headline contribution is the fused FFT-GEMM-iFFT operator for FNOs; GEMM is one stage of that fused pipeline, sized to FNO workloads rather than the track's independent square/irregular sweep.

gemm.title: CAT: Cellular Automata on Tensor Cores
gemm.one_liner: CAT: mapping large-radius cellular automata onto GPU tensor cores (and CPU AMX), up to 101x speedup
gemm.regime: cellular-automata neighborhood update reformulated as tensor-core matmul, not benchmarked as GEMM
gemm.centrality_rationale: CAT maps a CA transition function onto tensor-core matmul; results are reported in CA-domain metrics (speedup vs. GPU/CPU CA baselines) not GEMM GFLOP/s against vendor libraries.

gemm.title: High Performance OpenCL-Based GEMM Kernel Auto-Tuned by Bayesian Optimization
gemm.one_liner: OpenCL GEMM kernel with double-buffer pipeline and prefetching, auto-tuned via Bayesian optimization.
gemm.regime: OpenCL GEMM on FPGA/OpenCL devices, square + GEMMBATCHED sweeps
gemm.centrality_rationale: CL-DB-GEMM's headline IS an optimized, Bayesian-autotuned OpenCL GEMM kernel; its own 'multiples of 128/129' square sweep and GEMMBATCHED/GEMMSTRIDEDBATCHED sweep are literally the cited basis for this track's square and batched variants. FPGA/OpenCL, no NVIDIA GPU.

gemm.title: Optimizing Dynamic-Shape Neural Networks on Accelerators via On-the-Fly Micro-Kernel Polymerization
gemm.one_liner: Micro-kernel polymerization generates dynamic-shape tensor kernels, 1.49x over vendor libraries on GPU/NPU
gemm.regime: dynamic-shape DL tensor-program GEMM on GPU Tensor Cores / Ascend NPU
gemm.centrality_rationale: MikPoly is a dynamic-shape tensor compiler (micro-kernel polymerization) evaluated across GEMM and other dynamic-shape operators vs. vendor libraries; GEMM is one of several operator types it targets, and shapes are dynamic-DL-derived rather than the fixed sweep.

gemm.title: Accelerated Auto-Tuning of GPU Kernels for Tensor Computations
gemm.one_liner: Faster TVM auto-tuning of GPU GEMM/convolution tensor kernels
gemm.regime: TVM-tuned GEMM/2D-convolution shapes; the claim is auto-tuning search time, not raw GEMM throughput
gemm.centrality_rationale: This is an autotuning-acceleration paper (faster TVM search for GEMM and conv2d kernels), matching the 'autotuner that generates this kernel among others' component pattern; the headline metric is tuning-time reduction, not kernel throughput vs. a fixed baseline.

gemm.title: Harnessing Deep Learning and HPC Kernels via High-Level Loop and Tensor Abstractions on CPU Architectures
gemm.one_liner: Tensor Processing Primitives plus declarative loop abstractions yield portable, near-peak DL/HPC kernels on CPUs
gemm.regime: CPU DL/HPC kernels (incl. GEMM) via Tensor Processing Primitives + declarative loops
gemm.centrality_rationale: TPP-MLIR is a broader framework producing portable near-peak DL/HPC kernels via TPPs and loop abstractions; GEMM is one of several kernel types generated, evaluated with standalone and end-to-end workloads. CPU only.

gemm.title: A Holistic Approach to Automatic Mixed-Precision Code Generation and Tuning for Affine Programs
gemm.one_liner: PrecTuner: unified mixed-precision code generator + autotuner for affine programs, up to 3.28x over LuIs
gemm.regime: PolyBench affine-kernel suite (GEMM one of ~30 kernels) under mixed-precision autotuning
gemm.centrality_rationale: PrecTuner is a general mixed-precision code generator/autotuner for PolyBench affine programs; GEMM is a generic example among many affine kernels, not a dedicated GEMM optimization target.

gemm.title: ConvStencil: Transform Stencil Computation to Matrix Multiplication on Tensor Cores
gemm.one_liner: Transforms stencil computation into matmul on Tensor Cores for large speedups
gemm.regime: stencil-to-matmul transformation on Tensor Cores, not a general dense GEMM benchmark
gemm.centrality_rationale: ConvStencil transforms stencil computation into matmul to exploit Tensor Cores; headline and baselines are stencil-domain (speedup over stencil solvers), not GEMM vs. vendor libraries.

gemm.title: Fast Kronecker Matrix-Matrix Multiplication on GPUs
gemm.one_liner: Custom fused GPU kernels for Kronecker matrix-matrix multiplication beating tensor-algebra baselines
gemm.regime: Kronecker-structured matrix-matrix multiplication, a distinct operation from general dense GEMM
gemm.centrality_rationale: FastKron implements Kronecker-product matrix multiplication (multiplication with a Kronecker product of several smaller matrices), a structurally different operation from the spec's C=A*B GEMM; baselines are tensor-algebra libraries, not cuBLAS-style GEMM.

gemm.title: LoRAStencil: Low-Rank Adaptation of Stencil Computation on Tensor Cores
gemm.one_liner: LoRAStencil: low-rank decomposition of stencil weights removes redundancy on Tensor Cores, 2.16x
gemm.regime: low-rank stencil-weight decomposition on Tensor Cores, not a general dense GEMM
gemm.centrality_rationale: LoRAStencil decomposes stencil weight matrices into rank-1 factors to reduce TCU memory-access redundancy for stencil computation; it is not a GEMM implementation or benchmark.

gemm.title: Toward Capturing Genetic Epistasis From Multivariate Genome-Wide Association Studies Using Mixed-Precision Kernel Ridge Regression
gemm.one_liner: Mixed-precision tensor-core Cholesky/GEMM for GWAS kernel ridge regression, 1.8 mixed-precision ExaOp/s
gemm.regime: GWAS/KRR-specific mixed-precision GEMM inside a tile Cholesky-based solver, application-sized matrices
gemm.centrality_rationale: GEMM is a real, separable BLAS3 building block used inside the paper's tile-Cholesky-based KRR solver for GWAS; it is not independently benchmarked against vendor GEMM at the track's square/irregular sizes.

gemm.title: autoGEMM: Pushing the Limits of Irregular Matrix Multiplication on Arm Architectures
gemm.one_liner: autoGEMM: autotuned irregular GEMM micro-kernel generator for Arm, up to 2x over LIBXSMM
gemm.regime: small/irregular (tall-skinny, long-rectangular) GEMM on Arm CPUs
gemm.centrality_rationale: autoGEMM's headline IS an autotuned irregular-GEMM micro-kernel generator, evaluated kernel-level against LIBXSMM/LibShalom/OpenBLAS/Eigen; explicitly one of the cited source artifacts for the small-irregular variant. Arm CPU only.

gemm.title: Hidet: Task-Mapping Programming Paradigm for Deep Learning Tensor Programs
gemm.one_liner: Task-mapping paradigm compiles DL tensor programs into fast GPU kernels rivaling hand-optimized libraries.
gemm.regime: DL tensor-program GEMM/conv2d shapes on NVIDIA GPUs via task-mapping compiler
gemm.centrality_rationale: Hidet is a compiler paradigm producing fast GPU kernels for DL tensor programs (GEMM and conv2d among them); GEMM is one of the operator types it targets, not the sole headline kernel.

gemm.title: A Comprehensive Automated Exploration Framework for Systolic Array Designs
gemm.one_liner: Odyssey DSE tool explores tiling/dataflow for systolic-array matmul and conv kernels on FPGA
gemm.regime: FPGA systolic-array matmul/convolution design-space exploration
gemm.centrality_rationale: Odyssey is a DSE tool that explores tiling/dataflow for systolic-array designs across 'various matrix multiplication and convolution kernels' -- an autotuner generating multiple kernel-family designs, not a dedicated GEMM implementation. FPGA only.

gemm.title: High Performance, Low Power Matrix Multiply Design on ACAP: from Architecture, Design Challenges and DSE Perspectives
gemm.one_liner: AutoMM auto-generates matrix-multiply accelerator designs on Versal ACAP, beating A100/U250/TX2 in efficiency.
gemm.regime: Versal ACAP systolic-array matmul accelerator, FP32/INT16/INT8
gemm.centrality_rationale: AutoMM/CHARM is dedicated specifically to generating matrix-multiply accelerator designs (not a multi-kernel-family DSE tool), evaluated kernel-level (GFLOPs/TOPs) against A100/U250/TX2; but its INT16/INT8 emphasis and FPGA/ACAP target diverge from the spec's fp64/32/16 CPU/GPU-focused sweep.

gemm.title: Anatomy of High-Performance GEMM with Online Fault Tolerance on GPUs
gemm.one_liner: High-performance fault-tolerant GEMM on GPUs beating cuBLAS
gemm.regime: large/near-square dense GEMM, fp32/fp64, GPU, incl. irregular shapes
gemm.centrality_rationale: This paper's own 1024-6144-step-512 square sweep is explicitly the cited basis for the track's gemm-square-kernel variant; headline is a from-scratch GEMM kernel beating/matching cuBLAS.

gemm.title: A Fine-grained Prefetching Scheme for DGEMM Kernels on GPU with Auto-tuning Compatibility
gemm.one_liner: Fine-grained prefetching scheme for DGEMM, auto-tuned via Tensile, ~1.10x speedup on GPU
gemm.regime: DGEMM on AMD GPU via Tensile auto-tuning, batched and single
gemm.centrality_rationale: Tensile-FGPS's headline is a fine-grained prefetching scheme for DGEMM kernels, evaluated kernel-level and explicitly named in the spec text; but the GPU is AMD, not NVIDIA, so out of the benchmark's single-NVIDIA-GPU scope.

gemm.title: CA3DMM: A New Algorithm Based on a Unified View of Parallel Matrix Multiplication
gemm.one_liner: CA3DMM: communication-avoiding 3D matmul algorithm with near-optimal comm cost, beats SOTA PGEMM
gemm.regime: distributed dense matrix multiplication, arbitrary M=N=K, fp64
gemm.centrality_rationale: CA3DMM is explicitly the named source algorithm for the gemm-distributed-e2e variant (same example sizing rationale, ntest=10 convention); CPU-only distributed, no GPU.

gemm.title: Closing the "quantum supremacy" gap: achieving real-time simulation of a random quantum circuit using a new Sunway supercomputer
gemm.one_liner: Sunway tensor-contraction random-quantum-circuit simulator: fused permute-multiply, 1.2 Eflop/s
gemm.regime: tensor-contraction-based quantum-circuit simulation on Sunway many-core, not standalone dense GEMM
gemm.centrality_rationale: GEMM/matmul appears as a fused permute-multiply primitive deep inside a 42-million-core tensor-network quantum-circuit simulator; evaluated via whole-application EFLOPS, not a GEMM benchmark. Sunway platform, no NVIDIA GPU.

gemm.title: LIBSHALOM: optimizing small and irregular-shaped matrix multiplications on ARMv8 multi-cores
gemm.one_liner: LibShalom: optimized small/irregular-shaped GEMM library for ARMv8 multi-core, beats 5 BLAS libs
gemm.regime: small/irregular-shaped GEMM on ARMv8 multi-core
gemm.centrality_rationale: LibShalom's headline IS an optimized small/irregular GEMM library, explicitly and repeatedly cited as a canonical source for the gemm-small-irregular-kernel variant. Arm CPU only.

gemm.title: Transformations of High-Level Synthesis Codes for High-Performance Computing
gemm.one_liner: Catalog of HLS source-to-source optimizing transformations for HPC kernels on FPGA.
gemm.regime: GEMM as one illustrative HLS-transformation case study, not a dedicated optimized GEMM implementation
gemm.centrality_rationale: This is a catalog/tutorial of HLS optimizing transformations demonstrated on a sample set of HPC kernels (GEMM, stencil); GEMM is an example, not a competitively-optimized, vendor-baseline-compared implementation.

gemm.title: WET: Write Efficient Loop Tiling for Non-Volatile Main Memory
gemm.one_liner: Write-efficient hierarchical loop tiling for matrix multiply on NVMM; 81% fewer writes with better performance.
gemm.regime: matrix-multiply as case-study kernel for NVMM write-reduction tiling; no vendor-baseline throughput comparison
gemm.centrality_rationale: WET studies the effect of loop tiling on NVMM write amplification using matrix multiplication as its case-study kernel; the metric is write-count reduction (and secondarily performance), not GEMM throughput vs. cuBLAS/MKL-class baselines. CPU only.

gemm.title: TensorSVM: accelerating kernel machines with tensor engine
gemm.one_liner: TensorCore-accelerated SVM via low-rank Gram matrix approximation
gemm.regime: Tensor-Core low-rank Gram-matrix approximation (random-projection matmul) for SVM training
gemm.centrality_rationale: GEMM/matmul is used to compute a Tensor-Core-accelerated low-rank Gram-matrix approximation inside an SVM training system; it is a real, separable sub-kernel of a larger ML training pipeline, not independently GEMM-benchmarked.

gemm.title: fBLAS: streaming linear algebra on FPGA
gemm.one_liner: fBLAS: open-source streaming HLS BLAS library for FPGAs
gemm.regime: streaming HLS BLAS3 GEMM (and other BLAS routines) on FPGA
gemm.centrality_rationale: fBLAS is an open-source BLAS library whose evaluated routines include GEMM as a primary BLAS3 member; but its streaming, on-chip-communication-composed design differs from the spec's off-chip square/irregular DRAM-resident sweep. FPGA only.

gemm.title: FeatherCNN: Fast Inference Computation with TensorGEMM on ARM Architectures
gemm.one_liner: FeatherCNN: TensorGEMM-accelerated Winograd convolution inference library for ARM CPUs.
gemm.regime: Winograd-transform tile GEMM (TensorGEMM) embedded in CNN inference, ARM CPU
gemm.centrality_rationale: TensorGEMM accelerates Winograd-transformed convolution tiles inside the FeatherCNN inference library; GEMM performance is reported but the shapes are small Winograd-tile-specific, not the general square/irregular sweep, and the headline is the CNN inference framework. ARM CPU only.

spmm.title: Insum: Sparse GPU Kernels Simplified and Optimized with Indirect Einsums
spmm.one_liner: Indirect-Einsum compiler plus GroupCOO formats generating tensor-core sparse GPU kernels; 1.14-3.81x speedups.
spmm.regime: compiler-generated tensor-core kernels via torch.compile lowering of indirect Einsums; SpMM-COO is one worked example, no fixed matrix suite disclosed
spmm.centrality_rationale: Insum is a general indirect-Einsum compiler (SpMM/SDDMM/sparse-einsum all generated by the same lowering); README shows an SpMM-COO example but no named benchmark matrix suite, so it generates this kernel among others rather than being an SpMM-specific implementation.

spmm.title: InferFast: Bridging the Gap Between Unstructured LLM Sparsity and Practical GPU Throughput
spmm.one_liner: Tensor-Core bitmap sparse format (CDP-TCBE) + SpMM for unstructured LLM sparsity, 2.01x over dense GEMM
spmm.regime: unstructured-sparse pruned LLM weights, ~30-90% density, fp16/bf16 Tensor Cores via CDP-TCBE bitmap decoding
spmm.centrality_rationale: Headline is an SpMM kernel (CDP-TCBE format) but built and evaluated for LLM inference weight sparsity; spec's general variant is SuiteSparse fp32, only the tensorcore-fp16 variant is in range.

spmm.title: RASSM: Residue-based Acceleration of Single Sparse Matrix Computation via Adaptive Tiling
spmm.one_liner: Residue-guided adaptive 2D tiling for CPU sparse kernels; 1.36x over MKL SpMM, beats ASpT and J-Stream.
spmm.regime: CPU sparse matrices from the ASpT/J-Stream/CSF-4 comparison literature (SuiteSparse-derived), fp32, all-physical-core OpenMP, median-of-50
spmm.centrality_rationale: RASSM's residue-based adaptive tiling is evaluated with dedicated SpMM-specific GFLOPS/median-time numbers against MKL/ASpT/J-Stream/CSF-4; spec's CPU variant (RASSM's own median-of-50 protocol) is explicitly modeled on this paper.

spmm.title: GeneralSparse: Bridging the Gap in SpMM for Pruned Large Language Model Inference on GPUs
spmm.one_liner: GPU SpMM kernels adaptive to LLM pruning sparsity patterns; up to 20.82x over cuSPARSE, 2.33x end-to-end
spmm.regime: pruned LLM weight matrices AND the SuiteSparse collection (per README's matrix_example/{pruned_weight,suite_collection}), kernel-level vs cuSPARSE, fp32 with an optional half-precision path
spmm.centrality_rationale: README confirms GeneralSparse benchmarks both pruned-LLM weights and genuine SuiteSparse .mtx matrices at kernel level against cuSPARSE (not just an LLM afterthought), so the general fp32 GPU-kernel variant is directly covered alongside the LLM-pruning niche.

spmm.title: Voltrix: Sparse Matrix-Matrix Multiplication on Tensor Cores with Asynchronous and Balanced Kernel Optimization
spmm.one_liner: Tensor-core SpMM with async bit-compressed loading and I/O-balanced kernels; 1.7x over RoDe
spmm.regime: SuiteSparse/GNN benchmark matrices in the RoDe/DTC-SpMM/TC-GNN comparison lineage, fp32/tensor-core, unverified beyond convention
spmm.centrality_rationale: Voltrix is a general tensor-core SpMM kernel design (async loading, I/O-balanced partitioning) benchmarked directly against TC-GNN/DTC-SpMM/RoDe, the same comparison family DTC-SpMM's own artifact uses.

spmm.title: LiteForm: Lightweight and Automatic Format Composition for Sparse Matrix-Matrix Multiplication on GPUs
spmm.one_liner: Automatic composable sparse-format (CELL) selection for GPU SpMM, 2.06x over cuSPARSE
spmm.regime: general SuiteSparse-style sparse matrices vs cuSPARSE/Sputnik/dgSPARSE/TACO, fp32
spmm.centrality_rationale: LiteForm's CELL format and its auto-composition system are evaluated as a general SpMM kernel with GFLOPS speedups over cuSPARSE/Sputnik/dgSPARSE/TACO, not tied to any one downstream application.

spmm.title: Fused3S: Fast Sparse Attention on Tensor Cores
spmm.one_liner: Fused3S: fused SDDMM+softmax+SpMM sparse attention on tensor cores, up to 16x on H100/A30
spmm.regime: real-world graph datasets (single and batched graphs) feeding a fused SDDMM+softmax+SpMM sparse-attention pipeline, H100/A30
spmm.centrality_rationale: SpMM here is one of three fused steps (3S) inside a sparse-attention kernel, evaluated as the fused pipeline and end-to-end Graph Transformer inference rather than as a standalone SpMM vs. cuSPARSE-class baseline.

spmm.title: Loop Fusion in Matrix Multiplications with Sparse Dependence
spmm.one_liner: Tile-fusion compiler fusing consecutive matmuls with sparse dependence (GNN, sparse solve), 2.33x/1.32x
spmm.regime: GNN training graphs (via PyG) and sparse-solve matrices (via MKL), CPU tile-fused loop kernels
spmm.centrality_rationale: Tile fusion is a compiler technique that fuses SpMM tiles with an adjacent parallel loop (GNN aggregation or sparse triangular solve); SpMM is one of the loop shapes it fuses/generates, and speedups are reported for the fused GNN-training and sparse-solve pipelines, not an isolated SpMM benchmark.

spmm.title: Accelerating Graph Neural Networks Using a Novel Computation-Friendly Matrix Compression Format
spmm.one_liner: CBM: compressed binary-matrix format, >5x faster GNN sparse-dense matmul than SOTA kernels.
spmm.regime: binary (0/1) real-graph adjacency matrices for GNN inference, CPU shared-memory serial/parallel
spmm.centrality_rationale: CBM's headline contribution IS a compressed format + kernel for binary-matrix times dense-matrix multiplication, benchmarked directly against SOTA sparse-dense kernels; but it only handles 0/1-valued matrices, narrower than the spec's general real-valued SuiteSparse/GNN suite.

spmm.title: NM-SpMM: Accelerating Matrix Multiplication Using N: M Sparsity with GPGPU
spmm.one_liner: NM-SpMM: hierarchical-blocked N:M sparse matmul, 2.1x faster than nmSPARSE, up to 6.3x over cuBLAS dense GEMM
spmm.regime: N:M structured sparsity (e.g. 2:4/4:8 patterns), dense-format block matmul vs nmSPARSE and cuBLAS dense GEMM
spmm.centrality_rationale: NM-SpMM's headline is a general N:M-sparse matmul kernel evaluated at kernel level against nmSPARSE/cuBLAS, but N:M structured sparsity is a narrower regime than the spec's unstructured SuiteSparse/GNN headline.

spmm.title: FlashSparse: Minimizing Computation Redundancy for Fast Sparse Matrix Multiplications on Tensor Cores
spmm.one_liner: Swap-and-transpose strategy minimizes sparse granularity for SpMM/SDDMM on Tensor Cores, 5.5x over DTC-SpMM
spmm.regime: SuiteSparse/GNN matrices in the RoDe/DTC-SpMM comparison lineage, tensor-core, H100/RTX4090
spmm.centrality_rationale: FlashSparse is a general tensor-core SpMM/SDDMM kernel technique with geometric-mean speedups directly against RoDe and DTC-SpMM, the same matrix families those two use.

spmm.title: Bridging the Gap between Unstructured SpMM and Structured Sparse Tensor Cores
spmm.one_liner: MP-SpMM: matching+padding converts unstructured SpMM to structured sparse-tensor-core format, up to 8.6x over RoDe
spmm.regime: SuiteSparse/GNN matrices (same family RoDe/DTC-SpMM use), transformed via matching+padding into 2:4 structured Sparse Tensor Core layout
spmm.centrality_rationale: MP-SpMM's headline is converting general unstructured SpMM into structured 2:4 sparsity and is benchmarked directly against RoDe/DTC-SpMM; the underlying matrices match the spec's suite but the executed format is structured Sparse-Tensor-Core, not the spec's general unstructured fp32/fp16 kernel.

spmm.title: StraGCN: GPU-Accelerated Strassen's Sparse-Dense Matrix Multiplication for Graph Convolutional Network Training
spmm.one_liner: GPU Strassen's-algorithm SpMM for GCN training, 2-3.3x faster than GNNA/PyG/DGL
spmm.regime: GNN adjacency graphs (15 benchmark datasets), evaluated end-to-end against GCN training frameworks (GNNAdvisor/PyG/DGL), no cuSPARSE/kernel-library baseline reported
spmm.centrality_rationale: StraGCN's Strassen-based SpMM is real and separable, but every reported speedup (2.1-3.3x) is against full GCN training frameworks rather than a standalone kernel vs. a vendor/kernel-level baseline.

spmm.title: SSpMM: Efficiently Scalable SpMM Kernels Across Multiple Generations of Tensor Cores
spmm.one_liner: SSpMM: Tensor Core SpMM library scalable across GPU generations via Transpose Mapping, 1.9-2.8x over SOTA
spmm.regime: 3,000+ sparse matrices from established SuiteSparse-scale collections, 4 generations of Tensor Cores, structured+unstructured sparsity
spmm.centrality_rationale: SSpMM is a general tensor-core SpMM library benchmarked at kernel level across a very large matrix collection against the SOTA SpMM solution, squarely the spec's headline claim.

spmm.title: DTC-SpMM: Bridging the Gap in Accelerating General Sparse Matrix Multiplication with Tensor Cores
spmm.one_liner: General SpMM on tensor cores via compression format, reordering, pipelining; up to 1.91x end-to-end GNN
spmm.regime: 8-graph GNN suite (YeastH, OVCAR-8H, Yeast, DD, web-BerkStan, reddit, ddi, protein), origin+TCA-reordered, N in {128,256,512}, cuSPARSE/Sputnik/SparseTIR/TC-GNN baselines
spmm.centrality_rationale: Code-verified via run_DTC_SpMM.py (see survey.md #9): kernel is timed separately from one-shot TCA reordering, against vendor/kernel baselines on the exact GNN suite the spec's recommended_subset is built around.

spmm.title: MaxK-GNN: Extremely Fast GPU Kernel Design for Accelerating Graph Neural Networks Training
spmm.one_liner: MaxK nonlinearity + fast GPU SpMM/SSpMM kernels cutting SpMM memory traffic in GNN training
spmm.regime: 24 real GNN benchmark graphs (README's maxk_graphs set), kernel-level vs cuSPARSE and GNNAdvisor kernels (spmm_maxk.cu / spmm_cusparse.cu / spmm_gnna.cu), but the dense operand is pre-sparsified by th
spmm.centrality_rationale: README confirms the artifact ships standalone SpGEMM/SSpMM kernels benchmarked directly against cuSPARSE/GNNAdvisor kernel binaries on a 24-graph suite, but the feature matrix is MaxK-sparsified (an algorithmic change to what SpMM operates on), a narrower regime than the spec's fully-dense operand.

spmm.title: JITSPMM: Just-in-Time Instruction Generation for Accelerated Sparse Matrix-Matrix Multiplication
spmm.one_liner: JITSpMM: JIT assembly generation for SpMM on multi-core CPUs, 3.8x over Intel MKL
spmm.regime: CPU multi-core SpMM vs Intel MKL, fp32
spmm.centrality_rationale: JITSpMM's whole contribution is a JIT-codegen technique specifically for the SpMM kernel, benchmarked at kernel level against MKL's SpMM routine.

spmm.title: A Row Decomposition-based Approach for Sparse Matrix Multiplication on GPUs
spmm.one_liner: RoDe: row-decomposition CSR SpMM/SDDMM kernels, up to 7.9x/9.0x speedup over SOTA on GPUs
spmm.regime: SuiteSparse .mtx directory, fp32/fp64, N in {32,128}
spmm.centrality_rationale: Code-verified (survey.md #8): RoDe cleanly separates preprocessing from the per-call kernel and reports GFLOP/s against Sputnik/cuSPARSE on SuiteSparse; this is the paper the spec's kernel-f32 variant is built around.

spmm.title: Arrow Matrix Decomposition: A Novel Approach for Communication-Efficient Sparse Matrix Multiplication
spmm.one_liner: Arrow-matrix decomposition for communication-avoiding distributed sparse-dense matrix multiplication
spmm.regime: 13 of the largest SuiteSparse matrices decomposed into arrow matrices, 100+ nodes / 128-GPU distributed scale, communication-volume metric not throughput
spmm.centrality_rationale: Headline IS a sparse-dense-matmul algorithm (arrow decomposition) evaluated against a prior SpMM algorithm, but at distributed multi-node/multi-GPU scale with communication volume as the metric; spec's notes_on_fairness explicitly excludes distributed SpMM as incommensurable with the single-node kernel variants.

spmm.title: High Performance Unstructured SpMM Computation Using Tensor Cores
spmm.one_liner: SMaT: block-sparse SpMM library using Tensor Core MMA API, up to 125x over cuSPARSE
spmm.regime: 9 curated SuiteSparse matrices (matrix_list.csv: mip1, shipsec1, pdb1HYS, consph, cant, cop20k_A, dc2, rma10, conf5_4-8x8-10), A100, M=N=K=512
spmm.centrality_rationale: Code-verified (survey.md #10): SMaT's own matrix list is exactly the recommended_subset's SuiteSparse cluster, benchmarked at kernel level via the raw MMA API against DASP/cuSPARSE/Magicube.

spmm.title: SparseTIR: Composable Abstractions for Sparse Compilation in Deep Learning
spmm.one_liner: Composable sparse tensor compiler: 1.2-2.3x on GNN ops, up to 7.5x sparse conv vs vendor GPU libraries.
spmm.regime: standard GNN operator benchmark graphs, evaluated via a composable-format compiler generating SpMM/SDDMM/sparse-attention/sparse-conv kernels
spmm.centrality_rationale: SparseTIR is a sparse tensor compiler whose search space spans multiple operator classes (GNN ops, sparse attention, sparse conv); SpMM is one operator family among several the compiler targets and tunes, matching the compiler/DSL 'generates this kernel among others' case.

spmm.title: TC-GNN: Bridging Sparse GNN Computation and Dense Tensor Cores on GPUs
spmm.one_liner: Sparse-graph translation maps GNN SpMM/SDDMM onto GPU tensor cores; 1.70x avg over DGL
spmm.regime: GNN benchmark graphs (the TC-GNN/GNNAdvisor lineage the spec's recommended_subset traces back to), evaluated primarily as DGL-framework training speedup rather than standalone GFLOP/s
spmm.centrality_rationale: TC-GNN's sparse-graph-translation kernel is the ancestor of the exact 8-graph GNN suite this track's spec cites, and DTC-SpMM's own artifact runs TC-GNN's kernel as one of its parallel kernel-level baselines, evidencing a genuine separable SpMM/SDDMM kernel even though TC-GNN's own abstract reports only DGL-framework-level speedup.

spmm.title: Fast Sparse GPU Kernels for Accelerated Training of Graph Neural Networks
spmm.one_liner: Hybrid-parallel SpMM/SDDMM GPU kernels with dynamic task partition, up to 1.72x GNN training speedup
spmm.regime: sparse matrices from real GNN applications, kernel-level plus embedded in GCN full-graph and GraphSAINT sampling training
spmm.centrality_rationale: HP-SpMM/HP-SDDMM are new standalone GPU kernels (hybrid vertex/edge parallelism) directly benchmarked against SOTA sparse kernel implementations before being embedded into GNN frameworks.

spmm.title: Shfl-BW: accelerating deep neural network inference with tensor-core aware weight pruning
spmm.one_liner: Tensor-core-aware structured weight pruning kernels for faster DNN inference
spmm.regime: block-structured (Shfl-BW) pruned DNN weight matrices, tunable density (e.g. 10%), Tensor-Core GEMM benchmark vs dense baseline, V100/T4/A100
spmm.centrality_rationale: README confirms a genuine standalone kernel benchmark (benchmark.spmm.out, A x B with a chosen block-sparsity density) rather than an end-to-end system, but the sparsity pattern is structured block-wise pruning for DNN weights, not the spec's general unstructured SuiteSparse fp32 regime.

spmm.title: TLPGNN: A Lightweight Two-Level Parallelism Paradigm for Graph Neural Network Computation on GPU
spmm.one_liner: Two-level (vertex/feature) parallel GNN kernels beating DGL/GNNAdvisor/FeatGraph 3-8x
spmm.regime: real GNN graphs, two-level (vertex/feature) parallel aggregation kernel evaluated end-to-end against full GNN computation systems (DGL/GNNAdvisor/FeatGraph)
spmm.centrality_rationale: TLPGNN's SpMM-like aggregation redesign is real and separable, but every reported number (5.6x/7.7x/3.3x) is a comparison against complete GNN computation systems, not standalone kernel throughput vs. a vendor/kernel library.

spmm.title: SparseLNR: accelerating sparse tensor computations using loop nest restructuring
spmm.one_liner: Loop-nest restructuring codegen for sparse tensor algebra (TACO)
spmm.regime: mixed corpus (SuiteSparse + Network Repository + FROSTT + DARPA1998), CPU 64-core, TACO-generated fused loop-nest kernels
spmm.centrality_rationale: SparseLNR is a compiler (loop-nest restructuring for TACO) that generates fused kernels for multiple sparse tensor expressions, of which 2D SpMM (pdb1HYS, circuit5M, cora, bcsstk17) is one instance among 3D-tensor and other expressions.

spmm.title: Distributed-Memory Sparse Kernels for Machine Learning
spmm.one_liner: 1.5D/2.5D communication-eliding distributed SDDMM+SpMM (FusedMM) kernels, 10x+ over PETSc
spmm.regime: Erdos-Renyi random matrices + large real sparse matrices (100M+ edges), 256-node Cray XC40 CPU cluster, 1.5D/2.5D distributed communication-eliding algorithms vs PETSc
spmm.centrality_rationale: Headline IS distributed SpMM/SDDMM algorithms evaluated against PETSc's SpMM kernel, but the metric and scale (256-node communication time) are the distributed regime the spec explicitly separates from single-node kernel throughput.

spmm.title: Efficient Quantized Sparse Matrix Operations on Tensor Cores
spmm.one_liner: Magicube: quantized low-precision SpMM/SDDMM on Tensor Cores, up to 2.37x over vendor library
spmm.regime: quantized int4/int8/mixed-precision SpMM on Tensor Cores, A100
spmm.centrality_rationale: Code-verified (survey.md #11): Magicube is the paper the spmm-gpu-quantized-int variant is modeled on, with per-iteration CUDA-event timing and an exact-match integer reference.

spmm.title: Vectorizing Sparse Matrix Computations with Partially-Strided Codelets
spmm.one_liner: Partially-strided codelet mining vectorizes SpMV/SpMM/SpTRSV, beats MKL by up to 4.1x
spmm.regime: CPU vectorized SpMM (alongside SpMV/SpTRSV) vs Intel MKL
spmm.centrality_rationale: LCM I/E's codelet-mining vectorization reports a dedicated SpMM speedup (1.75x avg) against MKL among its three target kernels, a genuine kernel-level comparison.

spmm.title: Accelerating Backward Aggregation in GCN Training With Execution Path Preparing on GPUs
spmm.one_liner: Execution-path preparation turns GCN backward aggregation into partial-vertex GPU kernel, up to 6.6x
spmm.regime: GNN training graphs (Cora..YouTube, 10-80% training-vertex ratio), backward-aggregation-only partial-vertex SpMM isolated inside the full training-loop decomposition
spmm.centrality_rationale: Per survey.md #4, EPPGCN's own framing is explicit: SpMM/aggregation time is 'one component reported separately from total epoch time' of a whole-training-loop decomposition, not a standalone kernel microbenchmark, and it targets only the partial-vertex backward-aggregation sub-case.

spmm.title: FusedMM: A Unified SDDMM-SpMM Kernel for Graph Embedding and Graph Neural Networks
spmm.one_liner: FusedMM: unified vectorized SDDMM-SpMM kernel for graph embedding/GNNs, 10-28x faster than DGL.
spmm.regime: named real graphs (Cora..Orkut) + synthetic RMAT, 3 CPU architectures, fp32, MKL SpMM-only baseline plus DGL
spmm.centrality_rationale: Per survey.md #2 and spec.yaml's own cpu-kernel-f32 claim text, FusedMM is explicitly cited as one of the papers this CPU variant is modeled on; the paper isolates SpMM against an MKL SpMM-only baseline even though the kernel is fused with SDDMM for its primary use case.

spmm.title: Accelerating sparse DNN models without hardware-support via tile-wise sparsity
spmm.one_liner: Tile-wise sparsity pattern for sparse DNN matmul giving 1.95x speedup on GPU tensor cores
spmm.regime: tile-wise structured sparsity, pruned DNN weight matrices, GPU tensor core, compared only against the dense model (no SpMM-library baseline)
spmm.centrality_rationale: Headline IS a co-designed sparse-matmul kernel/pattern, evaluated at kernel level, but on structured tile-wise DNN-pruning sparsity rather than the spec's general unstructured SuiteSparse regime, and against a dense baseline rather than SpMM libraries.

spmm.title: FeatGraph: a flexible and efficient backend for graph neural network systems
spmm.one_liner: FeatGraph: co-optimized sparse templates + UDFs for GNN aggregation kernels, up to 32x speedup.
spmm.regime: real GNN graphs, composable sparse-templates+UDF backend generating GNN aggregation kernels, CPU and GPU
spmm.centrality_rationale: FeatGraph is a flexible backend that composes coarse-grained sparse templates with user-defined functions to generate various GNN aggregation kernels (of which SpMM-style aggregation is one instance), evaluated via end-to-end GNN training/inference speedup.

spmm.title: GE-SpMM: general-purpose sparse matrix-matrix multiplication on GPUs for graph neural networks
spmm.one_liner: GE-SpMM: CSR-native GNN SpMM with coalesced row caching and warp merging, beats cuSPARSE 1.41x.
spmm.regime: SNAP graph collection + misc SuiteSparse-like matrices, CSR-native, fp32, N in {32..512}
spmm.centrality_rationale: Code-verified (survey.md #7): ITER=200 batched CUDA-event GFLOP/s vs cuSPARSE/Gunrock, the classic kernel-level SpMM benchmark this spec's variant descends from.

spmm.title: Reducing communication in graph neural network training
spmm.one_liner: 1D/1.5D/2D/3D sparse-dense matmul parallel algorithms cutting communication in GNN training.
spmm.regime: Reddit + >1B-edge protein network, Summit >100 GPUs; wraps an unmodified cuSPARSE local SpMM kernel -- the contribution is the distributed communication schedule around it, not the kernel
spmm.centrality_rationale: Per survey.md #6, the paper's own text notes 'the SpMM kernel itself is not novel here, the contribution is the communication schedule'; CAGNET calls cuSPARSE via PyTorch without optimizing it, matching the 'kernel only touched, never optimized' tangential case.

spmm.title: Sparse GPU kernels for deep learning
spmm.one_liner: High-performance GPU SpMM/SDDMM kernels for moderate-sparsity DNNs, 1.2-2.1x speedup over dense
spmm.regime: DNN-pruned weight matrices (3,012 matrices from real pruned ResNet-50/Transformer models via magnitude pruning, moderate ~70-95% sparsity), fp32 primary + fp16-mixed variant, V100
spmm.centrality_rationale: Per survey.md #1, headline IS a general SpMM/SDDMM GPU kernel library (ancestor of Sputnik, later used as a baseline throughout this track) evaluated at kernel level vs cuSPARSE, but its own test corpus is DNN-pruned moderate-sparsity weight matrices, not SuiteSparse-class matrices.

sddmm.title: Insum: Sparse GPU Kernels Simplified and Optimized with Indirect Einsums
sddmm.one_liner: Indirect-Einsum compiler plus GroupCOO formats generating tensor-core sparse GPU kernels; 1.14-3.81x speedups.
sddmm.regime: unverified — claims tensor-core sparse GPU kernels (SpMM/SDDMM/sparse einsum) via an indirect-einsum compiler; artifact not yet recoverable
sddmm.centrality_rationale: Insum is a compiler generating multiple sparse-kernel types (SpMM/SDDMM/general sparse einsum), fitting the DSL-generates-this-kernel component rule; the spec's own evidence/open_questions state the artifact repo is an unrelated demo with no benchmark scripts recoverable since ASPLOS'26 has not yet occurred, so regime fit is genuinely unconfirmed.

sddmm.title: RASSM: Residue-based Acceleration of Single Sparse Matrix Computation via Adaptive Tiling
sddmm.one_liner: Residue-guided adaptive 2D tiling for CPU sparse kernels; 1.36x over MKL SpMM, beats ASpT and J-Stream.
sddmm.regime: CPU adaptive-tiling sparse kernels on 47 named SuiteSparse matrices overlapping RoDe's suite
sddmm.centrality_rationale: RASSM's own abstract frames its headline speedup entirely in SpMM terms with SDDMM as a secondary code path (--kernel sddmm exists but is SpMM-adjacent per the spec's open_questions), so SDDMM is real but not the paper's headline; its SuiteSparse selection matches the general-suite variant's input tradition closely.

sddmm.title: Fused3S: Fast Sparse Attention on Tensor Cores
sddmm.one_liner: Fused3S: fused SDDMM+softmax+SpMM sparse attention on tensor cores, up to 16x on H100/A30
sddmm.regime: fused SDDMM+softmax+SpMM sparse attention on real GNN graphs (cora/pubmed/reddit/ogbn-*), K=128, tensor cores
sddmm.centrality_rationale: Fused3S is the direct model for both the tensorcore-blocked-fp16 and attention-e2e variants — the spec calls its protocol 'the cleanest in the track' and reuses its exact warmup/rep/statistic and 3-term FLOP formula.

sddmm.title: FlashSparse: Minimizing Computation Redundancy for Fast Sparse Matrix Multiplications on Tensor Cores
sddmm.one_liner: Swap-and-transpose strategy minimizes sparse granularity for SpMM/SDDMM on Tensor Cores, 5.5x over DTC-SpMM
sddmm.regime: SpMM/SDDMM on 515 SuiteSparse matrices + DGL/PyG GNN graphs, fp16/tf32 tensor-core blocked format
sddmm.centrality_rationale: FlashSparse is named explicitly in the spec's tensorcore-blocked-fp16 claim text ('matches FlashSparse's and Fused3S's own kernel-only tables') and its dual fp16/tf32 rows and format-conversion ablation map directly onto the variant's protocol.

sddmm.title: A Row Decomposition-based Approach for Sparse Matrix Multiplication on GPUs
sddmm.one_liner: RoDe: row-decomposition CSR SpMM/SDDMM kernels, up to 7.9x/9.0x speedup over SOTA on GPUs
sddmm.regime: row-decomposition CSR SpMM/SDDMM on SuiteSparse matrices selected by rows/cols/nnz thresholds
sddmm.centrality_rationale: RoDe is the literal source of the sddmm-csr-kernel-f32 variant — the spec copies RoDe's own ssgetpy filter verbatim for its matrix suite.

sddmm.title: SparseTIR: Composable Abstractions for Sparse Compilation in Deep Learning
sddmm.one_liner: Composable sparse tensor compiler: 1.2-2.3x on GNN ops, up to 7.5x sparse conv vs vendor GPU libraries.
sddmm.regime: composable sparse tensor compiler generating GNN/SDDMM/sparse-attention/sparse-conv operators vs vendor libraries
sddmm.centrality_rationale: SparseTIR is a general sparse tensor compiler whose example set includes SDDMM among several kernel types (SpMM, sparse attention, sparse conv), matching the DSL/compiler component rule; it was not one of the 10 papers deep-surveyed for this spec so its exact suite overlap with the SuiteSparse/DLMC/GNN traditions is unconfirmed, only loosely similar (GNN-operator/vendor-library framing).

sddmm.title: TC-GNN: Bridging Sparse GNN Computation and Dense Tensor Cores on GPUs
sddmm.one_liner: Sparse-graph translation maps GNN SpMM/SDDMM onto GPU tensor cores; 1.70x avg over DGL
sddmm.regime: SpMM/SDDMM on real GNN graphs mapped to tensor cores via sparse-graph translation, vs DGL
sddmm.centrality_rationale: TC-GNN's headline is a manual kernel-translation design for SpMM+SDDMM on tensor cores and it is cited as a standard kernel-level baseline by peer papers in this exact track (FlashSparse's baseline list); it was not deep-surveyed here so its exact graph suite/precision overlap with the tensorcore-blocked-fp16 variant is unconfirmed.

sddmm.title: Fast Sparse GPU Kernels for Accelerated Training of Graph Neural Networks
sddmm.one_liner: Hybrid-parallel SpMM/SDDMM GPU kernels with dynamic task partition, up to 1.72x GNN training speedup
sddmm.regime: hybrid-parallel SpMM/SDDMM for GNN training, 16 named GNN graphs (Yelp/Flickr/.../reddit), K in {32,64,128}
sddmm.centrality_rationale: Paper/title claim a fused hybrid-parallel SpMM+SDDMM kernel evaluated kernel-level (GFLOPS) on a real-GNN-graph suite matching the tensorcore-blocked-fp16 tradition; flagged as a hard call because the spec's own open_questions note the currently hosted artifact snapshot contains only an SpMM benchmark path, no verifiable SDDMM code despite the paper/repo title.

sddmm.title: SparseLNR: accelerating sparse tensor computations using loop nest restructuring
sddmm.one_liner: Loop-nest restructuring codegen for sparse tensor algebra (TACO)
sddmm.regime: unverified — CPU loop-nest-restructuring compiler (TACO extension) with SDDMM as one example operator
sddmm.centrality_rationale: SparseLNR is a general sparse-tensor-algebra scheduling/codegen system (compiler/DSL component rule applies) with SDDMM as one of several example kernels; it was not deep-surveyed for this spec, is CPU-only, and TACO-family benchmarks typically diverge from this track's SuiteSparse/DLMC/GNN-graph traditions, so regime is marked mismatch on current evidence.

sddmm.title: Distributed-Memory Sparse Kernels for Machine Learning
sddmm.one_liner: 1.5D/2.5D communication-eliding distributed SDDMM+SpMM (FusedMM) kernels, 10x+ over PETSc
sddmm.regime: distributed-memory 1.5D/2.5D SDDMM+SpMM on synthetic Erdos-Renyi matrices, MPI/CPU cluster
sddmm.centrality_rationale: FusedMM/HnH's headline IS a distributed communication-eliding SDDMM+SpMM kernel evaluated kernel-level (GFLOP/s vs PETSc/MKL), but the spec's own notes_on_fairness explicitly says its min-wall-time dynamic-repetition protocol on synthetic ER matrices is structurally different from every fixed-rep GPU variant and is NOT folded into any of them.

sddmm.title: Efficient Quantized Sparse Matrix Operations on Tensor Cores
sddmm.one_liner: Magicube: quantized low-precision SpMM/SDDMM on Tensor Cores, up to 2.37x over vendor library
sddmm.regime: quantized (4b/8b/16b) SDDMM on DLMC sparse-DNN weight matrices at controlled sparsity buckets
sddmm.centrality_rationale: Magicube is the direct source of the sddmm-quantized-dlmc variant — the spec's sparsity-bucket file lists and precision rows are taken straight from Magicube's own eval_matrices/s*.txt convention.

sddmm.title: FusedMM: A Unified SDDMM-SpMM Kernel for Graph Embedding and Graph Neural Networks
sddmm.one_liner: FusedMM: unified vectorized SDDMM-SpMM kernel for graph embedding/GNNs, 10-28x faster than DGL.
sddmm.regime: unified vectorized SDDMM-SpMM on real graphs (Cora/Pubmed/YouTube/Orkut/OGBprot) for graph embedding, CPU/ARM
sddmm.centrality_rationale: FusedMM is named explicitly as a source paper for the sddmm-attention-e2e variant (its Force2Vec end-to-end runs) and its real-graph suite closely matches the tensorcore-blocked-fp16 input tradition, though its own correctness check is only an indirect downstream F1-score match, not a numerical tolerance.

sddmm.title: Sparse GPU kernels for deep learning
sddmm.one_liner: High-performance GPU SpMM/SDDMM kernels for moderate-sparsity DNNs, 1.2-2.1x speedup over dense
sddmm.regime: DLMC sparse-DNN weights + SuiteSparse, fp32/mixed-fp16, foundational Sputnik kernel library
sddmm.centrality_rationale: Gale et al./Sputnik is explicitly named as the common-denominator kernel every later paper in this track baselines against, and it spans both the DLMC and general-SuiteSparse traditions the spec's variants are built around.

mttkrp.title: SySTeC: A Symmetric Sparse Tensor Compiler
mttkrp.one_liner: SySTeC compiler auto-generates symmetry-aware sparse/dense tensor kernels, up to 30.4x on MTTKRP
mttkrp.centrality_rationale: SySTeC is a symmetry-aware sparse-tensor compiler generating multiple kernel types, but its own generator protocol directly defines the spec's mttkrp-symmetric-kernel variant and its headline result (30.4x) is specifically the 5-D symmetric MTTKRP.

mttkrp.title: SymProp: Scaling Sparse Symmetric Tucker Decomposition via Symmetry Propagation
mttkrp.one_liner: SymProp: symmetry-propagated sparse symmetric TTMc/TTMcTC kernels, up to 50.9x speedup over SPLATT
mttkrp.regime: synthetic + real hypergraph-derived symmetric sparse tensors, CPU
mttkrp.centrality_rationale: SymProp's headline is exactly symmetric S3TTMc/S3TTMcTC kernels (the spec's closely-related symmetric-Tensor-Times-Matrix-chain family); its 5 named hypergraph datasets directly define the spec's symmetric variant.

mttkrp.title: WACO: Learning Workload-Aware Co-optimization of the Format and Schedule of a Sparse Tensor Program
mttkrp.one_liner: Learned co-optimization of sparse format+schedule; 1.14-1.43x over MKL/ASpT on SpMV/SpMM/SDDMM/MTTKRP
mttkrp.centrality_rationale: WACO is a learned format+schedule autotuner covering four kernel types (SpMV, SpMM, SDDMM, MTTKRP); MTTKRP is one generated/optimized kernel among others rather than the paper's sole focus.

mttkrp.title: Efficient, out-of-memory sparse MTTKRP on massively parallel architectures
mttkrp.one_liner: BLCO format for out-of-memory sparse MTTKRP on GPUs, 2.1-2.6x geomean over MM-CSF
mttkrp.regime: FROSTT real-world sparse tensors, order 3-4, GPU
mttkrp.centrality_rationale: BLCO's headline is exactly out-of-memory sparse MTTKRP on GPUs; explicitly named (Table 2) as defining the spec's general-kernel-fp64 variant.

gemv.title: QIGen: A Kernel Generator for Inference on Nonuniformly Quantized Large Language Models
gemv.one_liner: QIGen generates CPU matrix-vector kernels for nonuniformly quantized LLM inference
gemv.regime: nonuniform-bitwidth (INT2/3/4) quantized-weight GEMV, CPU, LLM linear layers
gemv.centrality_rationale: QIGen's headline IS a kernel generator producing nonuniformly-quantized matrix-vector kernels for LLM inference; explicitly the named source for the gemv-quantized-weight-kernel variant. CPU only.

gemv.title: PackKV: Reducing KV Cache Memory Footprint through LLM-Aware Lossy Compression
gemv.one_liner: LLM-aware lossy KV-cache compression that also accelerates matrix-vector multiply vs cuBLAS
gemv.regime: KV-cache-compressed GEMV on NVIDIA GPUs, LLM decode
gemv.centrality_rationale: This is the instructions' own worked example: PackKV's headline is KV-cache lossy compression; GEMV acceleration is an additional benefit of the compression scheme, matching the gemv-e2e-compressed-format variant it is cited for.

gemv.title: MARLIN: Mixed-Precision Auto-Regressive Parallel Inference on Large Language Models
gemv.one_liner: Mixed-precision GPU GEMM kernels enabling memory-bound batched LLM inference speedups
gemv.regime: INT4-quantized-weight GEMV/GEMM batch sweep crossing the memory/compute-bound roofline knee, GPU, LLM linear layers
gemv.centrality_rationale: MARLIN's headline IS mixed-precision GPU GEMM/GEMV kernels for LLM inference; its bench.py MODELS dict and full batch-size ALL=True sweep are the explicit, verbatim basis for the gemv-quantized-weight-kernel and gemv-batched-decode variants.

gemv.title: GPU-based Private Information Retrieval for On-Device Machine Learning Inference
gemv.one_liner: GPU acceleration of PIR's core matrix-vector-multiply kernel for private embedding retrieval, >100x over CPU.
gemv.regime: compute-bound LWE-ring modular-arithmetic matrix-vector multiply for private information retrieval
gemv.centrality_rationale: GPU-DPF's MVM kernel is real and separable but embedded in a larger PIR system (evaluated via end-to-end QPS and PIR-ML co-design gains); the spec itself flags this kernel as compute- not memory-bound, unlike the memory-bandwidth-bound regime this track targets.

gemv.title: Scaling the "Memory Wall" for Multi-Dimensional Seismic Processing with Algebraic Compression on Cerebras CS-2 Systems
gemv.one_liner: Embarrassingly parallel TLR-MVM on 48 Cerebras CS-2 systems for seismic MDD, 92.58 PB/s bandwidth
gemv.regime: tile low-rank matrix-vector multiply, seismic MDD real datasets, Cerebras CS-2
gemv.centrality_rationale: TLR-MVM is explicitly the named source for the gemv-e2e-compressed-format variant (same seismic-redatuming datasets, same bench.cpp harness). Platform is Cerebras CS-2, not an NVIDIA GPU.

gnn-aggregation.title: Accelerating Graph Neural Networks Using a Novel Computation-Friendly Matrix Compression Format
gnn-aggregation.one_liner: CBM: compressed binary-matrix format, >5x faster GNN sparse-dense matmul than SOTA kernels.
gnn-aggregation.regime: binary-adjacency x dense-feature matmul (plain and degree-normalized GCN aggregation), CPU shared-memory (serial+parallel), SNAP/Planetoid/OGB graphs overlapping the recommended subset (Cora, PubMed),
gnn-aggregation.centrality_rationale: Headline is the CBM compression format specifically for accelerating binary@dense aggregation matmul; kernel-only timing (benchmark_matmul.py) is cleanly separated from format-conversion cost, matching the spec's kernel-f32 variant closely.

gnn-aggregation.title: StraGCN: GPU-Accelerated Strassen's Sparse-Dense Matrix Multiplication for Graph Convolutional Network Training
gnn-aggregation.one_liner: GPU Strassen's-algorithm SpMM for GCN training, 2-3.3x faster than GNNA/PyG/DGL
gnn-aggregation.regime: full GCN training via a GPU Strassen's-algorithm SpMM, single GPU (RTX 4090); no isolated kernel-level benchmark exposed and exact dataset names not confirmed from the README
gnn-aggregation.centrality_rationale: Headline is 'the first GPU-accelerated SpMM implementation based on Strassen's algorithm' for GCN training -- centrally about the aggregation kernel -- but the public artifact only exposes full-training numbers (matches the epoch-training-e2e variant's tier), and the dataset suite could not be independently confirmed.

gnn-aggregation.title: MaxK-GNN: Extremely Fast GPU Kernel Design for Accelerating Graph Neural Networks Training
gnn-aggregation.one_liner: MaxK nonlinearity + fast GPU SpMM/SSpMM kernels cutting SpMM memory traffic in GNN training
gnn-aggregation.regime: MaxK top-k-sparsified (CBSR-format) SpGEMM/SSpMM aggregation kernel, single A100, custom 24-graph kernel benchmark plus a 5-dataset full training pipeline
gnn-aggregation.centrality_rationale: Headline is a fast GPU SpMM/SSpMM kernel design reducing GNN memory traffic, with an isolated kernel-level benchmark harness (kernels/spmm_base.h) shared with cuSPARSE/GNNAdvisor baselines; but the actual operand is a structurally top-k-sparsified feature matrix, not the plain dense-N-column input the kernel-f32 variant specifies.

gnn-aggregation.title: FASTEN: Fast GPU-accelerated Segmented Matrix Multiplication for Heterogenous Graph Neural Networks
gnn-aggregation.one_liner: Autotuned GPU segmented matrix multiplication for heterogeneous GNNs
gnn-aggregation.regime: segmented/batched dense GEMM per relation-type for heterogeneous GNNs (RGCN/HGT/RGAT), H100/A100/RTX4090
gnn-aggregation.centrality_rationale: FASTEN's operator is segmented (grouped/batched) dense GEMM over relational graph types, not the sparse-adjacency-times-dense-feature aggregation this track's spec defines; its own categories tag it dense_la, not sparse_la, and the assignment to gnn-aggregation looks like a mismatch on operator identity.

gnn-aggregation.title: TC-GNN: Bridging Sparse GNN Computation and Dense Tensor Cores on GPUs
gnn-aggregation.one_liner: Sparse-graph translation maps GNN SpMM/SDDMM onto GPU tensor cores; 1.70x avg over DGL
gnn-aggregation.regime: isolated single-kernel SpMM/SDDMM plus full-epoch GCN training on GNNAdvisor-lineage real graphs heavily overlapping the recommended subset (citeseer/cora/pubmed/ppi/amazon0505/artist/soc-BlogCatalog/
gnn-aggregation.centrality_rationale: TC-GNN is one of the few papers in this track that ships both an isolated kernel-only benchmark AND an epoch-level model benchmark, and its 14-graph suite overlaps heavily with the spec's recommended_subset for both the kernel-f32 and epoch-training-e2e variants.

gnn-aggregation.title: TLPGNN: A Lightweight Two-Level Parallelism Paradigm for Graph Neural Network Computation on GPU
gnn-aggregation.one_liner: Two-level (vertex/feature) parallel GNN kernels beating DGL/GNNAdvisor/FeatGraph 3-8x
gnn-aggregation.regime: isolated kernel-only GNN aggregation call (vertex+feature two-level parallelism), dataset-agnostic real-graph CSR (citeseer worked example), N=32 default, single V100
gnn-aggregation.centrality_rationale: TLPGNN's own benchmark (gcn/test_kernel.py) is the narrowest, purest kernel-only scope surveyed in this track -- exactly the spec's kernel-f32 variant's claim.

gnn-aggregation.title: QGTC: accelerating quantized graph neural networks via GPU tensor core
gnn-aggregation.one_liner: QGTC: Tensor-Core CUDA kernels for any-bitwidth quantized GNN computation, 2.7x over DGL
gnn-aggregation.regime: quantized (1/2/4/8-bit) bit-decomposed Tensor-Core GNN aggregation, plus a separate synthetic INT8 GEMM comparison untethered to any real graph, Ampere-class GPU
gnn-aggregation.centrality_rationale: QGTC's headline contribution is a Tensor-Core kernel design for quantized GNN aggregation, but its precision axis (1-8-bit bit-decomposed) is not commensurable with the spec's fp32 dense-feature variant, which has no quantized counterpart in this track.

gnn-aggregation.title: Accelerating Backward Aggregation in GCN Training With Execution Path Preparing on GPUs
gnn-aggregation.one_liner: Execution-path preparation turns GCN backward aggregation into partial-vertex GPU kernel, up to 6.6x
gnn-aggregation.regime: GCN backward aggregation restructured as a partial-active-vertex GPU kernel, both kernel-only (1.48-5.65x) and with/without-preprocessing end-to-end numbers, real GNNAdvisor-lineage graphs, GPU
gnn-aggregation.centrality_rationale: EPPGCN is the paper the spec's preprocessing-amortized e2e variant is explicitly modeled on -- it is the only surveyed paper reporting both a with- and without-preprocessing end-to-end number side by side alongside a kernel-only figure.

gnn-aggregation.title: FeatGraph: a flexible and efficient backend for graph neural network systems
gnn-aggregation.one_liner: FeatGraph: co-optimized sparse templates + UDFs for GNN aggregation kernels, up to 32x speedup.
