gnn-aggregation.regime: co-optimized sparse-template+UDF GNN aggregation kernel via TVM autotuning, dataset-agnostic CSR input (Reddit worked example), feature width 128, CPU and GPU dual backend
gnn-aggregation.centrality_rationale: FeatGraph's whole contribution is optimizing the SpMM-like GNN aggregation operator via composable sparse templates and UDFs; it is dataset-agnostic like the spec's suite and reports both CPU and single-GPU kernel-level speedups.

gnn-aggregation.title: GE-SpMM: general-purpose sparse matrix-matrix multiplication on GPUs for graph neural networks
gnn-aggregation.one_liner: GE-SpMM: CSR-native GNN SpMM with coalesced row caching and warp merging, beats cuSPARSE 1.41x.
gnn-aggregation.regime: isolated kernel-only GNN SpMM, SNAP/SuiteSparse graphs (whole SNAP category mirrored), N in {128,256,512}, fp32, single GPU
gnn-aggregation.centrality_rationale: GE-SpMM is explicitly named as one of the papers defining the kernel-f32 variant's 'common denominator', and its dataset-sweep convention (N doubling 128->256->512) is reused verbatim by the spec.

gnn-aggregation.title: Reducing communication in graph neural network training
gnn-aggregation.one_liner: 1D/1.5D/2D/3D sparse-dense matmul parallel algorithms cutting communication in GNN training.
gnn-aggregation.regime: distributed multi-GPU 1D/1.5D/2D/3D parallel decomposition of GNN aggregation; local SpMM uses whichever library is available and is not itself optimized, torch.distributed on 100+ GPUs
gnn-aggregation.centrality_rationale: CAGNET's contribution and measured quantity is communication volume/time for a family of parallel decompositions, not local kernel throughput -- the aggregation kernel is used as an unoptimized sub-step (per survey.md), and the paper's target scenario is inherently multi-GPU-only.

graph-pattern-mining.title: DTMiner: A Data-Centric System for Efficient Temporal Motif Mining
graph-pattern-mining.one_liner: DTMiner: Load-Explore-Synchronize execution model regularizing cache access for temporal motif mining
graph-pattern-mining.regime: temporal motif mining with time-window queries on temporal graphs, not fixed-pattern counting on a static graph
graph-pattern-mining.centrality_rationale: The spec explicitly excludes DTMiner from all variants, stating it measures a different operation entirely (temporal, time-window motif queries, not counting occurrences of a fixed pattern in a static graph) — an assignment the spec itself flags as not fitting this track.

graph-pattern-mining.title: GLumin: Fast Connectivity Check Based on LUTs For Efficient Graph Pattern Mining
graph-pattern-mining.one_liner: Runtime lookup-table connectivity checks accelerate graph pattern mining by two orders of magnitude
graph-pattern-mining.regime: clique-ladder (K4-K7) and pattern counting on SNAP-style graphs (mico/patents/youtube/pokec) via LUT connectivity checks
graph-pattern-mining.centrality_rationale: GLumin is one of the 8 in-scope evidence papers this spec's clique_ladder pattern set and small/large-pattern variants are built around (CliqueSolver k=4-7 explicitly named).

graph-pattern-mining.title: Fringe-SGC: Counting Subgraphs with Fringe Vertices
graph-pattern-mining.one_liner: GPU subgraph-counting kernel exploiting fringe vertices, up to 20x over SOTA SGC frameworks
graph-pattern-mining.regime: GPU subgraph counting with fringe-vertex pruning on named real+synthetic graphs, edges/s throughput
graph-pattern-mining.centrality_rationale: Fringe-SGC is the sole surveyed paper reporting a throughput metric and is the direct source of the spec's GEPS (edges-processed-per-second) metric convention.

graph-pattern-mining.title: VertexSurge: Variable Length Graph Pattern Match on Billion-edge Graphs
graph-pattern-mining.one_liner: Engine for variable-length graph pattern matching on billion-edge graphs, beating graph databases
graph-pattern-mining.regime: variable-length graph pattern matching (path queries of unbounded/variable length) on billion-edge graphs
graph-pattern-mining.centrality_rationale: The spec explicitly excludes VertexSurge from all variants because it measures variable-length path queries, not counting occurrences of a FIXED-shape pattern, which the spec calls a different operation that would misrepresent the comparison if forced in.

graph-pattern-mining.title: Exploiting Fine-Grained Redundancy in Set-Centric Graph Pattern Mining
graph-pattern-mining.one_liner: Set-union op fuses fine-grained duplicate edge checks in GPU graph pattern mining, up to 305x over G2Miner
graph-pattern-mining.regime: set-centric GPM with redundancy elimination, clique-ladder + 4-motif census (G2Miner gallery) on 11 graphs
graph-pattern-mining.centrality_rationale: GraphFold is one of the 8 in-scope evidence papers and its TC/CF4-7/MC4/P1-8 pattern gallery is directly incorporated into the spec's pattern_set and recommended_subset.

graph-pattern-mining.title: INFINEL: An efficient GPU-based processing method for unpredictable large output graph queries
graph-pattern-mining.one_liner: One-phase GPU processing for unpredictable large-output graph queries via chunked kernel restart
graph-pattern-mining.regime: large-output triangle LISTING (not counting) via chunked kernel restart on RMAT/real graphs
graph-pattern-mining.centrality_rationale: INFINEL's search kernel is closely related (triangle enumeration) but the spec's own notes_on_fairness explicitly calls listing 'architecturally different' from the counting operation its core variants measure (IO-bound on materialized output vs a pure count) and excludes it from the core counting variants.

graph-pattern-mining.title: GraphSet: High Performance Graph Mining through Equivalent Set Transformations
graph-pattern-mining.one_liner: GraphSet: equivalent-set-transformation compiler for high-performance graph pattern mining
graph-pattern-mining.regime: equivalent-set-transformation compiler for subgraph pattern counting, mico/patents/orkut/livejournal/friendster
graph-pattern-mining.centrality_rationale: GraphSet is one of the 8 in-scope evidence papers and the only one with a real automated correctness oracle (gtest hardcoded references), which the spec adopts as its own correctness cross-check.

graph-pattern-mining.title: STMatch: Accelerating Graph Pattern Matching on GPU with Stack-Based Loop Optimizations
graph-pattern-mining.one_liner: STMatch: stack-based GPU graph pattern matching avoiding subgraph-centric sync/memory issues
graph-pattern-mining.regime: stack-based GPU pattern matching, 24 patterns (5-7 vertices) on wiki-Vote/Enron/youtube/LiveJournal
graph-pattern-mining.centrality_rationale: STMatch is one of the 8 in-scope evidence papers directly cited in the spec's recommended_subset (mico/cit-Patents/com-youtube usage) and pattern-size framing.

graph-pattern-mining.title: VSGM: View-Based GPU-Accelerated Subgraph Matching on Large Graphs
graph-pattern-mining.one_liner: VSGM: view-based multi-GPU subgraph matching pipeline hiding communication overhead
graph-pattern-mining.regime: view-based multi-GPU subgraph matching, 19 named patterns + k-clique/k-motif sweeps on com-friendster
graph-pattern-mining.centrality_rationale: VSGM is one of the 8 in-scope evidence papers and is literally cited by name for both the named_5v_plus pattern definitions and the com-friendster billion-edge graph in the spec's recommended_subset; its headline design is an explicit communication-hiding multi-GPU pipeline, so no meaningful single-GPU path is claimed.

graph-pattern-mining.title: cuTS: scaling subgraph isomorphism on distributed multi-GPU systems using trie based data structure
graph-pattern-mining.one_liner: cuTS: trie-based distributed multi-GPU subgraph isomorphism, drastically reduces intermediate storage
graph-pattern-mining.regime: trie-based distributed multi-GPU subgraph isomorphism, 33 patterns on 6 SNAP graphs, cross-diffed vs GSI
graph-pattern-mining.centrality_rationale: cuTS is one of the 8 in-scope evidence papers whose 6 SNAP graphs and 33-pattern sweep the spec's suite selection draws on, but it is explicitly a distributed multi-GPU system, not a single-GPU candidate.

tensor-contraction.title: Einsum Trees: An Abstraction for Optimizing the Execution of Tensor Expressions
tensor-contraction.one_liner: Einsum Tree IR globally optimizes data layout of contraction paths on Arm and x86 CPUs
tensor-contraction.regime: TCCG binary-contraction cases + named tensor-network application trees, fp32, CPU/ARM
tensor-contraction.centrality_rationale: Explicitly named in the spec's tccg-tree-kernel-fp32 variant as the source of the 'adjusted' TCCG configuration used.

tensor-contraction.title: cuKE: An Efficient Code Generator for Score Function Computation in Knowledge Graph Embedding
tensor-contraction.one_liner: cuKE: code generator fusing KGE score-function tensor ops into CUDA, 14.9x over TorchScript.
tensor-contraction.regime: knowledge-graph-embedding score functions (TransE/TransH/TransR/etc.) on real KGs, fused CUDA code
tensor-contraction.centrality_rationale: cuKE's headline IS a code generator for exactly the batched fused KGE score-function contractions the spec's kge-batched-fused-kernel-fp32 variant targets.

tensor-contraction.title: Fast Kronecker Matrix-Matrix Multiplication on GPUs
tensor-contraction.one_liner: Custom fused GPU kernels for Kronecker matrix-matrix multiplication beating tensor-algebra baselines
tensor-contraction.regime: Kronecker matrix-matrix multiplication, microbenchmark grid + 28 real-world sizes, NVIDIA GPU
tensor-contraction.centrality_rationale: Explicitly the sole anchor for the spec's kron-matmul-kernel-fp32-fp64 variant, which reuses FastKron's own Table 4 sizes verbatim.

tensor-contraction.title: Closing the "quantum supremacy" gap: achieving real-time simulation of a random quantum circuit using a new Sunway supercomputer
tensor-contraction.one_liner: Sunway tensor-contraction random-quantum-circuit simulator: fused permute-multiply, 1.2 Eflop/s
tensor-contraction.regime: extreme-scale random-quantum-circuit tensor-network contraction (Google Sycamore 53-qubit), Sunway supercomputer
tensor-contraction.centrality_rationale: Explicitly the anchor for the spec's quantum-circuit-contraction-kernel variant (Sycamore circuit reproduction target); Sunway architecture, not NVIDIA GPU.

spmv.title: Diagonal-Budgeted Trotterization for Efficient Quantum Hamiltonian Simulation
spmv.one_liner: Diagonal-sparse data layout and CUDA/SIMD kernels for classical Hamiltonian sim, huge speedups over Qiskit-Aer
spmv.regime: diagonal-structured Hamiltonian matrices (HamLib suite), custom diagonal-sparse layout, not general CSR
spmv.centrality_rationale: HamSim builds a diagonal-sparse matvec kernel but the headline contribution and evaluation are the full Hamiltonian-simulation speedup vs Qiskit-Aer, not isolated y=Ax throughput vs SpMV libraries; the diagonal-only structure and quantum-sim workload (HamLib) differ fundamentally from SuiteSparse.

spmv.title: RASSM: Residue-based Acceleration of Single Sparse Matrix Computation via Adaptive Tiling
spmv.one_liner: Residue-guided adaptive 2D tiling for CPU sparse kernels; 1.36x over MKL SpMM, beats ASpT and J-Stream.
spmv.regime: n/a - no SpMV implementation shipped
spmv.centrality_rationale: Per benchspecs/spmv/survey.md #10, RASSM's abstract advertises SpMV/SpTS among its SSMKs but the public artifact's kernel dispatch only implements spmm/sddmm; a repo-wide search for spmv returns zero hits, so it is excluded from the spmv spec entirely.

spmv.title: SSpMV: A Sparsity-aware SpMV Framework Empowered by Multimodal Machine Learning
spmv.one_liner: ML-based SpMV algorithm/parameter autotuning beating sparse libraries on multi-core
spmv.regime: general SuiteSparse-style sparse matrices, multi-core CPU
spmv.centrality_rationale: SSpMV's headline is an ML-based algorithm/parameter selector specifically for SpMV, evaluated at kernel level against SOTA sparse libraries across multi-core platforms; CPU-only.

spmv.title: CB-SpMV: A Data Aggregating and Balance Algorithm for for Cache-Friendly Block-Based SpMV on GPUs
spmv.one_liner: Cache-friendly 2D-blocked GPU SpMV, up to 3.95x over cuSPARSE/TileSpMV/DASP
spmv.regime: SuiteSparse Matrix Collection (2,843 matrices), fp64, GPU
spmv.centrality_rationale: CB-SpMV's headline is a cache-friendly blocked SpMV kernel evaluated on 2,843 SuiteSparse matrices vs cuSPARSE-BSR/TileSpMV/DASP, kernel-level throughput on A100/RTX4090; survey confirms fp64 kernel-only timing.

spmv.title: Accelerating Sparse Linear Solvers on Intelligence Processing Units
spmv.one_liner: DSL-generated sparse linear solvers (SpMV/ILU/PBiCGStab) on Graphcore IPUs, up to 150x vs CPU/GPU.
spmv.regime: SuiteSparse + synthetic Poisson matrices, on IPU (not NVIDIA GPU)
spmv.centrality_rationale: A DSL/framework (CodeDSL/TensorDSL) that generates a suite of solvers (SpMV, ILU, PBiCGStab) for Graphcore IPUs -- SpMV is one generated kernel among several, though isolated SpMV scaling numbers on SuiteSparse are reported; platform is IPU, not an NVIDIA GPU.

spmv.title: A Conflict-aware Divide-and-Conquer Algorithm for Symmetric Sparse Matrix-Vector Multiplication
spmv.one_liner: DCS-SpMV: conflict-aware divide-and-conquer symmetric SpMV with ML-selected hybrid execution
spmv.regime: structurally+numerically symmetric SuiteSparse subset (rows>5e4, nnz>1e5), fp; x86/ARM CPU
spmv.centrality_rationale: DCS-SpMV's headline is exactly a symmetric-SpMV divide-and-conquer algorithm evaluated at kernel level vs SOTA on x86/ARM; its own criterion defines the spec's spmv-symmetric-kernel variant. CPU-only.

spmv.title: AmgT: Algebraic Multigrid Solver on Tensor Cores
spmv.one_liner: AmgT: tensor-core/mixed-precision SpGEMM+SpMV kernels for AMG setup/solve, up to 2.2x over HYPRE
spmv.regime: tensor-core mixed-precision SpMV inside AMG V-cycle (level-dependent fp64/fp32/fp16 cascade), workload-weighted over solver levels
spmv.centrality_rationale: AmgT's SpMV kernel is real and separately instrumented (time_spmv) but per benchspecs/spmv/survey.md, it is evaluated embedded in the AMG solve phase (up to 1,551 calls/run) rather than as an isolated kernel benchmark; overlaps the sequence-krylov variant's usage pattern but at mixed/lower precision.

spmv.title: Efficient Algorithm Design of Optimizing SpMV on GPU
spmv.one_liner: Flat and line-enhance CSR SpMV algorithms with adaptive selection on GPU
spmv.regime: general CSR-format sparse matrices, GPU
spmv.centrality_rationale: Headline is two new general-purpose GPU SpMV algorithms (flat/line-enhance) with adaptive selection, evaluated directly against existing GPU SpMV approaches.

spmv.title: PERKS: a Locality-Optimized Execution Model for Iterative Memory-bound GPU Applications
spmv.one_liner: Persistent-kernel locality optimization for iterative stencil/CG GPU kernels
spmv.regime: SuiteSparse SpMV datasets ('smaller'/'larger' tiers), fp, GPU
spmv.centrality_rationale: PERKS's headline is a general persistent-kernel execution model demonstrated primarily on 2D/3D stencils, with a Krylov-subspace CG/SpMV instantiation as a secondary generality demonstration; it does report isolated SpMV speedups on SuiteSparse subsets vs a SOTA library.

spmv.title: Memory-aware Optimization for Sequences of Sparse Matrix-Vector Multiplications
spmv.one_liner: Memory-aware partitioning/pipelining for sequences of SpMV, beating Intel MKL on 4 CPU platforms
spmv.regime: sequence of SpMV calls (Ax, A^2x, ..., linear combinations) on the same matrix, SuiteSparse-class, CPU (ARM+Intel)
spmv.centrality_rationale: FBMPK's headline is exactly optimizing a bounded sequence of SpMV invocations on the same matrix; explicitly named in the spec as the paper defining the spmv-sequence-krylov variant.

spmv.title: Serpens: a high bandwidth memory based accelerator for general-purpose sparse matrix-vector multiplication
spmv.one_liner: HBM-based FPGA SpMV accelerator with memory-centric engines, beats GraphLily/Sextans/K80 GPU
spmv.regime: general SuiteSparse Matrix Collection (2,519 matrices, geomean density 1.4e-3), fp32, FPGA
spmv.centrality_rationale: Serpens's headline is a general-purpose HBM FPGA SpMV accelerator evaluated on the near-exhaustive SuiteSparse suite vs GraphLily/Sextans/K80 GPU at kernel level ('Kernel time' explicitly labeled in code); FPGA-only artifact.

spmv.title: An Integral-equation-oriented Vectorized SpMV Algorithm and its Application on CT Imaging Reconstruction
spmv.one_liner: CSCV sparse format + vectorized SpMV for CT imaging reconstruction, up to 3.7x over MKL
spmv.regime: CT-imaging / integral-equation-derived sparse matrices, fp32, CPU SIMD
spmv.centrality_rationale: CSCV's headline is a new SpMV format+vectorized-kernel evaluated at kernel level against 7 SOTA SpMV implementations, but the test matrices are domain-specific (CT-imaging/integral-equation derived) rather than the track's general SuiteSparse suite -- narrower emphasis than the general variant.

spmv.title: Bit-GraphBLAS: Bit-Level Optimizations of Matrix-Centric Graph Processing on GPU
spmv.one_liner: Bit-Block CSR (B2SR) format; bit-level GraphBLAS SpMV/SpGEMM sped up to 6555x on GPU
spmv.regime: 1-bit (binary/pattern-only) adjacency matrices, GPU
spmv.centrality_rationale: Bit-GraphBLAS reports explicit kernel-level SpMV speedups (up to 40x) for its B2SR bit-level format, but per benchspecs/spmv/survey.md this 521-matrix binary domain is explicitly excluded from the general fp SpMV variant since 1-bit storage changes the byte-accounting model.

spmv.title: AlphaSparse: Generating High Performance SpMV Codes Directly from Sparse Matrices
spmv.one_liner: AlphaSparse auto-generates novel SpMV formats+kernels per input matrix, 3.2x over hand-designed formats
spmv.regime: general SuiteSparse Matrix Collection (843 matrices), CPU/ARM
spmv.centrality_rationale: AlphaSparse's headline is auto-generating novel SpMV formats/kernels per input matrix, evaluated at kernel level against 5 SOTA hand-designed formats plus autotuning baselines across SuiteSparse.

spmv.title: Vectorizing Sparse Matrix Computations with Partially-Strided Codelets
spmv.one_liner: Partially-strided codelet mining vectorizes SpMV/SpMM/SpTRSV, beats MKL by up to 4.1x
spmv.regime: general sparse matrices, CPU, fp
spmv.centrality_rationale: LCM I/E's vectorization technique targets a family of sparse kernels (SpMV/SpMM/SpTRSV) with an explicit, separately-reported SpMV speedup (1.67x) vs MKL at kernel level -- SpMV is a primary named member of the evaluated family.

spmv.title: Combinatorial BLAS 2.0: Scaling Combinatorial Algorithms on Distributed-Memory Systems
spmv.one_liner: Combinatorial BLAS 2.0: distributed-memory sparse/graph BLAS primitives with GPU kernel support
spmv.regime: large-scale distributed/combinatorial graph matrices, CPU/GPU/distributed
spmv.centrality_rationale: CombBLAS 2.0 is a general distributed-memory combinatorial-algorithms library; SpMV is one of many primitives, evaluated mainly via scaling/application benchmarks across the whole library rather than isolated kernel-vs-vendor-library throughput -- hardest call in this group since GPU kernel support exists but is not the paper's evaluation focus.

spmv.title: Scaling up HBM Efficiency of Top-K SpMV for Approximate Embedding Similarity on FPGAs
spmv.one_liner: Top-K SpMV on HBM FPGA with packet-wise CSR compression and reduced precision; 100x vs CPU, 2x vs GPU.
spmv.regime: mostly synthetic embedding-similarity matrices (+1 real GloVe matrix), reduced/fixed-point precision, FPGA
spmv.centrality_rationale: Top-K SpMV fuses a top-k reduction into the SpMV kernel for approximate embedding similarity search -- a distinct operation from the spec's plain y=Ax, evaluated with ranking-quality metrics (not elementwise tolerance) on mostly-synthetic data; FPGA-only.

spmv.title: TileSpMV: A Tiled Algorithm for Sparse Matrix-Vector Multiplication on GPUs
spmv.one_liner: TileSpMV: tiled 2D-sparsity-aware SpMV on GPU with per-tile format selection, up to 426x over BSR.
spmv.regime: full SuiteSparse Matrix Collection, GPU
spmv.centrality_rationale: TileSpMV's headline is a general tiled GPU SpMV algorithm evaluated across the full SuiteSparse collection vs Merge-SpMV/CSR5/BSR at kernel level.

spmv.title: A Split Execution Model for SpTRSV
spmv.one_liner: Split-execution model dividing SpTRSV into two sub-solves plus SpMV across CPU/GPU, up to 10x speedup
spmv.regime: SpMV used only as a residual/correction sub-step inside an SpTRSV DAG split, SuiteSparse triangular matrices
spmv.centrality_rationale: The paper's contribution is a split-execution model for SpTRSV; SpMV appears only as a byproduct term of the DAG split (one of two sub-solves plus an SpMV), never independently optimized or benchmarked as a standalone kernel.

spmv.title: Adaptive SpMV/SpMSpV on GPUs for Input Vectors of Varied Sparsity
spmv.one_liner: Adaptive SpMV/SpMSpV kernel-selection framework for varied input-vector sparsity on GPUs
spmv.regime: SuiteSparse-class matrices with varied input-vector sparsity (SpMV/SpMSpV), GPU
spmv.centrality_rationale: Headline is an adaptive ML-based kernel-selection framework specifically for SpMV/SpMSpV evaluated at kernel level on GPUs; emphasis on varied vector sparsity is narrower than the spec's plain dense-vector SpMV variant.

ntt.title: Cheddar: A Swift Fully Homomorphic Encryption Library Designed for GPU Architectures
ntt.one_liner: 32-bit GPU FHE library with architecture-tuned, fused NTT/CKKS kernels; 2.18-4.45x over prior GPU FHE.
ntt.regime: NTT/INTT over Z_q[x]/(x^N+1) with 32-bit RNS-CKKS moduli, always fused inside HMult/HRot/HAdd/Rescale ops or whole-FHE-workload runs, never timed in isolation
ntt.centrality_rationale: Cheddar's headline is a GPU FHE library with fused elementary-CKKS-op kernels; NTT is a real, well-defined sub-kernel but is architecturally never isolated, matching the spec's dedicated ntt-embedded-fhe-op variant rather than a standalone microkernel claim.

sparse-tensor-contraction.title: Insum: Sparse GPU Kernels Simplified and Optimized with Indirect Einsums
sparse-tensor-contraction.one_liner: Indirect-Einsum compiler plus GroupCOO formats generating tensor-core sparse GPU kernels; 1.14-3.81x speedups.
sparse-tensor-contraction.regime: sparse(-structured/unstructured)-times-dense indirect-einsum GPU kernels (structured SpMM, unstructured SpMM, point-cloud sparse conv, equivariant tensor product), fp32/fp16, single NVIDIA GPU
sparse-tensor-contraction.centrality_rationale: Insum is the sole and literal basis for the spec's sparse-dense-indirect-einsum-gpu-kernel variant, whose recommended_subset is drawn directly from Insum's own evaluation classes.

sparse-tensor-contraction.title: Efficient Parallel Sparse Tensor Contraction
sparse-tensor-contraction.one_liner: Hashing-based parallel sparse tensor contraction (SpGETT) beats SpGEMM-based approaches by ~21-25%.
sparse-tensor-contraction.regime: sparse-tensor x sparse-tensor contraction (SpGETT) on real FROSTT N-mode tensors, fp64, CPU
sparse-tensor-contraction.centrality_rationale: parTC is the sole and literal basis for the spec's sparse-sparse-tensor-contraction-frostt-kernel-fp64 variant, whose recommended_subset (nips, uber, chicago-crime, etc.) is drawn directly from parTC's own worked examples.

sparse-tensor-contraction.title: SparseLNR: accelerating sparse tensor computations using loop nest restructuring
sparse-tensor-contraction.one_liner: Loop-nest restructuring codegen for sparse tensor algebra (TACO)
sparse-tensor-contraction.regime: fused multi-operator composite sparse-tensor-algebra expression chains (SDDMM->SpMM->GEMM etc.) via loop-nest restructuring, real SuiteSparse/FROSTT tensors, CPU
sparse-tensor-contraction.centrality_rationale: SparseLNR is the sole and literal basis for the spec's composite-fused-sparse-tensor-algebra-kernel variant, whose 14-matrix/5-tensor suite is drawn directly from this paper's own evaluation set.

attention-kernel.title: PAT: Accelerating LLM Decoding via Prefix-Aware Attention with Resource Efficient Multi-Tile Kernel
attention-kernel.one_liner: Prefix-aware multi-tile GPU decode-attention kernel exploiting hierarchical shared-prefix KV reuse.
attention-kernel.regime: paged fp16 KV cache decode attention, GQA-heavy, saturating batch sizes, GPU
attention-kernel.centrality_rationale: PAT's headline is exactly a prefix-aware decode-attention kernel; the spec's attn-decode-kv-cache-kernel variant is built directly around PAT's own claim and shapes.

attention-kernel.title: RedFuser: An Automatic Operator Fusion Framework for Cascaded Reductions on AI Accelerators
attention-kernel.one_liner: Automatic fusion of cascaded reductions (e.g. softmax+GEMM) into single kernels; 2-5x over AI compilers.
attention-kernel.regime: MHA/MLA shapes (BERT/ViT/LLaMA-65B/DeepSeek-R1), fp, GPU (A10/H800 per survey)
attention-kernel.centrality_rationale: RedFuser is a general cascaded-reduction fusion compiler; attention (softmax+GEMM) is one of several fused patterns alongside MoE routing and FP8-quantized GEMM, matching the compiler/DSL-generates-this-kernel-among-others definition, though its named MHA/MLA sources match the spec's prefill regime well.

attention-kernel.title: Hexcute: A Compiler Framework for Automating Layout Synthesis in GPU Programs
attention-kernel.one_liner: Hexcute auto-synthesizes GPU tensor layouts, matching cuBLAS/FlashAttention, 6.46x over Triton on MoE
attention-kernel.regime: MHA prefill (batch1/heads32/d64/seq2048) and flash-decoding shapes, fp, GPU
attention-kernel.centrality_rationale: Hexcute is a general GPU-layout-synthesis compiler; attention is one of four benchmarked kernel classes (GEMM, Attention, FP8 GEMM, warp-specialized) plus MoE/Mamba, but its own benchmark_attention.py shapes are explicitly named as defining the spec's prefill-kernel suite.

attention-kernel.title: FlashAttention-T: Towards Fully Tensorized Attention by Exploiting Tensor-Vector Parallelism
attention-kernel.one_liner: FlashAttention-T: fully tensorized GEMM+softmax attention exploiting tensor-vector parallelism
attention-kernel.regime: fused GEMM+softmax attention, tensor-vector parallelism, GPU
attention-kernel.centrality_rationale: FlashAttention-T's headline is exactly a fully-tensorized fused attention kernel evaluated against FlashAttention baselines at kernel level; explicitly named in the spec.

attention-kernel.title: MetaAttention: A Unified and Performant Attention Framework across Hardware Backends
attention-kernel.one_liner: MetaAttention: unified attention-kernel generation framework across hardware backends
attention-kernel.regime: unified attention across FlashAttention-style algorithm variants, NVIDIA+AMD GPU
attention-kernel.centrality_rationale: MetaAttention's sole target is attention-kernel generation across hardware backends (not a multi-kernel-class compiler like RedFuser/Hexcute), evaluated at kernel level against FlashAttention on both NVIDIA and AMD.

attention-kernel.title: Optimizing Attention by Exploiting Data Reuse on ARM Multi-core CPUs
attention-kernel.one_liner: Memory-efficient fused attention kernels for ARM multi-core CPUs
attention-kernel.regime: full-sequence self-attention, fp32, ARM multi-core CPU
attention-kernel.centrality_rationale: MEATTEN is the track's sole CPU paper and directly defines the spec's attn-cpu-kernel-multicore variant.

attention-kernel.title: ByteTransformer: A High-Performance Transformer Boosted for Variable-Length Inputs
attention-kernel.one_liner: Padding-free fused MHA kernel for variable-length transformers, 6.13x over PyTorch on A100
attention-kernel.regime: BERT-style bidirectional MHA, variable-length/padding-free, fp, GPU
attention-kernel.centrality_rationale: ByteTransformer's headline is a padding-free fused MHA kernel evaluated against PyTorch at kernel level; its BERT-base sweep directly defines part of the spec's prefill-kernel input suite.

attention-kernel.title: LightSeq2: Accelerated Training for Transformer-Based Models on GPUs
attention-kernel.one_liner: LightSeq2: GPU kernel optimizations for Transformer training compute/memory patterns, 1.4-3.5x speedup
attention-kernel.regime: fp16/int8 Transformer training kernels (embeddings, layers, attention), GPU
attention-kernel.centrality_rationale: LightSeq2 optimizes the whole Transformer training pipeline (embeddings, encoder/decoder, attention, etc.); attention is one of many fused kernels and evaluation is end-to-end training speedup, not an isolated attention-kernel throughput number.

attention-kernel.title: E.T.: re-thinking self-attention for transformer models on GPUs
attention-kernel.one_liner: E.T.: re-engineered self-attention GPU operators plus pruning, beats TensorRT/FasterTransformer
attention-kernel.centrality_rationale: E.T.'s headline includes a re-engineered self-attention operator (plus a separate pruning contribution) evaluated against TensorRT/FasterTransformer; one of the 9 papers the spec was directly built from.

dnn-operator-fusion.title: RedFuser: An Automatic Operator Fusion Framework for Cascaded Reductions on AI Accelerators
dnn-operator-fusion.one_liner: Automatic fusion of cascaded reductions (e.g. softmax+GEMM) into single kernels; 2-5x over AI compilers.
dnn-operator-fusion.regime: automatic fusion of cascaded reductions (softmax+GEMM, MHA/MLA, MoE routing, FP8-quant-GEMM) into single kernels
dnn-operator-fusion.centrality_rationale: RedFuser is one of the two primary evidence papers this spec is built around, reported at exactly the subgraph granularity the fusion-subgraph variant measures, with 4 of its own pattern types (MHA/MLA/MoE-routing/FP8-quant-GEMM) forming the variant's pattern set.

dnn-operator-fusion.title: Accelerating Sparse Transformer Inference on GPU
dnn-operator-fusion.one_liner: STOF: row/block-wise sparse-attention kernels plus searched operator-fusion templates, 1.6x MHA speedup
dnn-operator-fusion.regime: sparse-attention kernels plus searched fusion templates across kernel, subgraph, e2e-model, and tuning-time granularities
dnn-operator-fusion.centrality_rationale: STOF is the other primary evidence paper; its own three benchmark scripts (kernel-level 10/20, end-to-end 10/10, and its Table 4 search-time comparison) map one-to-one onto the spec's fusion-single-kernel, fusion-e2e-model, and fusion-compile-search-time variants.

dnn-operator-fusion.title: A Multi-level Compiler Backend for Accelerated Micro-kernels Targeting RISC-V ISA Extensions
dnn-operator-fusion.one_liner: MLIR compiler backend generating DNN micro-kernels for RISC-V streaming-register accelerator
dnn-operator-fusion.regime: unconfirmed — MLIR compiler backend for RISC-V streaming-register accelerator generating unspecified DNN micro-kernels
dnn-operator-fusion.centrality_rationale: The spec's own notes_on_fairness admits this paper 'only fits the taxonomy' at one corner and contributes no concrete numeric defaults; its listed artifact repo turned out to be an unrelated protobuf-acceleration project, so no fusion-specific behavior, shapes, or baselines could be confirmed at all, and its platform is a non-GPU RISC-V accelerator.

dnn-operator-fusion.title: LightSeq2: Accelerated Training for Transformer-Based Models on GPUs
dnn-operator-fusion.one_liner: LightSeq2: GPU kernel optimizations for Transformer training compute/memory patterns, 1.4-3.5x speedup
dnn-operator-fusion.regime: GPU kernel fusion for Transformer training (operator-level + full-training-model-level), V100/A100
dnn-operator-fusion.centrality_rationale: LightSeq2 is one of the two hand-written reference papers the spec's fusion-e2e-model variant is modeled on, reporting both an operator-level granularity (e.g. LayerNorm ~4x) and a full-training-model-level number exactly as the variant requires.

dnn-operator-fusion.title: SumMerge: an efficient algorithm and implementation for weight repetition-aware DNN inference
dnn-operator-fusion.one_liner: SumMerge: weight-repetition-aware DNN inference kernel factorizing/memoizing sub-computations in software
dnn-operator-fusion.regime: unconfirmed — weight-repetition factorization/memoization inside a single quantized conv/GEMM kernel on CPU
dnn-operator-fusion.centrality_rationale: The spec's own evidence entry states this is 'not a multi-op fusion chain' but a single-kernel redundancy-elimination technique, and calls the paper abstract-only with an empty-stub artifact and a paywalled PDF, so it barely fits the operator-fusion definition this track measures.

scan-reduction.title: RedFuser: An Automatic Operator Fusion Framework for Cascaded Reductions on AI Accelerators
scan-reduction.one_liner: Automatic fusion of cascaded reductions (e.g. softmax+GEMM) into single kernels; 2-5x over AI compilers.
scan-reduction.regime: online-softmax-then-GEMM cascaded reduction, GPU (A10/H800 per survey)
scan-reduction.centrality_rationale: RedFuser's headline methodology IS generalized cascaded-reduction fusion (of which softmax-then-GEMM is the canonical instance), evaluated at kernel level (2-5x over compilers, matching hand-written kernels); this matches the scan-reduction-fused-cascaded variant almost exactly. Note the platform field says 'other' but benchspecs/attention-kernel/survey.md confirms NVIDIA A10/H800 hardware.

scan-reduction.title: GPU Tensor Cores for Fast Arithmetic Reductions
scan-reduction.one_liner: Tensor-core MMA-based parallel arithmetic reduction, 3.2x faster than standard GPU reduction, 2x vs CUB
scan-reduction.regime: flat sum-reduction over large GPU-resident arrays, GPU
scan-reduction.centrality_rationale: Headline is exactly a tensor-core arithmetic-reduction kernel; explicitly named as defining the spec's scan-reduction-flat-kernel variant.

scan-reduction.title: Compiling generalized histograms for GPU
scan-reduction.one_liner: Work-efficient generalized-histogram codegen for GPU (Futhark), outperforms CUB.
scan-reduction.centrality_rationale: Headline is exactly generalized-histogram GPU codegen; explicitly named as defining the spec's scan-reduction-segmented-histogram variant.

quantized-gemm.title: Tilus: A Tile-Level GPGPU Programming Language for Low-Precision Computation
quantized-gemm.one_liner: Tile-level GPU DSL generating 1-8 bit low-precision GEMM kernels; 1.75x over Triton, beats Marlin
quantized-gemm.regime: tile-level DSL generating fused low-precision GEMM (1-8 bit) for real LLM linear layers, decode batches
quantized-gemm.centrality_rationale: Tilus is a general tile-level GPGPU DSL (arbitrary 1-8 bit types) whose flagship showcase is fused-dequant GEMM, so it fits the compiler/DSL-generates-this-kernel component rule; its own protocol (CUDA events, 50 reps median, L2 cleared, Gemma-2/Qwen2.5/Llama-3.3 shapes) is close kin to the spec's own decode-kernel protocol.

quantized-gemm.title: ZipServ: Fast and Memory-Efficient LLM Inference with Hardware-Aware Lossless Compression
quantized-gemm.one_liner: Tensor-core-aware lossless weight compression with fused decompress-GEMM kernel; 2.21x over cuBLAS
quantized-gemm.regime: lossless bit-exact weight compression (~30% size reduction) + fused decompress-GEMM (ZipGEMM), real LLM linear-layer shapes, fp16 tensor cores
quantized-gemm.centrality_rationale: Headline is a fused decompress+GEMM kernel evaluated kernel-level (2.21x cuBLAS) with e2e kept separate, structurally the same fused-dequant-GEMM pattern the spec measures; but it is lossless (bit-exact) compression not lossy weight quantization, so the model-accuracy variant is trivially a zero delta and the spec itself flags its correctness gate should differ from the 1e-3 tolerance.

quantized-gemm.title: QIGen: A Kernel Generator for Inference on Nonuniformly Quantized Large Language Models
quantized-gemm.one_liner: QIGen generates CPU matrix-vector kernels for nonuniformly quantized LLM inference
quantized-gemm.regime: CPU/AVX2 nonuniform-quantized matrix-VECTOR (GEMV) kernels for LLM inference, no GPU path
quantized-gemm.centrality_rationale: QIGen is explicitly a kernel generator (codegen) — matches the compiler/DSL component rule — and the spec's own notes_on_fairness names it as out-of-scope for the dense-GPU qgemm-* variants because it targets CPU GEMV, not GPU GEMM.

quantized-gemm.title: High-Throughput Non-uniformly Quantized 3-bit LLM Inference
quantized-gemm.one_liner: Quantix: fused dequant+matmul kernel for 3-bit LLM inference, 4.82x over FP16 cuBLAS
quantized-gemm.regime: non-uniform 3-bit weight-only quantization, fused dequant+matmul, batched LLM inference on GPU
quantized-gemm.centrality_rationale: Headline is a fused dequant-matmul GPU kernel with kernel-level speedup vs FP16 cuBLAS (4.82x), matching the spec's core operation; regime is only partially confirmed since the spec's own open_questions flag that Quantix's exact shapes/protocol could not be recovered from its paywalled paper/thin README.

quantized-gemm.title: QFactory: Accelerating Quantized Large Language Model Serving with Qtile Graphs
quantized-gemm.one_liner: Qtile-graph compiler generating quantized LLM kernels; 1.66x kernel and 1.23x end-to-end speedup
quantized-gemm.regime: Qtile-graph compiler generating quantized LLM GEMM kernels, matrix-size and bit-width sweeps, kernel+e2e split by GPU
quantized-gemm.centrality_rationale: QFactory is a compilation framework (Qtile/QGraph abstraction) that generates quantized kernels among a transformable search space, fitting the compiler/DSL component rule; its AE README's matrix-size/bit-width ablations and Marlin/BitBLAS baselines closely match the spec's suite.

quantized-gemm.title: MARLIN: Mixed-Precision Auto-Regressive Parallel Inference on Large Language Models
quantized-gemm.one_liner: Mixed-precision GPU GEMM kernels enabling memory-bound batched LLM inference speedups
quantized-gemm.regime: weight-only INT4/mixed-precision GEMM, LLaMA/Falcon-180B linear-layer shapes, batched decode regime
quantized-gemm.centrality_rationale: MARLIN is the canonical hand-written kernel this spec's variant is built around — its exact per-layer LLaMA/Falcon-180B shapes are copied verbatim into the spec's recommended_subset.

quantized-gemm.title: MXBLAS: Accelerating 8-bit Deep Learning with a Unified Micro-Scaled GEMM Library
quantized-gemm.one_liner: Unified micro-scaled 8-bit (MX-format) GEMM library removing model-specific kernel coupling
quantized-gemm.centrality_rationale: MXBLAS is a library whose headline IS the MX-GEMM kernel, evaluated kernel-level; it is the direct source of the spec's qgemm-w8a8-mx variant (including the flush_l2 fairness correction the spec applies to its own default).

quantized-gemm.title: Quant-LLM: Accelerating the Serving of Large Language Models via FP6-Centric Algorithm-System Co-Design on Modern GPUs
quantized-gemm.one_liner: TC-FPx: first Tensor-Core GPU GEMM kernels for FP6/arbitrary-bit weights; 1.69-2.65x over FP16 LLM inference
quantized-gemm.regime: FP6/arbitrary-bit Tensor-Core GEMM, LLaMA/OPT linear layers, batch {8,16,32}, PPL/zero-shot accuracy reported separately
quantized-gemm.centrality_rationale: TC-FPx/Quant-LLM is one of only two papers the spec calls out as treating model-level accuracy as first-class alongside kernel speed, and its batch-crossover finding (0.94x slowdown at batch=32) directly motivated the spec's batched-kernel variant.

quantized-gemm.title: MixQ: Taming Dynamic Outliers in Mixed-Precision Quantization by Online Prediction
quantized-gemm.one_liner: MixQ: locality-based outlier prediction enables efficient mixed-precision LLM quantization kernel
quantized-gemm.regime: outlier-aware mixed-precision (W8A8/W4A16) quantized GEMM for LLaMA-2/3, Falcon, ChatGLM, Qwen2 decode
quantized-gemm.centrality_rationale: The spec's own notes_on_fairness explicitly warns MixQ's headline throughput is a full autoregressive HF generate() decode loop, not isolated GEMM kernel time, which is the textbook 'evaluation is end-to-end' component case even though the quantization technique itself is real and substantial.

quantized-gemm.title: Efficiently emulating high-bitwidth computation with low-bitwidth hardware
quantized-gemm.one_liner: Emulating high-bitwidth computation on low-bitwidth hardware (precision emulation) for DSAs/GPUs
quantized-gemm.regime: FP32/INT16 precision EMULATION via low-bit Tensor-Core primitives (opposite direction: preserving high precision, not reducing model weight precision)
quantized-gemm.centrality_rationale: APE emulates high-bitwidth (FP32/INT16) results FROM low-bit hardware primitives for numerical fidelity, the inverse motivation of weight-quantization for LLM serving; the survey itself lists it as out-of-scope ('not GEMM-specific' to this track), and it has no LLM/weight-compression connection at all.

quantized-gemm.title: QGTC: accelerating quantized graph neural networks via GPU tensor core
quantized-gemm.one_liner: QGTC: Tensor-Core CUDA kernels for any-bitwidth quantized GNN computation, 2.7x over DGL
quantized-gemm.regime: bit-serial arbitrary-bitwidth (INT1-decomposed) GEMM/sparse-matmul on synthetic square shapes for quantized GNNs
quantized-gemm.centrality_rationale: QGTC's headline is a Tensor-Core low-bit GEMM kernel evaluated at kernel level (TFLOPs per bitwidth/shape vs cublasGemmEx), but the spec's own notes_on_fairness explicitly separates this bit-serial INT1-primitive family from the group-scaled dequantization family the mandatory variants target, and its synthetic square shapes have no LLM connection.

quantized-gemm.title: Efficient Quantized Sparse Matrix Operations on Tensor Cores
quantized-gemm.one_liner: Magicube: quantized low-precision SpMM/SDDMM on Tensor Cores, up to 2.37x over vendor library
quantized-gemm.regime: quantized (int4/int8) SpMM/SDDMM on sparse pruned DNN weight matrices (DLMC), not dense GEMM
quantized-gemm.centrality_rationale: Magicube's kernel is fundamentally a SPARSE-operand quantized kernel; the spec's own notes_on_fairness lists it as explicitly out of scope for the dense qgemm-* variants and recommends it get its own sparse-quantized-gemm track (it is core to the sddmm group instead).

quantized-gemm.title: NITI: Training Integer Neural Networks Using Integer-Only Arithmetic
quantized-gemm.one_liner: NITI: integer-only (8-bit) DNN training via per-layer block-scaling quantization, GPU+FPGA impl.
quantized-gemm.regime: 8-bit integer TRAINING (fwd+bwd+update) with per-layer block scaling on MNIST/CIFAR/ImageNet CNNs, GPU+FPGA
quantized-gemm.centrality_rationale: NITI's evaluation is a full training loop on small vision CNNs, not isolated inference-GEMM kernel time; the spec's own evidence entry states it is explicitly out of scope for this inference-GEMM track (training, non-LLM shapes).

quantized-gemm.title: APNN-TC: accelerating arbitrary precision neural networks on ampere GPU tensor cores
quantized-gemm.one_liner: Arbitrary-precision GEMM emulation via int1 Ampere Tensor Core primitives, beats CUTLASS
quantized-gemm.regime: arbitrary 1-8 bit GEMM/CONV via INT1 Tensor-Core emulation, fixed synthetic shapes (no real LLM/network beyond small CNNs)
quantized-gemm.centrality_rationale: APNN-TC's headline is a low-precision GEMM/CONV kernel evaluated kernel-level (TOPS vs CUTLASS-INT4/INT1), but per the spec's fairness notes this bit-serial arbitrary-precision family is a fundamentally different implementation strategy from the group-scaled dequant family the mandatory variants cover, and its shapes are synthetic, not LLM-derived.

quantized-gemm.title: Accelerating Binarized Neural Networks via Bit-Tensor-Cores in Turing GPUs
quantized-gemm.one_liner: Bit-Tensor-Core BNN kernels (bit-GEMM, bit-convolution) on Turing GPUs, 77% faster than prior art
quantized-gemm.regime: 1-bit XNOR/bit-tensor-core GEMM+convolution for Binarized Neural Networks, ResNet-18/ImageNet
quantized-gemm.centrality_rationale: TCBNN's headline is a bit-GEMM/bit-conv kernel evaluated kernel-level (ResNet-18 images/sec), but it is native 1-bit XNOR-popcount arithmetic with no dequantize-to-fp16 step at all, the extreme end of the bit-serial family the spec's fairness notes exclude from its mandatory variants (the survey lists it only as APNN-TC's baseline, not deeply surveyed).

quantized-gemm.title: Automatic generation of high-performance quantized machine learning kernels
quantized-gemm.one_liner: Automatic generation/tuning of ultra-low-precision quantized ML inference kernels
quantized-gemm.regime: CPU/ARM automatic generation of ultra-low-bit (bit-serial) quantized GEMM/convolution kernels
quantized-gemm.centrality_rationale: A codegen/autotuning framework generating quantized kernels — the compiler/DSL component rule applies directly — and it is CPU/ARM-only; the survey calls it redundant with QIGen's CPU coverage and it is excluded from the GPU-oriented qgemm-* variants.

lossless-compression.title: ZipServ: Fast and Memory-Efficient LLM Inference with Hardware-Aware Lossless Compression
lossless-compression.one_liner: Tensor-core-aware lossless weight compression with fused decompress-GEMM kernel; 2.21x over cuBLAS
lossless-compression.regime: LLM weight-tensor operand feeding a downstream GEMM, fused decompress-into-Tensor-Core-registers, GPU
lossless-compression.centrality_rationale: Headline IS a lossless-compression format (TCA-TBE) + fused decompress-GEMM kernel, reported at kernel level (2.21x over cuBLAS) as well as end-to-end vLLM; this is exactly the structured-operand-fused variant's target case.

lossless-compression.title: MANS: Efficient and Portable ANS Encoding for Multi-Byte Integer Data on CPUs and GPUs
lossless-compression.one_liner: Portable ANS lossless encoder with adaptive multi-byte mapping for CPU/GPU, up to 288x GPU speedup
lossless-compression.regime: multi-byte integer data (adaptive data mapping), CPU and GPU (A100/MI210)
lossless-compression.centrality_rationale: Headline IS a general multi-byte ANS lossless encoder benchmarked at kernel-level throughput across CPU/GPU, matching the GPU multi-byte-integer variant's scope.

lossless-compression.title: lsCOMP: Efficient Light Source Compression
lossless-compression.one_liner: Single-kernel GPU compressor for light-source X-ray data, up to 509 GB/s, 20x faster than SOTA GPU compressors
lossless-compression.regime: X-ray light-source detector/sensor integer data, single-kernel GPU compressor, A100
lossless-compression.centrality_rationale: Headline IS a single-kernel GPU lossless/lossy compressor for scientific sensor/detector streams -- the exact HPC-scientific multi-byte-integer domain this variant's summary names explicitly.

lossless-compression.title: hZCCL: Accelerating Collective Communication with Co-Designed Homomorphic Compression
lossless-compression.one_liner: hZCCL: CPU-optimized homomorphic compressor enabling ops directly on compressed collective data
lossless-compression.regime: unspecified HPC application datasets (five named), CPU multi-core, embedded in an MPI-collective compression-communication co-design
lossless-compression.centrality_rationale: Abstract frames the lightweight CPU compressor as built 'in addition to' the paper's main contribution (a homomorphic compression-communication co-design for collectives); the compressor is real and separable but a component of the collective-communication system, and the evaluation is dominated by collective speedup, not standalone codec throughput.

lossless-compression.title: Rapidgzip: Parallel Decompression and Seeking in Gzip Files Using Cache Prefetching
lossless-compression.one_liner: Rapidgzip parallel gzip decompression via cache prefetching, 55x over gzip on 128 cores
lossless-compression.regime: generic byte-stream corpora (Silesia corpus, base64-encoded data), CPU multi-core
lossless-compression.centrality_rationale: Rapidgzip's headline IS a parallel gzip/DEFLATE decompressor benchmarked at kernel-level GB/s against GNU gzip on the Silesia corpus, exactly the generic byte-stream CPU variant's target.

lossless-compression.title: GPULZ: Optimizing LZSS Lossless Compression for Multi-byte Data on Modern GPUs
lossless-compression.one_liner: GPU LZSS lossless compression for multi-byte data, high throughput
lossless-compression.centrality_rationale: Headline IS a GPU LZSS lossless compressor specifically designed for multi-byte data, benchmarked at kernel-level throughput/ratio against SOTA GPU compressors.

lossless-compression.title: Optimizing Huffman Decoding for Error-Bounded Lossy Compression on GPUs
lossless-compression.one_liner: GPU Huffman decoder optimizations speed up cuSZ decompression by 2.43x on average
lossless-compression.regime: SZ/cuSZ quantization-code streams (8 scientific datasets), V100
lossless-compression.centrality_rationale: Headline IS an optimization of the Huffman-decoding lossless sub-kernel inside cuSZ, benchmarked at kernel level against cuSZ's own decoder -- exactly the SZ/cuSZ quantization-stream domain this variant's summary names.

other:json-parsing.title: cuJSON: A Highly Parallel JSON Parser for GPUs
other:json-parsing.one_liner: Branch-minimal, highly parallel JSON parsing algorithm and kernel for GPUs
other:json-parsing.regime: fully GPU-offloaded JSON parsing (UTF-8 validate+tokenize+nest), standard corpora
other:json-parsing.centrality_rationale: cuJSON's headline IS a GPU JSON-parsing algorithm/kernel, the sole and direct basis for this track's only variant.

hash-table.title: Towards Iterative Relational Algebra on the GPU
hash-table.one_liner: GPU hash-join with open-addressing table and operator fusion for iterative RA; up to 10.8x vs cuDF
hash-table.regime: 18 named real-world SNAP/DIMACS/road-network relations, GPU open-addressing build/probe join table, load_factor=0.4 fixed
hash-table.centrality_rationale: Survey.md states the paper's contribution is an iterative-Datalog transitive-closure engine using 'a standard equi-join build/probe table' as a supporting kernel, evaluated end-to-end via transitive closure rather than isolated hash-table throughput; its real relations are the explicit anchor for the spec's hash-table-build-probe-kernel variant.

hash-table.title: Distributed-Memory k-mer Counting on GPUs
hash-table.one_liner: First GPU-accelerated distributed-memory k-mer counter, up to 100x over CPU counters.
hash-table.regime: 6 named real genomic k-mer datasets at k=17, GPU counting/upsert hash table embedded in a distributed communication-optimized pipeline
hash-table.centrality_rationale: DEDUKT's paper-level speedups conflate hash-table counting with distributed communication/partitioning (which the spec's variant explicitly isolates out); it is the exact anchor for the spec's dataset list.

hash-table.title: Lock-free Concurrent Level Hashing for Persistent Memory
hash-table.one_liner: Lock-free concurrent level hashing on Optane persistent memory; up to 4.2x over prior PM hashing
hash-table.regime: YCSB workloads, Zipfian(0.99)/uniform, 15-byte keys/values, lock-free concurrent hash table on Optane persistent memory
hash-table.centrality_rationale: Headline IS the concurrent hash-table design; explicitly the sole track anchor for the spec's CRUD-mixed-ops variant. CPU/PM only, no GPU.

other:ann-search.title: X-HD: Fast Hausdorff Distance Computation with Ray Tracing
other:ann-search.one_liner: RT-core + CUDA Hausdorff-distance kernel, 5.3x over ITK
other:ann-search.regime: MRI/GIS/PLY real 2D-3D point clouds treated as k-NN queries (RT-core accelerated)
other:ann-search.centrality_rationale: X-HD's own deliverable is a Hausdorff-distance VALUE (a max-min reduction over k-NN results), which the spec explicitly puts out of scope for the ann-search variants — only its internal k-NN routine is a valid submission; its real point-cloud domains are, however, literally folded into the exact-spatial-knn-kernel suite.

other:ann-search.title: PathWeaver: A High-Throughput Multi-GPU System for Graph-Based Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
other:ann-search.one_liner: Multi-GPU graph-based ANNS with pipelined path extension and pruning; 3.24x geomean over SOTA
other:ann-search.regime: graph-based (CAGRA) approximate NN search, SIFT-128-euclidean, mean-recall@10 + median-latency per swept config
other:ann-search.centrality_rationale: PathWeaver is one of the 4 primary high-dim papers this spec's Pareto-recall/QPS variant is built around; although its headline 3.24x claim requires 4 GPUs+NVLink, the spec's own open_questions confirm a single-GPU harness script (single_pathweaver_one.py) exists and was read.

other:ann-search.title: CLOVER: A GPU-native, Spatio-graph-based Approach to Exact kNN
other:ann-search.one_liner: GPU-native graph-based exact kNN, 4-230x over grid/tree/FAISS
other:ann-search.regime: exact GPU k-NN via spatio-graph hubs+lower-bounds, synthetic uniform 3D points + real mesh point clouds
other:ann-search.centrality_rationale: CLOVER is the direct source of the exact-spatial-knn-kernel variant — its own dataset sizes/dimensions are copied into the spec's recommended_subset and its correctness gaps (dead-code check) are what the spec's mandatory correctness requirement fixes.

other:ann-search.title: DRIM-ANN: An Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search Engine based on Commercial DRAM-PIMs
other:ann-search.one_liner: DRIM-ANN: ANNS engine on UPMEM DRAM-PIM using lookup tables instead of squaring, up to 2.67x over GPU
other:ann-search.regime: IVF-PQ ANNS on SIFT/DEEP/SPACEV at 1B and 100M scale, 10K queries, recall@10>=0.8 floor
other:ann-search.centrality_rationale: DRIM-ANN is one of the 4 primary high-dim papers whose SIFT/DEEP/SPACEV suite the spec's recommended_subset is built from directly, but it runs on UPMEM DRAM-PIM hardware, not a GPU.

other:ann-search.title: UpANNS: Enhancing Billion-Scale ANNS Efficiency with Real-World PIM Architecture
other:ann-search.one_liner: PIM-accelerated billion-scale ANNS with data placement and early-pruning top-k, 4.3x QPS vs Faiss
other:ann-search.regime: PIM billion-scale ANNS with early-pruning top-k, same SIFT/DEEP/SPACEV suite as DRIM-ANN
other:ann-search.centrality_rationale: UpANNS is one of the 4 primary high-dim papers sharing the exact SIFT/DEEP/SPACEV suite the spec standardizes on, but it runs on PIM hardware ('other' platform), not a single GPU.

other:ann-search.title: Co-design Hardware and Algorithm for Vector Search
other:ann-search.one_liner: FANNS: FPGA hardware-algorithm co-design framework auto-generating vector search accelerators, up to 37x speedup
other:ann-search.regime: FPGA hardware-algorithm co-design auto-generating vector-search accelerators for user-given recall targets, SIFT/Deep100M
other:ann-search.centrality_rationale: FANNS has the most complete recall-Pareto framing of any surveyed paper and is the direct model for the spec's recall@{1,10,100}-vs-QPS metric and batch/single-query latency-distribution requirement, but it targets FPGA, not GPU.

other:ann-search.title: RTNN: accelerating neighbor search using hardware ray tracing
other:ann-search.one_liner: RTNN: maps neighbor search onto GPU ray-tracing hardware via query scheduling/partitioning, up to 65x speedup
other:ann-search.regime: RT-core-mapped exact/bounded-approximate low-dim (3D) neighbor search on KITTI/Stanford-3D/Millennium-N-body
other:ann-search.centrality_rationale: RTNN's three real domains are directly incorporated into the exact-spatial-knn-kernel variant's recommended_subset and its measured-error-rate practice for approximate radius relaxation is adopted as the spec's own reporting requirement.

stencil.title: WindStencil: Unleashing GPU Potential for High-Order Stencil Computation in High-Performance Inviscid CFD Simulations
stencil.one_liner: GPU-optimized high-order stencil kernels for inviscid CFD (title-only, no abstract)
stencil.regime: production 7th-order WENO CFD solver (BF3W fused kernel), whole-application timing with a separately reported kernel-focused ratio; AMD MI60/MI200 GPUs (HIP/ROCm), fp64
stencil.centrality_rationale: Headline contribution is the high-order stencil kernel for inviscid CFD; README reports an isolated kernel-focused gain alongside full-application speedup, which is exactly the spec's e2e-application variant (this paper is its own worked example in the spec). Note: input platform metadata says nvidia-gpu but survey.md documents AMD MI60/MI200 via HIP/ROCm with no NVIDIA path evidenced, so gpu_single_card is rated false against the survey, not the metadata tag.

stencil.title: High-Order-Preserving Acceleration of a Shallow-Water Dynamical Core Using Tensor Units
stencil.one_liner: Ozaki-scheme FP16 Tensor Cores accelerate high-order shallow-water stencil dynamical core, up to 4.34x speedup.
stencil.regime: full shallow-water dynamical core (HOPE) on the Williamson standard test suite, Ozaki-scheme fp16 Tensor Cores emulating fp64 accuracy, single NVIDIA GPU (A40/RTX A6000)
stencil.centrality_rationale: Headline is the Ozaki-scheme TCU stencil reformulation itself, and this paper is the explicit worked example for the spec's e2e-application variant (Williamson geostrophic-flow case named verbatim in its recommended_subset).

stencil.title: SPIDER: Unleashing Sparse Tensor Cores for Stencil Computation via Strided Swapping
stencil.one_liner: SPIDER: strided swapping reduces sparsity overhead of stencil-as-matmul on sparse tensor cores
stencil.regime: 1D/2D stencil-as-sparse-matmul on Sparse Tensor Cores, fp16, single A100, kernel microbenchmark
stencil.centrality_rationale: SPIDER is one of the four papers whose shared CLI/shape catalog literally defines the TCU-matmul variant; reports kernel-level GStencil/s vs cuDNN/ConvStencil/LoRAStencil/FlashFFTStencil with preprocessing excluded and measured separately, exactly the variant's protocol.

stencil.title: Efficient Locality-aware Instruction Stream Scheduling for Stencil Computation on ARM Processors
stencil.one_liner: AOStencil compiler: instruction-stream scheduling + GA tuning for stencils on ARM many-core, up to 4.4x
stencil.regime: synthetic 2D/3D box/star stencils (9pt/7pt/27pt), fp32 default (fp64 variant available), ARM many-core CPU (Kunpeng/Phytium), GA-tuned
stencil.centrality_rationale: AOStencil is explicitly named as one of the six papers defining variant 1's 'common denominator'; it is a domain-specific compiler exclusively for stencils, evaluated at kernel level via GCells/GFLOPS against SOTA domain-specific compilers.

stencil.title: FlashFFTStencil: Bridging Fast Fourier Transforms to Memory-Efficient Stencil Computations on Tensor Core Units
stencil.one_liner: Bridges FFT to dense stencil computation on Tensor Core Units, 2.57x avg speedup
stencil.regime: 1D/2D/3D stencil via FFT-bridged Tensor-Core matmul, fp16, A100/H100, kernel microbenchmark
stencil.centrality_rationale: FlashFFTStencil shares the ConvStencil/LoRAStencil/SPIDER CLI/timing convention that defines the TCU-matmul variant; headline 2.57x average kernel-level speedup over prior SOTA.

stencil.title: SARIS: Accelerating Stencil Computations on Energy-Efficient RISC-V Compute Clusters with Indirect Stream Registers
stencil.one_liner: Indirect stream registers on RISC-V compute clusters accelerate stencils 2.72x with 81% FPU utilization
stencil.regime: various stencil codes on an 8-core RISC-V compute cluster (Snitch) with indirect stream registers; precision/shape convention unconfirmed, plus an extrapolated 256-core projection not measured hardwar
stencil.centrality_rationale: Headline is stencil-acceleration hardware (indirect stream registers) evaluated at kernel level (speedup, FPU utilization) against an RV32G baseline -- same general-purpose-compute class as variant 1, but this paper wasn't in the depth survey and its shape/precision convention could not be checked against the named star/box catalog, so only partial confidence in suite overlap.

stencil.title: A Holistic Approach to Automatic Mixed-Precision Code Generation and Tuning for Affine Programs
stencil.one_liner: PrecTuner: unified mixed-precision code generator + autotuner for affine programs, up to 3.28x over LuIs
stencil.regime: PolyBench affine-kernel suite (stencil is one of several loop-nest kernel types) under a unified mixed-precision codegen+autotuner, CPU and GPU
stencil.centrality_rationale: PrecTuner is a general mixed-precision code generator/autotuner spanning the whole PolyBench affine-kernel family (GEMM, stencils, etc.), not a stencil-specific contribution -- fits the 'compiler/autotuner that generates this kernel among others' component case; device class matches variant 1 loosely but not its named shape/grid convention.

stencil.title: ConvStencil: Transform Stencil Computation to Matrix Multiplication on Tensor Cores
stencil.one_liner: Transforms stencil computation into matmul on Tensor Cores for large speedups
stencil.regime: 1D/2D/3D stencil-as-matmul on Tensor Cores, fp16-class, single A100, kernel microbenchmark
stencil.centrality_rationale: ConvStencil originates the shape/CLI catalog and bulk-timing idiom the whole TCU-matmul variant reuses verbatim; kernel-level GStencil/s vs cuDNN im2col baseline.

stencil.title: LoRAStencil: Low-Rank Adaptation of Stencil Computation on Tensor Cores
stencil.one_liner: LoRAStencil: low-rank decomposition of stencil weights removes redundancy on Tensor Cores, 2.16x
stencil.regime: 1D/2D/3D stencil-as-matmul on Tensor Cores (low-rank weight decomposition), fp16-class, single A100, kernel microbenchmark
stencil.centrality_rationale: LoRAStencil is explicitly named alongside ConvStencil/FlashFFTStencil/SPIDER as defining the TCU-matmul variant's shared CLI and shape catalog.

stencil.title: PERKS: a Locality-Optimized Execution Model for Iterative Memory-bound GPU Applications
stencil.one_liner: Persistent-kernel locality optimization for iterative stencil/CG GPU kernels
stencil.regime: 2D/3D Jacobi-style stencils (5/9/13/17/21/25pt) plus sparse variants, fp64 default, single NVIDIA GPU, persistent-kernel execution model
stencil.centrality_rationale: PERKS is explicitly named as one of the papers defining variant 1's 'common denominator'; reports kernel-level GCells/s, GFLOPS, and bandwidth against SOTA libraries.

stencil.title: A GPU-Accelerated AMR Solver for Gravitational Wave Propagation
stencil.one_liner: GPU-accelerated adaptive-mesh numerical-relativity solver: 6x over SOTA, 800 GFlops/s on an A100
stencil.regime: adaptive-mesh-refinement (octree) finite-difference update inside a full multi-GPU numerical-relativity solver, fp64; weak/strong scaling to hundreds of GPUs, with a single-A100 point (800 GFlops/s) a
stencil.centrality_rationale: The FD stencil update is one part of a much larger AMR gravitational-wave solver and is evaluated end-to-end (whole-simulation speedup/scaling), not as an isolated kernel; adaptive octree grids are also a structurally different regime than the spec's dense D-dimensional grid.

stencil.title: Memory Optimizations in an Array Language
stencil.one_liner: Functional array-language compiler with cost-free layout memory optimizations for GPU kernels
stencil.regime: Rodinia Hotspot 2D thermal-diffusion stencil benchmark at its standard problem size, single NVIDIA GPU; one of three unrelated Rodinia kernels (LUD, Hotspot, NW) generated by a general array-language
stencil.centrality_rationale: Futhark is a general-purpose array-language compiler evaluated across three unrelated Rodinia kernels, so stencil is one of several targets, not the paper's sole subject; Hotspot is a legitimate dense structured-grid stencil but uses Rodinia's own problem size/suite, not the AN5D/ConvStencil shape convention.

stencil.title: StencilFlow: Mapping Large Stencil Programs to Distributed Spatial Computing Systems
stencil.one_liner: StencilFlow maps stencil DAGs to FPGAs: 1.31/4.18 TOp/s single/multi-device, record FPGA stencil performance
stencil.regime: general stencil-DAG programs (including a production weather-simulation stencil) mapped to FPGA spatial hardware, single- and multi-device, TOp/s
stencil.centrality_rationale: Headline contribution is entirely stencil-DAG-to-hardware mapping, evaluated at kernel level (TOp/s) -- the whole paper is about stencils, matching 'core'; but FPGA device class and heterogeneous-DAG framing differ from the CPU/GPU shape/grid convention, though the spec's own variant-1 digest cites sibling FPGA paper StencilsOnFPGA as informing the same general-purpose-compute class.

stencil.title: Towards a Domain-Extensible Compiler: Optimizing an Image Processing Pipeline on Mobile CPUs
stencil.one_liner: Rewrite-based extensible compiler generates Harris kernels up to 16x over OpenCV, up to 1.4x over Halide on ARM
stencil.regime: single-pass Harris corner-detection image pipeline (Sobel gradients + structure tensor), fixed 2-image evaluation set, ARM mobile CPU, no time-stepping
stencil.centrality_rationale: Harris corner detection is a one-shot 2D image-filter pipeline, not the track's iterative T-time-step PDE stencil sweep; this paper is the sole subject of its own dedicated morphology-image-kernel track, so its assignment here looks like an over-generalization of 'neighborhood-weighted-sum operation' rather than a genuine PDE-stencil match.

stencil.title: YaskSite: Stencil Optimization Techniques Applied to Explicit ODE Methods on Modern Architectures
stencil.one_liner: YaskSite: ECM-model-guided stencil tuning for explicit ODE methods on Cascade Lake and Rome CPUs
stencil.regime: stencil kernels arising from explicit ODE-method discretizations, ECM-performance-model-guided autotuning, CPU (Cascade Lake/Rome); overlap with the named star/box catalog not confirmed
stencil.centrality_rationale: Headline is a stencil-optimization/performance-prediction tool built directly on Intel's YASK stencil framework, reporting measured gains from ECM-guided kernel selection -- matches variant 1's CPU general-compute class conceptually, but the specific ODE-derived shapes weren't confirmed against the named shape catalog.

stencil.title: High-Level FPGA Accelerator Design for Structured-Mesh-Based Explicit Numerical Solvers
stencil.one_liner: FPGA HLS design workflow with batching/tiling for structured-mesh explicit stencil solvers, near-GPU performance.
stencil.regime: Poisson-5pt/Jacobi-7pt/RTM-25pt stencils, fp32, Xilinx Alveo U280 FPGA, on-chip-capacity-limited grid sizes vs a V100 GPU energy/runtime comparison
stencil.centrality_rationale: Headline is entirely an FPGA stencil-accelerator design workflow, evaluated at kernel level (GB/s, runtime); explicitly named alongside AN5D/PERKS as informing variant 1's design and its rtm3d25p8th shape is folded into variant 1's own recommended_subset, but its own grid sizes (50^3-400^2) are far smaller than the CPU/GPU convention and the spec reports it separately by design.

stencil.title: Temporal blocking of finite-difference stencil operators with sparse "off-the-grid" sources
stencil.one_liner: Devito-generated temporal blocking for FD stencils with sparse off-the-grid sources, up to 1.6x over spatial blocking.
stencil.regime: 3D finite-difference wave-propagation stencils (isotropic/anisotropic acoustic, elastic), fp32, CPU (Broadwell/Skylake), CFL-determined iteration counts
stencil.centrality_rationale: Explicitly named as one of variant 1's defining papers ('Devito's generated code'); ablates temporal blocking against Devito's own spatially-blocked baseline at kernel level (GPoints/s).

stencil.title: K-Athena: A Performance Portable Structured Grid Finite Volume Magnetohydrodynamics Code
stencil.one_liner: K-Athena: Kokkos-ported MHD finite-volume stencil kernel, >10^8 cell-updates/s on V100, scales to 24576 GPUs
stencil.regime: structured-grid finite-volume MHD update (2nd-order box-shaped stencil support), fp64, single V100 reported plus CPU/multi-GPU scaling
stencil.centrality_rationale: Explicitly named as variant 1's defining example ('K-Athena's core update kernel'); reports a clean single-GPU cell-updates/s number (>10^8 on one V100) alongside its production-application framing.

stencil.title: Transformations of High-Level Synthesis Codes for High-Performance Computing
stencil.one_liner: Catalog of HLS source-to-source optimizing transformations for HPC kernels on FPGA.
stencil.regime: a general catalog of HLS source-to-source optimizing transformations demonstrated across several HPC kernels (GEMM, stencil among others), FPGA spatial architectures
stencil.centrality_rationale: This is a general transformation catalog, not a stencil-specific contribution -- stencil is one of several example kernels used to demonstrate the taxonomy, evaluated on FPGA rather than the CPU/GPU convention.

stencil.title: AN5D: automated stencil framework for high-degree temporal blocking on GPUs
stencil.one_liner: Stencil CUDA code generator with degree-10 temporal blocking; best reported perf on V100
stencil.regime: synthetic star/box 2D/3D stencils plus named application kernels, fp64 (fp32 secondary), single V100/P100, degree-10 temporal blocking
stencil.centrality_rationale: AN5D originates the star/box shape-naming convention the whole track reuses verbatim and is the primary defining paper for variant 1's protocol (400ms floor, 5 reps + discarded warmup).

stencil.title: Multi-node multi-GPU diffeomorphic image registration for large-scale imaging problems
stencil.one_liner: Multi-GPU CLAIRE: optimized interpolation/FD/FFT kernels + preconditioner for image registration.
stencil.regime: high-order finite-difference operators (interpolation/gradient/divergence) embedded in a Gauss-Newton-Krylov image-registration solver, fp64/fp32, multi-GPU with a single-V100 number reported
stencil.centrality_rationale: The FD stencil operators are one part of a larger nonlinear image-registration optimization pipeline (interpolation+FD+FFT+Krylov solve), not an isolated iterative PDE sweep; a genuine single-V100 256^3-in-5s number exists but the operators are single-application inside a much larger solver stack.

sssp.title: Traversing Large Compressed Graphs on GPUs
sssp.one_liner: Elias-Fano compressed graph format with GPU decompression enables BFS/SSSP/PageRank on larger graphs
sssp.regime: large real-world graphs compressed via Elias-Fano encoding (primarily unweighted for BFS); SSSP and PageRank are stated extensions, not the depth-evaluated algorithm
sssp.centrality_rationale: The paper's headline contribution is a GPU-decompressible graph compression format evaluated in depth via BFS; SSSP is explicitly an added extension ('we also extend our work to...'), so it is a downstream application of the compression kernel rather than the headline SSSP algorithm, and its base format targets unweighted graphs.

sssp.title: A fast work-efficient SSSP algorithm for GPUs
sssp.one_liner: Work-efficient GPU SSSP via novel approximate priority-queue work scheduler
sssp.regime: weighted directed graphs, GPU steady-state SSSP kernel, novel approximate priority-queue scheduler
sssp.centrality_rationale: Headline IS a GPU SSSP algorithm evaluated at kernel level against prior GPU SSSP work, exactly the spec's kernel-weighted-static variant.

sssp.title: Optimizing ordered graph algorithms with GraphIt
sssp.one_liner: GraphIt priority extension with bucket fusion generates ordered graph kernels up to 3x over Julienne/Galois/GAPBS
sssp.regime: standard graph benchmarks including road networks with large diameters, CPU, SSSP is one of six ordered graph algorithms generated by the DSL
sssp.centrality_rationale: GraphIt's priority/bucket-fusion extension is a DSL that generates and optimizes several ordered graph algorithms (SSSP among them); comparisons are against Julienne/Galois/GAPBS on the standard ordered-algorithm benchmark set.

morphology-image-kernel.title: Towards a Domain-Extensible Compiler: Optimizing an Image Processing Pipeline on Mobile CPUs
morphology-image-kernel.one_liner: Rewrite-based extensible compiler generates Harris kernels up to 16x over OpenCV, up to 1.4x over Halide on ARM
morphology-image-kernel.regime: Harris corner-response pipeline (grayscale->Sobel->structure tensor->response) on the artifact's own fixed 2-image evaluation set, mobile ARM CPU
morphology-image-kernel.centrality_rationale: This is the sole surveyed paper for this track, and the spec's variant is built entirely around its own confirmed protocol (30 timing iterations, median/min/max, the exact 2-image suite); headline is the domain-extensible rewrite-rule compiler generating this Harris kernel and comparing it to Halide/OpenCV.

moe-kernel.title: Hexcute: A Compiler Framework for Automating Layout Synthesis in GPU Programs
moe-kernel.one_liner: Hexcute auto-synthesizes GPU tensor layouts, matching cuBLAS/FlashAttention, 6.46x over Triton on MoE
moe-kernel.regime: mixed-type MoE grouped-GEMM operator (auto-synthesized GPU layouts) vs Triton; full token-routing/permute/gate-combine pipeline not detailed in the abstract
moe-kernel.centrality_rationale: Hexcute is a general layout-synthesis compiler evaluated across GEMM, FlashAttention, and MoE operators; MoE is one benchmarked operator class among several the compiler targets, matching the compiler/DSL 'generates this kernel among others' case, and the reported number appears to be the grouped-GEMM piece rather than the full routing+combine MoE FFN.

tensor-network.title: Bit-Slicing the Hilbert Space: Scaling Up Accurate Quantum Circuit Simulation
tensor-network.one_liner: Bit-sliced algebraic state encoding scales accurate quantum-circuit simulation to tens of thousands of qubits.
tensor-network.regime: exact-arithmetic scalability frontier under fixed time/memory budget (bit-sliced algebraic state encoding), tens of thousands of qubits, CPU
tensor-network.centrality_rationale: SliQSim is the paper this track's exact-arithmetic-scalability-frontier variant is built to isolate -- its claim is scaling accurate simulation, not steady-state gate-kernel throughput.

tensor-network.title: HyQuas: hybrid partitioner based quantum circuit simulation system on GPU
tensor-network.one_liner: HyQuas: hybrid-partitioner GPU quantum circuit simulation improving data locality per circuit pattern
tensor-network.regime: gate-by-gate state-vector quantum circuit simulation, hybrid partitioner selecting per circuit pattern, GPU
tensor-network.centrality_rationale: HyQuas is explicitly named in the spec's state-vector/density-matrix gate-kernel variant as one of the four exemplar systems.

tensor-network.title: Closing the "quantum supremacy" gap: achieving real-time simulation of a random quantum circuit using a new Sunway supercomputer
tensor-network.one_liner: Sunway tensor-contraction random-quantum-circuit simulator: fused permute-multiply, 1.2 Eflop/s
tensor-network.regime: random-quantum-circuit tensor-network contraction via slicing + path search, Sunway 42M-core distributed, mixed/single precision
tensor-network.centrality_rationale: SWQsim is the sole exemplar of the spec's rqc-tensor-network-contraction variant, a structurally distinct paradigm (contraction, not gate propagation) from the fp64 state-vector/density-matrix variant, and runs on Sunway (no NVIDIA GPU).

tensor-network.title: SV-sim: scalable PGAS-based state vector simulation of quantum circuits
tensor-network.one_liner: SV-Sim: PGAS-based state-vector quantum-circuit simulation kernels across heterogeneous CPU/GPU backends
tensor-network.regime: gate-by-gate state-vector propagation, PGAS communication model across heterogeneous CPU/GPU backends (NVIDIA/AMD GPUs, multiple CPU vendors)
tensor-network.centrality_rationale: SV-Sim is explicitly named in the spec's state-vector/density-matrix gate-kernel variant; it includes an NVIDIA-GPU backend usable as a single-card kernel path.

tensor-network.title: Density matrix quantum circuit simulation via the BSP machine on modern GPU clusters
tensor-network.one_liner: Multi-GPU BSP density-matrix quantum circuit simulator (DM-Sim), 10x faster than prior sims.
tensor-network.regime: gate-by-gate density-matrix propagation, multi-GPU BSP communication scheme across GPU clusters (DGX-1/DGX-2/Summit)
tensor-network.centrality_rationale: DM-Sim is named in the spec's gate-kernel variant and the underlying gate operation matches, but the paper's own contribution and all reported speedups are about the multi-GPU BSP communication methodology (MG-BSP) rather than a single-card kernel path.

pagerank.title: Traversing Large Compressed Graphs on GPUs
pagerank.one_liner: Elias-Fano compressed graph format with GPU decompression enables BFS/SSSP/PageRank on larger graphs
pagerank.regime: global PageRank (fixed 50-iter cap) on large real web/social graphs (soc-LiveJournal1/orkut/twitter/uk-2007/etc.)
pagerank.centrality_rationale: PageRank is one of four kernels (BFS/SSSP/PageRank/Elias-Fano compression) this Elias-Fano compressed-graph-traversal paper demonstrates; its graph suite is one of only two sources the spec's global-PageRank suite is built from, but the artifact ships BFS-only code with zero PageRank source recoverable to reproduce its own numbers.

pagerank.title: Workload Balancing via Graph Reordering on Multicore Systems
pagerank.one_liner: Corder: cache-aware graph reordering balancing multicore workload, up to 2.59x speedup.
pagerank.regime: PageRank as one target kernel of a cache-aware graph-reordering technique (1-iteration + 20-iteration profiling), large real graphs
pagerank.centrality_rationale: Corder's headline contribution is graph reordering, evaluated across PageRank (and BFS) as target kernels; it is the direct model for the spec's pagerank-e2e-reorder variant (its own 'N iterations of PR to amortize' argument is operationalized as a first-class metric there).

pagerank.title: MELOPPR: Software/Hardware Co-design for Memory-efficient Low-latency Personalized PageRank
pagerank.one_liner: Stage/linear-decomposed personalized PageRank on CPU+FPGA; up to 707x speedup at ~80-90% precision.
pagerank.regime: Personalized (single-source, depth-truncated) PageRank on CPU+FPGA, top-k set-overlap correctness, small graphs
pagerank.centrality_rationale: MELOPPR solves Personalized, not global, PageRank — a different-enough problem (single-source, depth-truncated, top-k-set correctness notion, different damping factor) that the spec's own open_questions flag it as warranting a separate track rather than being folded into this one's variants.

pagerank.title: Practical parallel hypergraph algorithms
pagerank.one_liner: Efficient parallel hypergraph algorithm suite built on extended Ligra framework
pagerank.regime: PageRank generalized to hypergraphs (bipartite vertex/hyperedge propagation), 1-iteration timing, one algorithm among a general hypergraph suite
pagerank.centrality_rationale: PageRank is one of several algorithms (betweenness centrality, k-core, SSSP, PageRank) in a general parallel hypergraph-algorithm framework, and the spec's own evidence entry states this is hypergraph PageRank, 'not plain-graph PageRank,' the operation this track's variants actually measure.

topk-selection.title: UpANNS: Enhancing Billion-Scale ANNS Efficiency with Real-World PIM Architecture
topk-selection.one_liner: PIM-accelerated billion-scale ANNS with data placement and early-pruning top-k, 4.3x QPS vs Faiss
topk-selection.centrality_rationale: UpANNS's early-pruning top-k selection is one of four innovations inside a larger PIM-based ANNS system, evaluated end-to-end (QPS); still the explicit, sole basis for the topk-e2e-ann-approx variant. Platform is UPMEM PIM, not a GPU.

topk-selection.title: Parallel Top-K Algorithms on GPU: A Comprehensive Study and New Methods
topk-selection.one_liner: AIR Top-K/GridSelect: adaptive iteration-fused GPU top-K, up to 574x over prior radix top-K
topk-selection.regime: exact top-k of a GPU-resident array, synthetic distributions, batch sweep
