topk-selection.centrality_rationale: AIR Top-K/GridSelect's headline IS GPU top-k selection algorithms, explicitly and repeatedly named as 'the most systematically-swept paper in this track' and the direct basis for the topk-array-kernel-exact variant.

topk-selection.title: Scaling up HBM Efficiency of Top-K SpMV for Approximate Embedding Similarity on FPGAs
topk-selection.one_liner: Top-K SpMV on HBM FPGA with packet-wise CSR compression and reduced precision; 100x vs CPU, 2x vs GPU.
topk-selection.regime: reduced-precision-score Top-K SpMV for embedding similarity, FPGA
topk-selection.centrality_rationale: Top-K SpMV's headline IS a Top-K SpMV FPGA kernel, explicitly the sole named basis for the topk-approx-precision variant (same synthetic sweep and GloVe dataset). FPGA only.

graph-partitioning.title: Tera-Scale Multilevel Graph Partitioning
graph-partitioning.one_liner: TeraPart: memory-efficient parallel multilevel graph partitioning, partitions trillion-edge graphs in minutes
graph-partitioning.regime: trillion-edge web/synthetic graphs, large k, CPU/distributed
graph-partitioning.centrality_rationale: TeraPart's own operating point and headline 16x peak-memory reduction directly define the spec's gp-kernel-large-k and gp-memory-scaling variants.

graph-partitioning.title: G-kway: Multilevel GPU-Accelerated k-way Graph Partitioner
graph-partitioning.one_liner: G-kway: multilevel GPU k-way graph partitioner, 8.6x/3.8x faster than CPU/GPU baselines
graph-partitioning.regime: DIMACS10-scale graphs, small power-of-2 k, GPU
graph-partitioning.centrality_rationale: G-kway's own operating point directly defines the spec's gp-kernel-small-k variant.

other:spectral-sparsification.title: inGRASS: Incremental Graph Spectral Sparsification via Low-Resistance-Diameter Decomposition
other:spectral-sparsification.one_liner: Nearly-linear-time parallel-friendly incremental graph spectral sparsification algorithm
other:spectral-sparsification.regime: incremental spectral sparsification, SuiteSparse Laplacian-derived graphs, CPU
other:spectral-sparsification.centrality_rationale: inGRASS's headline IS the incremental spectral-sparsification algorithm itself (LRD decomposition + resistance-embedding updates), the sole and direct basis for both variants, matching the paper's own 200x speedup claim. CPU only.

lossy-compression.title: FFCz: Fast Fourier Correction for Spectrum-Preserving Lossy Compression of Scientific Data
lossy-compression.one_liner: FFCz: GPU-accelerated FFT-based error correction preserves both spatial and frequency accuracy in lossy compression.
lossy-compression.regime: GPU FFT-based spectral error-correction layered atop off-the-shelf base compressors (SZ3/ZFP/SPERR); cosmology/X-ray/combustion/EEG grids
lossy-compression.centrality_rationale: Headline is a post-hoc spectral-domain error-correction algorithm applied on top of an existing compressor's output, not a standalone Compress(D,eb) implementation; domains (cosmology, combustion) partially overlap SDRBench but the correction-only operation isn't directly comparable to fixed-EB throughput/ratio.

lossy-compression.title: PackKV: Reducing KV Cache Memory Footprint through LLM-Aware Lossy Compression
lossy-compression.one_liner: LLM-aware lossy KV-cache compression that also accelerates matrix-vector multiply vs cuBLAS
lossy-compression.regime: LLM KV-cache tensors (attention K/V), lossy compression co-designed with system architecture, evaluated via memory-reduction rate and throughput vs cuBLAS GEMV kernels
lossy-compression.centrality_rationale: PackKV's compression is co-designed with a KV-cache management system and its headline numbers (memory-reduction %, throughput vs cuBLAS GEMV) are end-to-end system metrics on LLM KV-cache data, a different regime from SDRBench-style scientific floating-point fields.

lossy-compression.title: IPComp: Interpolation Based Progressive Lossy Compression for Scientific Applications
lossy-compression.one_liner: Interpolation-based progressive lossy compressor, up to 487% higher ratio and 698% faster
lossy-compression.regime: interpolation-based SZ-family error-bounded compression, real-world scientific datasets, progressive/bitplane retrieval, CPU
lossy-compression.centrality_rationale: IPComp's headline is an interpolation-based error-bounded lossy compressor (same SZ-family predictor class), evaluated by compression ratio/speed against SOTA progressive compressors on real scientific datasets; CPU only.

lossy-compression.title: Enhanced JPEG Decoding Using PIM Architectures with Parallel MCU Processing
lossy-compression.one_liner: NPD: PIM-based (UPMEM) parallel JPEG decoder exploiting multi-DPU MCU-level parallelism.
lossy-compression.regime: JPEG image decoding on UPMEM PIM hardware; fixed-quantization image codec, not error-bounded scientific floating-point compression
lossy-compression.centrality_rationale: NPD's headline is a full JPEG decoder (a lossy-compression kernel family member) evaluated at kernel level against a prior PIM decoder, but the codec (DCT+quantization, integer images) and platform (UPMEM PIM, no GPU) are entirely different from the spec's error-bounded fp32/fp64 SDRBench regime.

lossy-compression.title: Fast and Effective Lossy Compression on GPUs and CPUs with Guaranteed Error Bounds
lossy-compression.one_liner: PFPL: error-bounded lossy compressor, CPU/GPU-portable, highest throughput and ratio vs 7 compressors
lossy-compression.regime: SDRBench inputs, fp32/fp64, CPU+GPU-portable error-bounded compression
lossy-compression.centrality_rationale: PFPL is a headline error-bounded lossy compressor evaluated directly on SDRBench inputs with compression ratio/throughput against 7 competing compressors on both CPU and GPU; explicitly named in the spec as an SZ-family denominator paper.

lossy-compression.title: GPU Lossy Compression for HPC Can Be Versatile and Ultra-Fast
lossy-compression.one_liner: Versatile ultra-fast GPU lossy compression kernel (VGC) with memory-efficient and selective-decompress modes
lossy-compression.regime: SDRBench-class scientific data, GPU single-kernel fused compression, versatile modes
lossy-compression.centrality_rationale: VGC/cuSZp's headline is the GPU error-bounded lossy compression kernel itself, matching the spec's GPU dual-scope variant directly.

lossy-compression.title: lsCOMP: Efficient Light Source Compression
lossy-compression.one_liner: Single-kernel GPU compressor for light-source X-ray data, up to 509 GB/s, 20x faster than SOTA GPU compressors
lossy-compression.regime: light-source/X-ray detector integer data (uint16/uint32), quantization-bin + selective-pooling lossy knobs, no abs/rel error bound
lossy-compression.centrality_rationale: lsCOMP's headline is a single-kernel GPU compressor, but survey.md flags its integer (not fp32/fp64) light-source data and non-error-bound lossy knobs as a genuine divergence explicitly scoped out of the track's core error-bound variants.

lossy-compression.title: TAC+: Optimizing Error-Bounded Lossy Compression for 3D AMR Simulations
lossy-compression.one_liner: TAC+: high-dimensional SZ-based error-bounded lossy compression optimized for 3D AMR data
lossy-compression.regime: 3D AMR simulation data, SZ-based per-refinement-level compression, CPU, fp32/fp64
lossy-compression.centrality_rationale: TAC+ is explicitly named in the spec's own kernel-cpu-ebound variant as one of the SZ-family denominator papers this track is built around.

lossy-compression.title: FZ-GPU: A Fast and High-Ratio Lossy Compressor for Scientific Computing Applications on GPUs
lossy-compression.one_liner: FZ-GPU fused GPU lossy compressor, 4.2x over cuSZ and 2.3x over cuZFP
lossy-compression.regime: SDRBench (6 datasets), GPU fused quantization+bitshuffle+encoding
lossy-compression.centrality_rationale: FZ-GPU is explicitly named/used to help define the spec's SDRBench dataset selection and GPU dual-scope variant.

lossy-compression.title: FAZ: A flexible auto-tuned modular error-bounded compression framework for scientific data
lossy-compression.one_liner: Adaptive auto-tuned modular error-bounded lossy compression framework
lossy-compression.regime: real-world scientific applications, SZ-family adaptive/auto-tuned framework, CPU
lossy-compression.centrality_rationale: FAZ is explicitly named as one of the SZ-family denominator papers anchoring the spec's CPU error-bound variant.

lossy-compression.title: Lossy Scientific Data Compression With SPERR
lossy-compression.one_liner: SPERR: SPECK-wavelet-based lossy scientific data compressor with parallel and point-wise-error modes
lossy-compression.regime: SDRBench-class structured scientific data, wavelet/SPECK rate-distortion + point-wise error mode, CPU
lossy-compression.centrality_rationale: SPERR is explicitly the rate-target anchor named in the spec's rate-distortion variant.

lossy-compression.title: ZFP-X: Efficient Embedded Coding for Accelerating Lossy Floating Point Compression
lossy-compression.one_liner: Bit-group embedded coding backend for ZFP boosts (de)compression throughput up to 2.5x
lossy-compression.regime: real-world scientific simulation datasets, ZFP embedded-coding backend, CPU
lossy-compression.centrality_rationale: ZFP-X's headline is a new embedded-coding backend directly measured as compression/decompression throughput against baseline ZFP on scientific datasets.

lossy-compression.title: cuSZp: An Ultra-fast GPU Error-bounded Lossy Compression Framework with Optimized End-to-End Performance
lossy-compression.one_liner: cuSZp: single-kernel fused GPU lossy compressor, 95.5x faster end-to-end than cuSZ
lossy-compression.regime: SDRBench scientific data (6 datasets), GPU single-fused-kernel compression
lossy-compression.centrality_rationale: cuSZp is explicitly the anchor paper for the spec's fused-single-kernel 'end-to-end' sense in the GPU dual-scope variant.

lossy-compression.title: TAC: Optimizing Error-Bounded Lossy Compression for Three-Dimensional Adaptive Mesh Refinement Simulations
lossy-compression.one_liner: Dimension-aware error-bounded lossy compression for 3D AMR data, up to 3.3x better ratio
lossy-compression.regime: 3D AMR simulation data, high-dimensional SZ compression per refinement level, CPU
lossy-compression.centrality_rationale: TAC (predecessor of TAC+) is explicitly named as an SZ-family denominator paper the CPU error-bound variant is built around.

lossy-compression.title: CEAZ: accelerating parallel I/O via hardware-algorithm co-designed adaptive lossy compression
lossy-compression.one_liner: CEAZ: FPGA SZ-family adaptive lossy compression, 2.3x throughput / 3x ratio over prior FPGA compressor
lossy-compression.regime: real-world scientific datasets, SZ-family adaptive lossy compression on FPGA
lossy-compression.centrality_rationale: CEAZ's headline is a full FPGA-based error-bounded compressor evaluated with compression ratio/throughput against a prior FPGA compressor; FPGA-only, not GPU.

lossy-compression.title: Optimizing Huffman Decoding for Error-Bounded Lossy Compression on GPUs
lossy-compression.one_liner: GPU Huffman decoder optimizations speed up cuSZ decompression by 2.43x on average
lossy-compression.regime: cuSZ's standard scientific datasets, GPU Huffman-decoding sub-stage of the compression pipeline
lossy-compression.centrality_rationale: The paper optimizes only cuSZ's internal Huffman-decoding sub-stage of the lossless-encoding step, not the full compress/decompress operation the spec measures.

lossy-compression.title: Dynamic Quality Metric Oriented Error Bounded Lossy Compression for Scientific Datasets
lossy-compression.one_liner: QoZ: dynamic quality-metric-oriented error-bounded lossy compressor, up to 270% ratio gain vs SOTA
lossy-compression.regime: real-world scientific application datasets, SZ-based interpolation predictor, dynamic quality-metric tuning, CPU
lossy-compression.centrality_rationale: QoZ is explicitly named as an SZ-family denominator paper anchoring the CPU error-bound variant.

lossy-compression.title: Accelerating Multigrid-based Hierarchical Scientific Data Refactoring on GPUs
lossy-compression.one_liner: GPU multigrid-based hierarchical data-refactoring kernels for MGARD, 250TB/s (83% peak) on Summit
lossy-compression.regime: large-scale scientific simulation/visualization data, GPU multigrid data-refactoring throughput (not compress-at-EB throughput/ratio)
lossy-compression.centrality_rationale: The paper optimizes MGARD's multigrid data-decomposition/refactoring kernel, a preprocessing stage feeding MGARD's lossy compression, not the compress(D,eb)->C operation itself.

lossy-compression.title: Error-controlled, progressive, and adaptable retrieval of scientific data with multilevel decomposition
lossy-compression.one_liner: Multilevel error-bounded data refactoring/retrieval framework, 64% less data retrieved
lossy-compression.regime: large-scale scientific simulation data, multilevel progressive decomposition/retrieval built on MGARD, CPU+distributed
lossy-compression.centrality_rationale: Headline is a progressive retrieval/decomposition framework built atop MGARD's multilevel decomposition, evaluated by data-retrieved-volume and I/O time, not standalone compress/decompress-at-EB throughput; CPU-only, no GPU.

lossy-compression.title: Significantly Improving Lossy Compression for HPC Datasets with Second-Order Prediction and Parameter Optimization
lossy-compression.one_liner: 2nd-order prediction + parameter optimization boosting SZ compression ratio up to 46%
lossy-compression.regime: large-scale HPC simulation datasets, SZ 2nd-order prediction + parameter optimization, CPU/distributed
lossy-compression.centrality_rationale: Headline is an SZ-family compression-ratio improvement (2nd-order prediction), evaluated directly by compression ratio and parallel I/O throughput on real HPC datasets; CPU only.

sparse-format-conversion.title: LiteForm: Lightweight and Automatic Format Composition for Sparse Matrix-Matrix Multiplication on GPUs
sparse-format-conversion.one_liner: Automatic composable sparse-format (CELL) selection for GPU SpMM, 2.06x over cuSPARSE
sparse-format-conversion.regime: automatic composable sparse-format (CELL) selection + conversion for GPU SpMM, real GNN adjacency matrices (cora/citeseer/pubmed/ppi/arxiv/proteins/reddit), single NVIDIA GPU
sparse-format-conversion.centrality_rationale: LiteForm is the sole and literal basis for both spec variants (its own driver scripts and matrix names are reused verbatim); headline is format selection/conversion itself, evaluated as both a standalone conversion number and an amortized end-to-end SpMM pipeline.

embedding-ops.title: cuKE: An Efficient Code Generator for Score Function Computation in Knowledge Graph Embedding
embedding-ops.one_liner: cuKE: code generator fusing KGE score-function tensor ops into CUDA, 14.9x over TorchScript.
embedding-ops.regime: KGE score-function fused tensor ops (TransE/TransH/TransR/TransF/RESCAL family), single NVIDIA GPU
embedding-ops.centrality_rationale: cuKE's own evaluated score functions are exactly the spec's embed-single-index-gather recommended_subset; headline is a code generator fusing these score-function tensor ops.

embedding-ops.title: RecFlex: Enabling Feature Heterogeneity-Aware Optimization for Deep Recommendation Models with Flexible Schedules
embedding-ops.one_liner: RecFlex: per-field schedule tuning + fusion compiler for recsys embedding kernels, up to 20.8x
embedding-ops.regime: fused per-field embedding-operator kernels for DLRM-style recsys at MLPerf/EL-Rec-scale table configs, single NVIDIA GPU
embedding-ops.centrality_rationale: RecFlex's own table configs and end-to-end sampling convention (sample_batch_nums default) are named directly as the basis for the spec's embed-dlrm-pooled-kernel-f32 and embed-dlrm-e2e-preproc variants.

embedding-ops.title: EL-Rec: Efficient Large-Scale Recommendation Model Training via Tensor-Train Embedding Table
embedding-ops.one_liner: Tensor-train compressed embedding-table kernel (PyTorch drop-in) speeds DLRM training 3x on 1 GPU
embedding-ops.regime: Tensor-Train (TT) factorized/compressed embedding-table lookup for DLRM training, single GPU
embedding-ops.centrality_rationale: EL-Rec's headline contribution is a TT-decomposed compressed embedding table (a structurally different, factorized representation reconstructed via small tensor contractions), not the plain dense/uncompressed table gather+pool or single-index lookup either named variant assumes.

embedding-ops.title: FULL-W2V: fully exploiting data reuse for W2V on GPU-accelerated systems
embedding-ops.one_liner: FULL-W2V: GPU Word2Vec exploiting data reuse, 5.72x over prior GPU state-of-the-art
embedding-ops.regime: Word2Vec single-index embedding gather plus fused elementwise update with data-reuse optimization, single NVIDIA GPU (P100/V100)
embedding-ops.centrality_rationale: The spec's embed-single-index-gather variant explicitly names this paper's style ('KGE and word-embedding workloads (cuKE, FULL-W2V style)') as its defining shape.

kcore-kclique.title: Root-Down Exposure for Maximal Clique Enumeration on GPUs
kcore-kclique.one_liner: RDMCE: root-down exposure load balancing for GPU maximal clique enumeration, up to 5.4x
kcore-kclique.regime: maximal clique enumeration on large real graphs (up to 146B cliques), GPU
kcore-kclique.centrality_rationale: RDMCE's headline IS a GPU MCE algorithm/kernel, explicitly and by name the basis for the mce-enum variant, including its own SNAP/nrvis/KONECT graph suite.

kcore-kclique.title: Parallel k-Core Decomposition with Batched Updates and Asynchronous Reads
kcore-kclique.one_liner: Concurrent-parallel dynamic k-core decomposition data structure with async reads amid batched updates
kcore-kclique.regime: batch-dynamic k-core maintenance under streamed edge updates, CPU
kcore-kclique.centrality_rationale: LiuSZ24's headline IS a parallel batch-dynamic k-core decomposition data structure, explicitly and repeatedly named as the source for the kcore-dynamic-batch variant (its own dynamic graph streams and batch sizes). CPU only.

kcore-kclique.title: Parallel K-clique counting on GPUs
kcore-kclique.one_liner: Parallel k-clique counting kernel on GPUs
kcore-kclique.regime: exact k-clique counting on GPU, SNAP graphs
kcore-kclique.centrality_rationale: KCGPU's headline IS a parallel GPU k-clique-counting kernel, explicitly the basis for the kclique-count-exact variant (its own Table 1 graph set).

kcore-kclique.title: ProbGraph: High-Performance and High-Accuracy Graph Mining with Probabilistic Set Representations
kcore-kclique.one_liner: ProbGraph: Bloom-filter probabilistic set representations accelerate graph mining up to 50x
kcore-kclique.centrality_rationale: ProbGraph's headline IS Bloom-filter probabilistic set representations applied to clique counting and clustering, explicitly the basis for the kclique-count-approx variant (its own Table VIII graph suite). CPU only.

kcore-kclique.title: Practical parallel hypergraph algorithms
kcore-kclique.one_liner: Efficient parallel hypergraph algorithm suite built on extended Ligra framework
kcore-kclique.regime: hypergraph (bipartite vertex-hyperedge) algorithms, k-core one of ~8 algorithms covered
kcore-kclique.centrality_rationale: The spec itself explicitly excludes this paper's hypergraph inputs as a structurally different data model (bipartite incidence, not a plain adjacency list); k-core is only one of eight algorithms (betweenness, PageRank, SSSP, etc.) in a general hypergraph-processing framework, not a dedicated k-core/k-clique contribution.

dp-dynamic-programming.title: Fast All-Pairs Shortest Paths Algorithm in Large Sparse Graph
dp-dynamic-programming.one_liner: Distributed-GPU Floyd+Dijkstra all-pairs shortest paths for sparse graphs
dp-dynamic-programming.regime: large sparse real-world graphs, hybrid Floyd-Warshall+Dijkstra APSP, distributed multi-GPU
dp-dynamic-programming.centrality_rationale: This is the sole paper the dp-dynamic-programming spec was built around -- its Floyd+Dijkstra hybrid, METIS partitioning, and distributed-GPU framework match the spec verbatim. Hardest call on gpu_single_card: the paper's core novelty is resolving a GPU-count-vs-block-count mismatch, i.e. it is designed around multi-GPU scaling (headline result: 2048 GPUs), though a single-GPU/single-partition degenerate case likely runs.

multigrid.title: AmgT: Algebraic Multigrid Solver on Tensor Cores
multigrid.one_liner: AmgT: tensor-core/mixed-precision SpGEMM+SpMV kernels for AMG setup/solve, up to 2.2x over HYPRE
multigrid.regime: tensor-core/mixed-precision SpGEMM (setup phase) + SpMV (solve phase) AMG kernels incorporated into HYPRE, single A100/H100/MI210
multigrid.centrality_rationale: AmgT's own `t_start/t_stop` setup/solve split is quoted directly as the basis for the spec's mg-gpu-setup-kernel-f64 and mg-gpu-solve-kernel-fixed-iter variants; this is the origin paper for both.

multigrid.title: Optimizing Multi-grid Computation and Parallelization on Multi-cores
multigrid.one_liner: Optimized SYMGS/multigrid parallelization on multicore CPUs (HPCG)
multigrid.regime: HPCG-style geometric-multigrid SYMGS+MG on structured grids with no separate algebraic setup phase, CPU (ARMv8 and x86)
multigrid.centrality_rationale: MGopt-APP's exact evaluation shape (HPCG integration, 192^3 grid) is named directly as the spec's mg-cpu-geometric-symgs variant's basis; headline is SYMGS/MG parallelization itself, evaluated against vendor/engineer-tuned implementations.

multigrid.title: Harnessing the Crowd for Autotuning High-Performance Computing Applications
multigrid.one_liner: Crowd-sourced transfer-learning autotuner (GPTuneCrowd) speeds PDGEQRF, SuperLU_DIST, Hypre tuning
multigrid.regime: crowd-sourced transfer-learning autotuner reducing Hypre AMG's tuning search space, alongside two unrelated tuning targets (ScaLAPACK PDGEQRF, SuperLU_DIST), distributed/CPU
multigrid.centrality_rationale: GPTuneCrowd only tunes existing runtime knobs of the pre-built HYPRE library as one of three unrelated case studies; it does not implement or modify the multigrid setup/solve kernels themselves, so the assignment reads as a tuning-target mention rather than genuine multigrid-kernel work.

multigrid.title: A Multi-GPU Aggregation-Based AMG Preconditioner for Iterative Linear Solvers
multigrid.one_liner: Multi-GPU MPI-CUDA AMG-preconditioned Krylov solver (BootCMatchG), up to 2x over Nvidia AmgX.
multigrid.regime: AMG-preconditioned Krylov solver on synthetic 3D-Laplacian stencil SPD systems, weak/strong scaling including a rank=1 single-GPU point, multi-GPU MPI-CUDA
multigrid.centrality_rationale: BootCMatchGX's AMG setup+solve on both 7-point and 27-point Laplacian stencils is the explicit basis for the spec's distributed/weak-scaling framing in this track as well as cg-krylov.

multigrid.title: Accelerating Multigrid-based Hierarchical Scientific Data Refactoring on GPUs
multigrid.one_liner: GPU multigrid-based hierarchical data-refactoring kernels for MGARD, 250TB/s (83% peak) on Summit
multigrid.regime: multigrid-inspired hierarchical multiresolution decomposition used purely for lossy scientific-data compression on GPU, not an algebraic/geometric-multigrid solve of Ax=b
multigrid.centrality_rationale: MGARD's 'multigrid' is a hierarchical decomposition/refactoring transform for a compression codec (a literal instance of the 'component' definition's own compression-codec example, but here so far removed from the actual operation -- no SpGEMM coarsening, no V-cycle smoothing+SpMV solve -- that the fundamental operation doesn't match the track's Ax=b solver definition at all); GPU-kernel-centric work makes a single-GPU path plausible though not explicitly confirmed.

cg-krylov.title: Accelerating Sparse Linear Solvers on Intelligence Processing Units
cg-krylov.one_liner: DSL-generated sparse linear solvers (SpMV/ILU/PBiCGStab) on Graphcore IPUs, up to 150x vs CPU/GPU.
cg-krylov.regime: DSL-generated SpMV/ILU/PBiCGStab sparse solvers on Graphcore IPUs, SuiteSparse plus synthetic Poisson matrices, MPIR+double-word arithmetic for missing native fp64
cg-krylov.centrality_rationale: Graphene is a general DSL/codegen framework generating a suite of linear solvers/preconditioners (SpMV, ILU, PBiCGStab), not a CG implementation; the spec explicitly excludes nonsymmetric/BiCGStab-type solves as out of scope for this CG-specific track, and the platform (IPU) is outside the benchmark's NVIDIA-GPU scope.

cg-krylov.title: A Nested Krylov Method Using Half-Precision Arithmetic
cg-krylov.one_liner: Nested FGMRES/Richardson Krylov solver exploiting fp16 inner iterations, up to 2.42x speedup
cg-krylov.regime: nested FGMRES/Richardson Krylov solver with fp16 inner iterations, to-convergence solve on symmetric/SPD matrices overlapping the recommended subset, CPU
cg-krylov.centrality_rationale: F3R is one of the two papers the spec's cg-mixed-precision-cascade variant is explicitly built around ('F3R's own symmetric list already overlaps heavily with' the recommended subset); headline is the reduced-precision-cascade solver itself, evaluated to convergence.

cg-krylov.title: Sparsified Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient Solver on GPUs
cg-krylov.one_liner: Sparsified ILU-preconditioned CG solver increases GPU parallelism, up to 3.73x end-to-end speedup
cg-krylov.regime: ILU(0)/ILU(K)-preconditioned CG on SPD SuiteSparse matrices, both iterative-phase and end-to-end speedups with preconditioner setup measured and reported separately, single A100
cg-krylov.centrality_rationale: SPCG's own artifact discipline (separating preconditioner analysis+factorization from the PCG loop) is generalized directly into the spec's cg-e2e-ilu0-to-convergence variant as a mandatory requirement.

cg-krylov.title: Mille-feuille: A Tile-Grained Mixed Precision Single-Kernel Conjugate Gradient Solver on GPUs
cg-krylov.one_liner: Mille-feuille: tile-grained mixed-precision single-kernel CG/BiCGSTAB solver, up to 3-5x over cuSPARSE
cg-krylov.regime: tile-grained mixed-precision single-kernel CG/PCG/BiCGSTAB/PBiCGSTAB solver, single A100 and single MI210
cg-krylov.centrality_rationale: Mille-feuille is explicitly named as one of the two papers ('the two papers in this track that build reduced-precision Krylov solvers as their central contribution') the cg-mixed-precision-cascade variant targets.

cg-krylov.title: PERKS: a Locality-Optimized Execution Model for Iterative Memory-bound GPU Applications
cg-krylov.one_liner: Persistent-kernel locality optimization for iterative stencil/CG GPU kernels
cg-krylov.regime: unpreconditioned CG kernel (SpMV + 2 dots + 3 axpys), SuiteSparse matrices (smaller and larger sets), single NVIDIA GPU, persistent-kernel execution model
cg-krylov.centrality_rationale: PERKS's own CG research question is quoted verbatim as the spec's cg-kernel-fixed-iter variant's defining claim ('matching PERKS's explicit research question').

cg-krylov.title: A Multi-GPU Aggregation-Based AMG Preconditioner for Iterative Linear Solvers
cg-krylov.one_liner: Multi-GPU MPI-CUDA AMG-preconditioned Krylov solver (BootCMatchG), up to 2x over Nvidia AmgX.
cg-krylov.regime: AMG-preconditioned Krylov solver on synthetic 3D-Laplacian stencil SPD systems, weak/strong scaling including a rank=1 single-GPU starting point, multi-GPU MPI-CUDA
cg-krylov.centrality_rationale: BootCMatchGX's own `--laplacian-3d` generator and convergence protocol (relative residual < 1e-6, capped 1000 iterations) is quoted verbatim as the spec's cg-hpcg-generator-amg and cg-e2e-ilu0-to-convergence variants' basis; its own weak-scaling series starts at rank count 1, giving a genuine single-GPU data point.

cg-krylov.title: Multi-node multi-GPU diffeomorphic image registration for large-scale imaging problems
cg-krylov.one_liner: Multi-GPU CLAIRE: optimized interpolation/FD/FFT kernels + preconditioner for image registration.
cg-krylov.regime: Gauss-Newton-Krylov solve embedded in a nonlinear diffeomorphic image-registration pipeline, single-V100 number reported alongside multi-GPU scaling, not a standalone SPD test-matrix solve
cg-krylov.centrality_rationale: The Krylov solve here is the inner linear-system step of an outer nonlinear Gauss-Newton optimization for image registration (a solver stack), not a direct CG-on-SPD-matrix claim comparable to the spec's SuiteSparse/HPCG-generator regime.

batched-gemm.title: FASTEN: Fast GPU-accelerated Segmented Matrix Multiplication for Heterogenous Graph Neural Networks
batched-gemm.one_liner: Autotuned GPU segmented matrix multiplication for heterogeneous GNNs
batched-gemm.regime: variable-shape/segmented GEMM on 8 real heterogeneous-graph relation-type distributions, NVIDIA GPU
batched-gemm.centrality_rationale: FASTEN's headline IS the segmented-GEMM kernel, matching the spec's batched-gemm-variable-kernel variant exactly, but the spec notes its own uniform-shape variant is 'not directly evidenced by FASTEN's own artifact.'

bfs.title: BLEST: Blazingly Efficient BFS using Tensor Cores
bfs.one_liner: Tensor-Core accelerated pull-based BFS via bitmap SpMSpV, 3.6-4.9x over Gunrock/GSWITCH
bfs.regime: real-world graphs, GPU tensor-core-accelerated pull-based BFS, vs Gunrock/GSWITCH/BerryBees
bfs.centrality_rationale: BLEST's headline IS a BFS algorithm/implementation evaluated directly against BFS baselines on real-world graphs.

bfs.title: FuseIM: Fusing Probabilistic Traversals for Influence Maximization on Exascale Systems
bfs.one_liner: Fused probabilistic BFS traversals for influence maximization, up to 360x on Frontier
bfs.regime: probabilistic (stochastic edge-weighted) breadth-first traversals for influence-maximization Monte-Carlo sampling, AMD GPU + distributed (Frontier)
bfs.centrality_rationale: Per survey.md, this is 'not a plain-BFS paper' -- probabilistic traversal is a materially different kernel from deterministic reachability BFS, embedded as the sampling step of an influence-maximization application; platform is AMD GPU/distributed, not a single NVIDIA GPU.

bfs.title: Doubling Graph Traversal Efficiency to 198 TeraTEPS on the Supercomputer Fugaku
bfs.one_liner: Pruning/reordering/bitmap-compression BFS techniques hit 198 TeraTEPS on Fugaku
bfs.regime: Graph500 R-MAT/Kronecker graphs, distributed BFS at Fugaku-class SCALE, ARM CPU
bfs.centrality_rationale: Headline IS Graph500-benchmark BFS performance; the spec explicitly notes SCALE>=38 Fugaku-class as reportable. No GPU (ARM CPU, distributed).

bfs.title: Traversing Large Compressed Graphs on GPUs
bfs.one_liner: Elias-Fano compressed graph format with GPU decompression enables BFS/SSSP/PageRank on larger graphs
bfs.regime: Elias-Fano compressed real-world graphs on GPU; BFS is one of three downstream applications (BFS/SSSP/PageRank) of a novel compression format
bfs.centrality_rationale: Headline contribution is the graph-compression format; BFS is one of three applications used to demonstrate its benefit rather than the paper's own optimized kernel.

bfs.title: Bit-GraphBLAS: Bit-Level Optimizations of Matrix-Centric Graph Processing on GPU
bfs.one_liner: Bit-Block CSR (B2SR) format; bit-level GraphBLAS SpMV/SpGEMM sped up to 6555x on GPU
bfs.regime: bit-level B2SR SpMV/SpGEMM GraphBLAS primitives; BFS is a composed downstream application, not directly measured in the reachable artifact (only the BMV microbenchmark is)
bfs.centrality_rationale: Per survey.md, the public artifact ships only the underlying Boolean matrix-vector-multiply microbenchmark; BFS-specific numbers are an abstract-level composed claim ('GraphBLAS-based BFS accelerate up to 433x'), not a directly benchmarked kernel.

bfs.title: Workload Balancing via Graph Reordering on Multicore Systems
bfs.one_liner: Corder: cache-aware graph reordering balancing multicore workload, up to 2.59x speedup.
bfs.regime: cache-aware graph reordering evaluated via downstream BFS/PageRank/etc. on 7 large real graphs, CPU
bfs.centrality_rationale: Corder is explicitly named in the spec's bfs-reordering-cost variant ('gives reordering-focused papers (Corder, RCM) a variant that measures what they actually contribute').

bfs.title: Speculative Parallel Reverse Cuthill-McKee Reordering on Multi- and Many-core Architectures
bfs.one_liner: First GPU-capable speculative parallel RCM bandwidth-reducing reordering, orders of magnitude faster than cuSolver.
bfs.regime: GPU/CPU speculative parallel bandwidth-reducing reordering, downstream BFS/SpMV benefit
bfs.centrality_rationale: Explicitly named alongside Corder in the spec's bfs-reordering-cost variant as a reordering-focused anchor paper.

other:spatial-join.title: RayJoin: Fast and Precise Spatial Join
other:spatial-join.one_liner: GPU ray-tracing-accelerated spatial join (LSI/PIP), up to 28x
other:spatial-join.regime: RT-core-accelerated line-segment-intersection + point-in-polygon spatial join on real geospatial polygon datasets
other:spatial-join.centrality_rationale: RayJoin is the sole surveyed paper and the direct, entire basis for this track's spec (grid/lbvh/rt modes, build-vs-query split, cuSpatial baseline all drawn straight from its own artifact).

other:maximal-independent-set.title: A Multi-GPU Algorithm for Computing Maximal Independent Sets in Large Graphs
other:maximal-independent-set.one_liner: Multi-GPU maximal independent set algorithm, 17-23x over single-GPU UVM
other:maximal-independent-set.regime: large real-world graphs exceeding single-GPU memory (>32GB / >12GB classes), multi-GPU (2-4 GPUs), vs single-GPU UVM baseline, MIS cardinality reported alongside throughput
other:maximal-independent-set.centrality_rationale: MG-MIS's headline IS exactly the spec's single-node multi-GPU MIS problem, including the exact single-GPU-UVM baseline comparison the spec's second variant names; but the paper's own contribution requires multiple GPUs (the single-GPU UVM path is the pre-existing baseline, not MG-MIS's method), so per these instructions' single-card scope it reads false even though it is the track's defining paper.

sparse-attention-kernel.title: Achieving Low Latency Inference on High Resolution Images by Exploiting Sparsity in Vision Transformers
sparse-attention-kernel.one_liner: Tile-aware ILP scheduling for sparse ViT attention, up to 2.1x over FlashAttention fixed tiling.
sparse-attention-kernel.regime: structured/regional sparse ViT attention masks, fp16, GPU
sparse-attention-kernel.centrality_rationale: Headline is a tile-aware ILP scheduling framework for structured sparse attention, evaluated against FlashAttention fixed tiling; matches the spec's structured-mask variant regime.

sparse-attention-kernel.title: Accelerating Sparse Transformer Inference on GPU
sparse-attention-kernel.one_liner: STOF: row/block-wise sparse-attention kernels plus searched operator-fusion templates, 1.6x MHA speedup
sparse-attention-kernel.centrality_rationale: STOF's 5 named mask types directly define the spec's sparse-attn-structured-mask-kernel variant.

sparse-attention-kernel.title: Fused3S: Fast Sparse Attention on Tensor Cores
sparse-attention-kernel.one_liner: Fused3S: fused SDDMM+softmax+SpMM sparse attention on tensor cores, up to 16x on H100/A30
sparse-attention-kernel.regime: real graph adjacency (single + batched graphs), tensor cores, GPU
sparse-attention-kernel.centrality_rationale: Fused3S's own claim is explicitly the sole basis for the spec's sparse-attn-graph-adjacency-kernel variant (fused SDDMM+softmax+SpMM over real graph adjacency).

sparse-attention-kernel.title: Longer Attention Span: Increasing Transformer Context Length With Sparse Graph Processing Techniques
sparse-attention-kernel.one_liner: Graph-computing view of attention gives truly work-optimal sparse-mask kernels, beats FlashAttention, 160M token context
sparse-attention-kernel.regime: structured sparse-attention masks, swept sparsity factor, GPU
sparse-attention-kernel.centrality_rationale: TomczakK25's own swept sparsity-factor range across Local/Local-1D-Dilated/Local-2D masks directly defines part of the spec's structured-mask variant.

spmspv.title: BLEST: Blazingly Efficient BFS using Tensor Cores
spmspv.one_liner: Tensor-Core accelerated pull-based BFS via bitmap SpMSpV, 3.6-4.9x over Gunrock/GSWITCH
spmspv.regime: real-world graph BFS-frontier density trajectory, tensor-core bitwise-tile batched SpMSpV
spmspv.centrality_rationale: SpMSpV is a compute-level technique inside BLEST's larger tensor-core BFS pipeline, not the paper's headline; explicitly the anchor for the spec's spmspv-bfs-frontier-trace variant.

spmspv.title: Adaptive SpMV/SpMSpV on GPUs for Input Vectors of Varied Sparsity
spmspv.one_liner: Adaptive SpMV/SpMSpV kernel-selection framework for varied input-vector sparsity on GPUs
spmspv.regime: SuiteSparse matrices, swept input-vector density, GPU kernel-selection framework
spmspv.centrality_rationale: Explicitly the central anchor for the spec's spmspv-density-sweep-kernel variant ('the controlled-sensitivity-curve variant LiAY21 runs directly'); SpMSpV is one of the two co-headline kernels.

spgemm.title: Communication-Avoiding SpGEMM via Trident Partitioning on Hierarchical GPU Interconnect
spgemm.one_liner: Hierarchy-aware trident-partitioned communication-avoiding distributed SpGEMM, up to 2.38x
spgemm.regime: large unstructured SuiteSparse/HipMCL-style matrices, distributed multi-GPU
spgemm.centrality_rationale: Trident's headline is exactly a distributed communication-avoiding SpGEMM algorithm; its own Table 2 workloads define the spec's distributed-strong-scaling variant. Multi-GPU/multi-node is the point of the paper.

spgemm.title: Ocean: Fast Estimation-Based Sparse General Matrix-Matrix Multiplication on GPU
spgemm.one_liner: Estimation-based GPU SpGEMM replacing symbolic pass with HyperLogLog, 1.4-2.8x on A100/H100
spgemm.regime: SuiteSparse square/rectangular matrices, fp64, single GPU
spgemm.centrality_rationale: Ocean's headline is a single-GPU estimation-based SpGEMM kernel replacing the symbolic pass; explicitly named as one of the papers defining the spec's flop-threshold selection and square-kernel variant.

spgemm.title: Communication-Avoiding Linear Algebraic Kernel K-Means on GPUs
spgemm.one_liner: 1.5D communication-avoiding distributed LA algorithms scale Kernel K-means to 256 GPUs, 79.7% weak-scaling eff.
spgemm.regime: kernel-matrix / clustering-derived sparse operands for distributed Kernel K-means, not general A^2 self-products
spgemm.centrality_rationale: SpGEMM/GEMM are internal distributed linear-algebra primitives used to scale Kernel K-means clustering; the paper's headline and evaluation are Kernel K-means weak-scaling efficiency end-to-end, not isolated SpGEMM kernel throughput. Multi-GPU distributed is the whole point.

spgemm.title: Popcorn: Accelerating Kernel K-means on GPUs through Sparse Linear Algebra
spgemm.one_liner: GPU kernel K-means accelerated via sparse linear algebra formulation
spgemm.regime: kernel-matrix operands for GPU Kernel K-means, not general A^2 self-products
spgemm.centrality_rationale: Popcorn formulates Kernel K-means via sparse linear algebra (including SpGEMM-like primitives) as an internal building block; evaluation is end-to-end clustering time, not isolated SpGEMM throughput vs SpGEMM competitors.

spgemm.title: Improving SpGEMM Performance Through Matrix-Reordering and Cluster-wise Computation
spgemm.one_liner: Matrix-reordering plus cluster-wise computation scheme to improve SpGEMM locality/performance
spgemm.centrality_rationale: clusterwise-spgemm's headline is exactly an SpGEMM row-reordering + cluster-wise computation scheme; its own break-even-iteration methodology directly defines the spec's e2e-preproc variant. CPU-only.

spgemm.title: Efficient Parallel Sparse Tensor Contraction
spgemm.one_liner: Hashing-based parallel sparse tensor contraction (SpGETT) beats SpGEMM-based approaches by ~21-25%.
spgemm.regime: sparse tensors (order>=3) reformulated as matrices, CPU
spgemm.centrality_rationale: parTC's contribution is sparse tensor contraction (SpGETT) that deliberately AVOIDS the SpGEMM-based approach, using SpGEMM only as a comparison baseline it outperforms.

spgemm.title: ToT: Triangle Counting on Tensor Cores
spgemm.one_liner: ToT: Tensor Core triangle counting via sparse matrix ops, 3.81x speedup, 17x memory savings
spgemm.regime: boolean/graph adjacency matrices via tensor cores, low-precision, GPU
spgemm.centrality_rationale: ToT reformulates triangle counting as SpGEMM+intersection+reduction on tensor cores, but the paper's headline and evaluation metric are end-to-end triangle-counting speedup/memory savings, not general-purpose fp64 A^2 SpGEMM throughput; operates on boolean graph matrices rather than general SuiteSparse values.

spgemm.title: AmgT: Algebraic Multigrid Solver on Tensor Cores
spgemm.one_liner: AmgT: tensor-core/mixed-precision SpGEMM+SpMV kernels for AMG setup/solve, up to 2.2x over HYPRE
spgemm.regime: tensor-core mixed-precision R.A.P coarsening products from AMG's own hierarchy, not a benchmark-chosen A^2
spgemm.centrality_rationale: Per benchspecs/spgemm/survey.md, AmgT's SpGEMM is 'not a standalone SpGEMM microbenchmark' -- it is measured as it naturally occurs inside AMG setup (R_i.A.P_i per level), an AMG-workload-weighted mixture rather than a clean kernel-level A^2 measurement; validated only via AMG solve convergence, not elementwise SpGEMM correctness.

spgemm.title: Bit-GraphBLAS: Bit-Level Optimizations of Matrix-Centric Graph Processing on GPU
spgemm.one_liner: Bit-Block CSR (B2SR) format; bit-level GraphBLAS SpMV/SpGEMM sped up to 6555x on GPU
spgemm.centrality_rationale: Bit-GraphBLAS reports an even larger explicit kernel-level SpGEMM speedup (up to 6555x) for its B2SR format as one of the paper's 'essential GraphBLAS kernels', but the binary-matrix regime differs fundamentally from the spec's general fp64 A^2 self-product.

spgemm.title: High-order Line Graphs of Non-uniform Hypergraphs: Algorithms, Applications, and Experimental Analysis

spgemm.title: TileSpGEMM: a tiled algorithm for parallel sparse general matrix-matrix multiplication on GPUs

other:hamiltonian-simulation.title: Diagonal-Budgeted Trotterization for Efficient Quantum Hamiltonian Simulation
